title: Walk every book step in CI; fix stale checkpoint cleanup
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Adds a harness (`scripts/walk-books.ts`, `bun run test:books`) that drives the compiled CLI through the authored book steps in order (`--book` and `--from` can narrow it; after a book's first failure its remaining steps are marked `not-run`), and smoke-tests two graphical launches (`py-9-01`, `java-11-01`) under Xvfb. It also checks `--version` at startup, and on an unfiltered walk where every step passed, that `progress --all` reports 154 exercises done (the total is hard-coded). Any failure, not-run step or failed smoke fails the job. It writes `test-results/book-walk/report.json`.

The motivating report was that step java-6-05 failed. This PR fixes that checkpoint problem, plus related fixes made alongside the harness:

- **Stale checkpoint files.** `prepareExerciseFiles` now removes files that an earlier checkpoint of the same project generated but the current one doesn't want, but only if the file is unchanged from what the CLI wrote. If the learner edited it, it is left alone and the run fails with `checkpoint_conflict`. Ownership records for already-missing files are dropped. `GeneratedFileStore` gains `recordsUnder` and `forget`, and `forget` is also called when clean targets are deleted. The Java book's 6-05 step also lists `ThermostatApp.java` under `clean`.
- **Replay `rm` parsing.** `simpleRemoveArgument` now accepts only a single, properly quoted or bare argument instead of stripping quotes loosely.
- **Failure visibility.** Failed replay commands report their command, timeout state, stdout and stderr in `replay execute` output, and `aifirst learn` shows program/tool failures in a tool card or plain output.
- **Harness-only `--relax-output`** for `replay execute`: skips exact stdout/stderr matching, and is rejected unless `AIFIRST_BOOK_WALK=1`.

## CI and packaging

- New reusable workflow `.github/workflows/book-walk.yml` (Java 21, Python + pygame-ce/Pillow, Maven, JUnit console jar, Xvfb/xdotool), called from `ci.yml` and `release.yml`; the release job now `needs` it, so a walk failure blocks releases. The report is uploaded as an artifact.
- Dockerfile test stage gains `libgtk-3-0 xauth xdotool xvfb`.
- `@aifirst/content` is pinned to a commit (embedded pack version 2.0.1), and the package version is bumped to 0.13.2.

## Testing

I did not re-run anything while preparing this description, and no check receipts were recorded for this run, so test results are unknown to this PR text. Tests were added or extended in `test/run.test.ts`, `test/generated-files.test.ts`, `test/native-learn.test.ts`, `test/replay-flow.test.ts`, `test/e2e.test.ts` and the new `test/book-walk-workflow.test.ts`, covering multi-file portable `rm`, Chapter 6 checkpoint reconciliation in both directions, and a failing `java` launch. The new CI job will exercise the full walk on this PR.

title: Walk every authored book step in order, and fix the bugs it found
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
A learner hit a failure at exercise java-6-05 ("The program did not run cleanly"), and the request that followed was to build a harness that runs through every sample in both books in order and fix any bugs it finds. This PR adds that harness and the fixes.

`scripts/walk-books.ts` drives the compiled CLI through the authored steps in document order, one persistent workspace per book, plus graphical smoke tests. A new `book-walk` workflow is called from `ci.yml` and `release.yml`, and the release job now also needs it.

Fixes the walk drove:
- `GeneratedFileStore` gains `recordsUnder` and `forget`, and `prepareExerciseFiles` uses them to remove files from earlier project checkpoints that the learner hasn't changed. If such a file has learner edits it throws `checkpoint_conflict` and leaves the file alone.
- `replay` accepts `--relax-output`, which skips matching of captured stdout/stderr (the exit code is still checked) and fails with `bad_option` unless `AIFIRST_BOOK_WALK` is `1`. When a command doesn't match, the results now include its command, `timedOut`, stdout and stderr.
- The replay executor's `rm` handling is changed so the portable shell can remove more than one file, and it normalises backslashes in paths.
- When a program launch fails, the native learn UI now renders the command's details through `renderExecutionFailure`.
- The Java book's chapter 6 step gets a `clean` entry for `src/main/java/ThermostatApp.java`.

Housekeeping: a `.gitignore` entry for the report directory, Docker test-image packages for the graphical smokes (`libgtk-3-0`, `xauth`, `xdotool`, `xvfb`), the embedded pack version moving from 2.0.0 to 2.0.1 in `src/content/embedded.generated.ts` and a regenerated `bun.lock`, and a `package.json` version of 0.13.2 with a `test:books` script.

`walk-books.ts` and `generatedFiles.ts` contain Windows-specific branches, and the workflow changes have no recorded CI run.

title: fix: use Homebrew for Maven on immutable Linux
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
`java-11-01` tries to install Maven through `dnf` and fails on Bazzite, where rpm-ostree discourages it: "Can you detect an immutable distribution and install via homebrew instead?". This PR detects immutable Linux and installs Maven with Homebrew there when `brew` is available.

`isImmutableLinux` reports true on Linux when `/run/ostree-booted` exists or `rpm-ostree` is on PATH. On such a system `systemDependencyInstallPlan` returns `install maven` run through the located `brew` if one is found, ahead of the apt/dnf/apk branches. If `brew` is missing it returns no plan, so `dnf` is not run. When that happens and `mvn` is the sole missing dependency, `installDependencies` says Homebrew must be installed and on PATH. Previously the Linux branches went straight to APT, DNF or apk. The platform, `which` and filesystem probes are injectable parameters for tests.

Manual verification step 18 in `docs/learn-verification.md` now covers rpm-ostree systems (Homebrew chosen ahead of `dnf`, `dnf` not run without it), `test/dependencies.test.ts` adds cases for both paths, and `package.json` goes to 0.10.3.

title: fix: make Claude hooks independent of PATH
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

On Windows, the Claude Code `/aifirst` hook and `aifirst next --format json` failed with `aifirst: command not found` (exit 127) (reported in the session). The docs attribute this to Claude Code processes that kept the PATH from before the installer ran. This change routes the Claude hook, skill and command files through a launcher script so those no longer need `aifirst` on PATH.

## What changed

- **Launcher.** `aifirst skill install --claude` now writes `~/.claude/skills/aifirst/aifirst-cli.sh`, a small script that `exec`s the current aifirst executable (plus the Bun entrypoint when running from source). Windows paths are converted to Git Bash form (`C:\x` -> `/c/x`) and quoted (`src/agents/claude.ts`).
- **Hook.** The `UserPromptSubmit` hook command is now `bash '<launcher>' replay hook # aifirst-managed-replay-hook-v1`. The marker identifies hooks we own; the old bare `aifirst replay hook` is still recognised and replaced by the new entry on reinstall.
- **Skill and command text.** `skillMarkdown` and `commandFiles` take a `cliCommand` prefix, so the commands rendered from those templates go through the launcher. The missing-binary advice is now per platform: `irm .../install.ps1 | iex` on native Windows (including Git Bash, where `install.sh` should not be used), `install.sh` for macOS/Linux/WSL, and a note to restart Claude Code afterwards (`src/skills/content.ts`).
- **Permissions.** `claudeEntries(command)` builds the allowlist for the launcher prefix. Granting replaces legacy `Bash(aifirst ...)` entries and leaves unrelated entries alone; revoking removes both legacy and launcher entries; `bookmode` pre-approval checks the launcher form.
- **Docs.** `docs/integrations/replay.md` explains the launcher, migration via `aifirst skill install --claude`, and the Windows install path.

## Known gaps

- `src/commands/replay.ts` is unchanged and still emits a bare `aifirst replay execute <id>` command, which the new allowlist (launcher form) does not cover, and the docs sentence about rendering it through the launcher is ahead of the code.
- Granting permissions removes the bare `Bash(aifirst ...)` entries, so upgraders lose pre-approval of the bare `replay execute`; `permissionState()` also only counts launcher-form entries.
- The launcher records the executable path at install time.
- Some unchanged skill prose (for example `aifirst done`, `aifirst run`) is still bare.
- The docs claim the shell installer deliberately skips the Windows binary from Git Bash; that behavior is not part of this diff.

## Testing

Added tests (including an end-to-end launcher run with `PATH=/nonexistent`, skipped when bash is absent) in `test/agents.test.ts`, `test/permissions.test.ts` and `test/upgrade.test.ts` for path conversion, quoting, launcher contents, hook install and legacy migration, permission migration/revoke, and the platform install text. No test results were captured for this PR description, and I have no record of hosted CI status or Windows testing.

title: fix: make Claude hooks independent of PATH
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Windows users of Claude Code hit `aifirst: command not found` (exit 127) from the `UserPromptSubmit` hook and the generated instructions. The goal was to make the whole Claude Code integration independent of the parent process's `PATH`, not just the hook.

Previously the permission rules were written against the bare command, for example `Bash(aifirst <command>:*)`, and the hook command was the literal `aifirst replay hook`.

Now the install writes a Claude-owned Bash launcher, `aifirst-cli.sh` in the skill directory, that forwards to the current `aifirst` executable, and entries invoke it as `bash '<launcher path>'`. Hook entries, the generated skill and command markdown, and the allowlist entries use that command instead of the bare name. Backslashes in launcher paths are replaced with forward slashes, whatever the platform. On win32, drive-letter paths such as `C:/x` also become `/c/x` for Git Bash. When the CLI runs from source under `bun` with a `src/index.ts` entry, the launcher keeps that entrypoint.

For existing installs, a hook counts as ours if its `command` is a string that equals the legacy `aifirst replay hook` or ends with the `# aifirst-managed-replay-hook-v1` marker. Allowlist status is checked against the launcher-based entries. Legacy bare-command permissions are migrated and revoked, the "skill install migration" option chosen for existing Windows installs. `src/commands/bookmode.ts` also uses the launcher command, and `docs/integrations/replay.md` mentions `aifirst skill install --claude`.

The generated skill also changes its install guidance when `aifirst` is missing. Native Windows, including Git Bash, is told to run `install.ps1` in PowerShell rather than `install.sh`. macOS, Linux and WSL keep the `install.sh` curl command. Claude Code must be fully restarted after installing.

`test/agents.test.ts` has cases for platform-specific install instructions, Git Bash path conversion, quoting of spaces and apostrophes, and the forwarding script. `test/permissions.test.ts` has cases for the legacy migration and revocation.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- `bun run typecheck`: passed, run on the submitted content.
- `bun test`: failed (443 pass, 2 fail, Ran 482 tests across 47 files. [399.09s]), run on the submitted content. The repo pins bun 1.4.0 (.bun-version; this environment runs 1.3.14); the failure may reflect this environment rather than the change.

Where to start: `install` in `src/agents/claude.ts`.

Feedback wanted: is a generated launcher script the right trade-off versus writing the absolute executable path directly into hook and permission entries?

title: Add read-only prompt gate and tool cards to learner replay
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Reworks the built-in learner replay experience (`aifirst` Home → learn) and bumps the package to 0.10.5.

- **Prompt gate.** Each exercise now shows its prompt in a read-only "Exercise Prompt" panel (typed out unless animation is off) and waits for Enter before running when stdin is a TTY (otherwise it proceeds immediately). Esc goes back and Ctrl+C exits. This is implemented for both the plain terminal (`renderExercisePrompt`) and the TUI (`presentPrompt`).
- **Replay presentation.** Replies built from replay events carry `nativeBlocks`, so text and status events keep their boundaries. In the TUI, status blocks render as "Claude activity" cards and tool calls and results as cards (using the new optional `display` field on replay operations); the plain terminal prints one-line bullets instead. Code previews are capped at 40 lines, with `e` to expand.
- **Replay execution.** Async executor functions replace the synchronous path in `aifirst replay` and the native learn flow. Commands gain `portableCommand`, `timeoutMs` and `expectedTimeout`, plus `<python>` and `<shell>` placeholders. Python/pygame game steps are verified with `py_compile` instead of launching the game.
- **Home menu.** "Browse" and "Connect an AI assistant" are removed. Progress and Help now clear the transcript, then wait for Enter or Esc to return Home.
- **CI.** Adds a `windows-duckling-replay` job (Windows, bun, Python 3.12, pygame-ce, Pillow) running `test/windows-duckling-replay.test.ts` in portable mode.

Tests were added or updated for the TUI learn flow, streaming, replay flow, planning, graphical run and the Windows duckling replay, along with the driver fixtures.

## Validation

Earlier development runs, before later edits and so not a verified result for the final content:

body:

## Why

A Windows user reported that `aifirst` wasn't recognized after install, and the plan that followed was to get the Windows binaries code-signed through SignPath Foundation. This PR prepares a published license, a code-signing policy, and release artifacts with real PE metadata for that signing. The project also decided to move from MIT to Apache-2.0 for its explicit patent grant.

## What changed

- **Licensing and policy:** `LICENSE` (Apache-2.0), `NOTICE`, `package.json` license field, `CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md`, `TRADEMARKS.md`, and README updates.
- **Windows builds happen on Windows:** new `scripts/build-config.ts` selects build targets by host OS and adds Windows title, publisher, version, description and copyright flags. `scripts/build.ts` uses it. Windows targets requested from a non-Windows host now throw, and `--all` is rejected. By default each host builds only its own OS family.
- **Release workflow:** the combined Linux/Windows job is split into `build-linux` and `build-windows` (on `windows-latest`). The Windows job verifies PE metadata and smoke-tests the x64 and baseline `.exe` files before uploading them as unsigned artifacts. title: Make learner TUI responsive with live program output
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Why

The session started from a request for quality-of-life fixes to the learner TUI: long prompts and plans stream slowly and should finish on a click or keypress, an exercise that printed an image rendered as garbage terminal characters, interactive programs left the TUI with no visible output, and the scroll position and PocketCFO choice picker needed work. The in-process runner below is what makes program output visible inside the TUI.

## What changed

- **Skip streaming.** A keypress (or a click in the TUI panels) reveals the rest of a streaming prompt, and of a plan that has a `## Proposed plan` heading (`src/learn/terminalRenderer.ts`, `src/tui/session.ts`). Plain-terminal mode is keypress only.
- **Image reads.** `replayReadText` in `src/replay/executor.ts` summarises PNG and binary file reads instead of dumping their bytes.
- **Programs run in-process.** `runExercise` in `src/learn/native.ts` and `aifirst run` (`src/commands/run.ts`) now share `executePreparedExercise`, built on a new async runner, `runAsyncProcess` (`src/process.ts`), with abort signals, streamed stdout/stderr, timeouts and interactive stdin. Previously the learn flow spawned a nested `aifirst run --format json` and parsed its JSON; that parser (`nestedRunFailure`) is removed. The runner kills the process group on abort or timeout (exit 124 on timeout, 127 on spawn failure).
- **Live output in the TUI.** `withTerminalProgram` streams program output inside the TUI instead of suspending it. `withTaskRunning` shows a spinner for verification commands and lets Esc or Ctrl+C stop them.
- **Abort for verification.** Plain argv replay commands go through the async runner and honour the abort signal; `<shell>`-sourced commands take the older path and ignore it.
- **Behaviour changes to be aware of.** `AIFIRST_LEARN_FINAL_RUN=1` is no longer passed on the final run (`test/fixtures/sitecustomize.py` still reads it). Outside the TUI, an interactive exercise with no authored sample now gets stdin ignored where it previously inherited the terminal's.

- Version bumped to 0.13.4.

New and updated tests cover streaming, scroll-follow, interactive-program and plan-stream drivers, plus `run`, replay-flow, graphical-run, terminal-renderer, choice and learn behaviour. No test results are claimed here.

The request was to keep terminal programs inside the TUI with live stdout/stderr and an embedded input field, to let long exercise prompts and proposed plans reveal on an ordinary keypress or click, and to stop synchronous process execution from freezing replay of long-running commands such as PocketCFO.

**Prompt and plan pacing.** While an exercise prompt animates, a non-Esc, non-Ctrl+C key reveals the rest of it (Esc goes back, Ctrl+C exits); that keypress does not also run the prompt, and the read-only prompt still needs Enter afterwards. A `## Proposed plan` document reveals through `BlockSkipController`'s `anyKey` mode.

**Program output and input.** Previously `native.ts` built program output from the parsed tool result (`parsed?.ran?.stdout`); it now uses the executed result's `stdout` and `stderr`. `runAsyncProcess` in `src/process.ts` accepts `stdin` as `"ignore"`, `"inherit"`, supplied text or bytes, or `"interactive"`; the interactive and supplied-input modes pipe stdin, and `onInputReady` hands the caller a `ProcessInput` to write to or end. In `run.ts`, a multi-step run breaks on a non-zero exit, timeout or abort, a program with no output prints "Program completed with no console output.", and the interactive-without-TTY check now reads `step.interactive` and `process.stdin.isTTY`. `test/graphical-run.test.ts` covers streaming output and reader input without leaving the TUI.

**Replay.** The async replay path no longer delegates non-shell commands to the synchronous `runCommand`; they go through `runAsyncProcess` with timeout and abort handling, and a timeout reports exit 124. `replayReadText` describes PNG reads rather than rendering them. On Linux with neither `DISPLAY` nor `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, a graphical operation returns exit 0 with "Skipped graphical launch because no display is available." and `matchesExpected: true` without launching.

**TUI session.** In `LearnTuiSession`, a key press can skip typing (`cancelled || skipped`). After a "run" result the view follows the latest output. ## Summary

`scripts/run-exercises.ts` used to run each exercise once, in a throwaway temp directory. title: Add portable command and display fields to Python replay operations
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Python replays captured on one OS stored the exact shell command and tool label from the author's machine (e.g. `bash -lc "python3 main.py"`, or a Windows `PowerShell` call), so they could not be replayed faithfully elsewhere. This PR adds replay fields that separate what is executed from what is displayed, and has the importer emit `portableCommand` and `display` for Python shell commands. The motivation is taken from the commit message `fix: make Python replays portable across platforms`; no user prompt in the session states a specific bug.

**Where to start:** `operationFromTool` in `scripts/lib/import-showtail.ts`, then the `requirePortable` checks in `scripts/validate.ts`.

## What changes

- **New optional replay fields** (`src/types.ts`, `schema/content.schema.json`): `display` (`toolName`, optional `description`/`command`) on every operation and on `status` events; and, on commands, `portableCommand` (argv used instead of the captured one), `timeoutMs` and `expectedTimeout`. Previously none existed and the schema rejected them.
- **Importer** (`scripts/lib/import-showtail.ts`): when a replay's source paths include a `.py` file, each imported shell command gets `portableCommand: ["<shell>", <command>]` and a `display` taken from the original tool event. In the portable command, `python3` followed by `--version`, `-c`, `-m` or a `*.py` script becomes the `<python>` placeholder. Non-Python replays are unchanged.
- **Validation** (`scripts/validate.ts`): for `python` steps, a `bash` command whose script uses `python`/`python3`, `rm`, `timeout`, `ls` or `VAR=` assignments must have a `portableCommand` starting with `<shell>`. Empty `portableCommand` and `expectedTimeout` without `timeoutMs` are rejected for all languages.
- **Content**: `books/ai-first-python-programming.json` and the four generated fixture books are regenerated with these fields; `package.json` bumps `1.7.1` to `1.7.2`.

`timeoutMs` and `expectedTimeout` are accepted and validated but not emitted by the importer, and `display` is emitted only on imported shell commands. This PR only defines and emits the data. The code that consumes `<shell>`/`<python>` is not in this diff.

## Tests

Added or updated tests: a chapters 9–10 audit that every captured shell command has a `<shell>` portable command and that `py-9-01` keeps its `PowerShell` label while its portable command contains `<python> --version`; an importer expectation for `portableCommand`/`display`; and the privacy-equivalence comparison now ignores `display` and `portableCommand`.

I did not run tests for this description. An earlier logged run of `bun test test/windows-duckling-replay.test.ts` passed (1 pass, 0 fail) before later edits, so the tested content is unknown. title: Stop stale xdg-desktop-portal when Gamescope session exits
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Problem

After returning from Gaming Mode to Plasma, Deskflow failed with errors like `No such interface "org.freedesktop.portal.FileChooser"`. The working diagnosis (from code comments, not independently reproduced here) is that Gamescope and Plasma can reuse the same user systemd manager, leaving `xdg-desktop-portal` alive without the KDE backend.

## Change

- `scripts/gamescope-clear-autologin.conf`: adds `ExecStopPost=-/usr/bin/systemctl --user stop xdg-desktop-portal.service` ahead of the existing autologin-clearing `ExecStopPost`. The intent is that the next Plasma session activates a fresh portal with the KDE environment. The leading `-` makes it best-effort, so a closing user bus doesn't mark the Gamescope unit failed. Only the generic broker is stopped. The autologin hooks are unchanged and still report failures.
- `tests/test-units.sh` (new): static checks of the drop-in. It checks one start hook, two stop hooks, portal cleanup first and best-effort, and autologin cleanup still failure-reporting. It also runs `systemd-analyze --user verify` when `systemd-analyze` and the Gamescope base unit exist, and skips otherwise.
- `tests/test-ensure.sh`: shellcheck annotation fixes, a small change to export `WAYLAND_SESSION_DIR` in a subshell, and the executable bit.
- `README.md`: documents the hook, tells existing users to re-run the installer, and adds a troubleshooting entry with a `gdbus` check and manual recovery commands.

## Testing

Run by me locally: `./tests/test-ensure.sh` and `./tests/test-units.sh` both pass, including the `systemd-analyze` check. The author reported in the session doing a full Gaming Mode cycle after which Deskflow came back up (plus a monitor glitch needing a replug, possibly unrelated); I can't confirm that was on the final code. I did not run it on Bazzite myself, and hosted CI status is unknown.

title: fix(digest): don't count commands quoted inside scripts or heredocs
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What changed

Tracetoon split command lines on `;`, `|`, `&&`, `||` and newlines even inside quotes and heredoc bodies. A line of an inline script that mentioned `bun test` (`python -c "..."`, `cat <<'EOF' ... EOF`) therefore counted as a test run, and (per the commit message) its grouping key came out as `bun test',`. This fixes a known gap noted in #8 (per the commit message).

- New `splitCommands` in `src/util/shell.ts` splits a command line while leaving quoted strings alone and skipping heredoc bodies. Splitting resumes after the heredoc terminator.
- Test detection (`testSegment`), command grouping (`commandKey`) and commit detection (`makesCommit` in `src/correlate/correlate.ts`) now use it instead of the old regex split.
- `commandKey` also drops heredoc and redirection tokens (`<`, `>`, `2>`), so `python - <<'PY'` groups as `python`.
- Version bumped to 1.0.0-rc.12 and the committed bundle `plugin/skills/tracetoon/dist/tracetoon.mjs` changed.

`tests/shell.test.ts` covers splitting chains and pipes, quoted separators and escaped quotes inside double quotes, heredoc bodies, test detection for quoted scripts and heredocs, and the `python` grouping key.

## Testing

Results from the earlier development session, run before later edits, so they don't verify the final content:

- `bun test > <log> 2>&1`: 96 pass, 0 fail (historical result; files changed afterwards).
- `bun x prettier --check "src/**/*.ts" "tests/**/*.ts"`: passed.

An earlier `bun test tests/shell.test.ts` run showed 4 pass, 1 fail; the later full run passed. The `bun x tsc --noEmit` result was not recorded, and no hosted CI result is recorded here.

The description was drafted inline by the coordinating agent; a fresh-context agent reviewed it (no host identity recorded).

Known limitation found in review: `splitCommands` treats a `<<<` here-string as a heredoc opener, so when no terminator follows, the rest of the command, such as a later `bun test`, is swallowed (the old regex split it). Only the first heredoc on a line is tracked. `$(...)` and `#` comments aren't handled either.

title: Check digests against real work, and show the evidence behind them
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Why

The maintainer wanted to dogfood Tracetoon and see whether its summaries are generated properly. An evaluation harness over six real stretches of past work (known ground truth) started at 41/48 checks; per the commit message, these fixes bring it to 50/50.

## What changed

**Which work belongs to a PR** (`src/correlate/correlate.ts`, `src/git/pr.ts`)
- Work already in the base branch is left out when the session's logs show it committing one of the last 200 base commits; that moment is the cutoff (no match, nothing dropped) (`earlierWorkCutoff`); turns finished before it are dropped, and a turn that crosses it keeps its conversation but loses earlier work.
- The time window ends 5 minutes after the last commit (was 30 minutes, or "now" with a dirty tree), so uncommitted or later work no longer stretches it.
- Quiet commits (`git commit -q`) are recognized by their subject as well as by the SHA in output (`commitMoments`).
- Files under `.git` (Tracetoon's own run files) are not repo edits; binary files now count as changed in the diff parser.
- `prTruth` takes a `head` option and records `baseCommits`, so past PRs can be re-described for evaluation.

**Reading the logs** (`src/trace/claude.ts`, `src/trace/types.ts`, `src/digest/build.ts`, `src/story/story.ts`)
- Text typed while rejecting a tool call is kept as a prompt (`feedback`) and continues the current turn instead of starting a new one.
- Test failures are read from test output, so piped runs (`bun test | tail`) count and "failing → passing" is detected; test commands are labeled by their runner rather than the first command.
- Sharing a session no longer makes two PRs a saga.

**Showing evidence** (`src/preview/html.ts`, `writing-guide.md`)
- The preview gains an Evidence panel with the digest's facts, replacing the old "Sessions used" list; the writing guide asks for a claim-by-claim check before rendering.

**Housekeeping**: `scripts/eval-summaries.ts` (the local evaluation harness), version bump to 1.0.0-rc.6, regenerated `dist/tracetoon.mjs`, new `tests/summary-fixes.test.ts`, and an updated `tests/comic.test.ts` (sharing a session alone no longer makes a saga; a linked PR still passes its saga on).

## Testing

I did not rerun checks for this description. The session log shows earlier runs: `bun test` (60 pass, 0 fail), `bun test tests/summary-fixes.test.ts` (5 pass), and `tsc --noEmit` passing, all before later edits, so they don't establish results for the final content. Hosted CI status is unknown.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Tracetoon's summaries need to match the work they describe; the session behind it started from wanting to "see if summaries are being generated properly" while dogfooding Tracetoon on its own development. This PR adds a way to measure that and fixes the digest problems it exposed.

**Measuring.** A local-only harness, `scripts/eval-summaries.ts`, rebuilds digests for six real stretches of work with known ground truth; it has a `--json` mode. The commit message reports going from 41/48 to 50/50 checks; that figure is the message's claim, not a run I can cite.

**Digest fixes.**
- Work already in the base branch is left out: the cutoff is the latest moment the session committed something the base already has, looking at the newest 200 base commits; a session command whose output shows a base commit's SHA counts too. A turn is judged by its last edit: turns that finished before the cutoff are dropped whole, and a turn that crosses it keeps its conversation. Previously the window ended at now (dirty tree) or 30 minutes after the last commit; with commits it now ends 5 minutes after the last one.
- Files under `.git` (Tracetoon's own run files) are not repo edits, binary files count as changed, and work more than 5 minutes after the last commit belongs to the next PR.
- Failure of a recorded test command is now judged from its output via `testOutputFailed`, extracted from `sessionDigest`, rather than from the exit flag alone. Test commands are labeled by their test runner, not the first command.
- Quiet commits (`git commit -q`) are recognized when a command contains the commit's subject, for subjects of 12+ characters.
- Feedback typed while rejecting a tool call is kept as a prompt and continues the turn.
- Sharing a session no longer makes two PRs a saga; stacked branches and linked PRs still relate them.

**Evidence panel.** The preview shows an Evidence section with the digest's facts (replacing the sessions-used list), and the writing guide asks for a claim-by-claim check before rendering. New tests are in `tests/summary-fixes.test.ts`.

Also a version bump to 1.0.0-rc.6 and a rebuilt bundle.

body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Three fixes (release 1.0.0-rc.8). Per the commit messages, they were found while dogfooding Tracetoon on its own PR:

- **Clickable preview link.** `render` and `preview` printed a bare path, which, per the commit message, agents passed on as a relative path the user couldn't open. Both now print an absolute `file:///` URL (Ctrl+click in terminals) and return it as `previewUrl` in `--json`. The comic image path in `preview` is shown the same way, and the skill text tells agents to pass the link on as printed.
- **Earlier work no longer leaks into a PR's story.** A turn's end was judged by every edit, so an edit outside the repo (a report, notes) kept a whole earlier turn and its prompts in the PR. Now only edits inside the repo count (a turn with no in-repo edit still falls back to all its records). Also, a commit SHA in any command's output used to count as the session having made the commit, so `git log` in another repo claimed authorship. Now only commit-making commands (commit, merge, cherry-pick, revert, am, rebase, pull), chained or not, count for that SHA-in-output path; matching by commit subject is unchanged.
- **`cd`-prefixed commands are judged by where they go.** Agents log a command with the shell's directory from before it ran, so, per the commit message, `cd ../other-repo && bun test` was filed under this repo and its failures showed up in the PR. New `leadingCd` (`src/trace/pathMatch.ts`) resolves a leading `cd`/`pushd`/`Set-Location`/`sl` target (including `~` and Git Bash drive paths), and `belongs` in `src/correlate/correlate.ts` uses it, still accepting the command if it mentions a repo root.

The eval harness (`scripts/eval-summaries.ts`) pins two cases (one now points at a commit in another repo that can't be checked from this checkout) whose branches have since merged or been committed, so they stop drifting. The plugin's bundled `dist/tracetoon.mjs`, `VERSION` and manifests are rebuilt/bumped for rc.8.

## Testing

Tests were added in `tests/flow.test.ts` (preview URL in JSON and text output), `tests/units.test.ts` (`leadingCd` and commit-maker detection) and `tests/summary-fixes.test.ts` (an out-of-repo edit added to an existing case, no new assertion). In the development session (not repeated for this PR), the last full `bun test` run passed (71 passing, 0 failing), and that output also showed 57/57 checks from `scripts/eval-summaries.ts`; an earlier direct `bun scripts/eval-summaries.ts` run was 56/57. Known limits: the SHA-in-output change affects only the output path; matching a commit by its subject in a `git commit` command is unchanged. The Git Bash drive-path conversion applies only on Windows, and `~`, `pushd` and quoted targets have no tests. A command whose leading `cd` target is outside the repo is now excluded even if its logged directory was inside the repo, unless the command mentions a repo root.

body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What changed

`tracetoon comic art` drew panels with the built-in SVG artist unless a Gemini or OpenAI key was set and approved. It now draws the comic with an AI image model once the user has approved one, and still falls back to the built-in artist.

- **New routes, no API key needed:** the Codex CLI (its image tool, via the user's Codex login) and the Antigravity CLI (experimental). Prompts go to them on stdin or in a file, never on the command line.
- **Updated API routes:** OpenAI now defaults to `gpt-image-2.5-flare`; Gemini moves to `gemini-nano-banana-2.1` through the Interactions API. Both can still be overridden with `TRACETOON_OPENAI_MODEL` / `TRACETOON_GEMINI_MODEL`.
- **Character sheets:** each cast member gets a reference portrait once per series. Sheets are attached to panel prompts (Codex and Antigravity get all of them; the API routes get those of the characters in the panel, plus the first drawn panel as a style anchor), uploaded to the assets branch on publish and recorded in the series bible, so later episodes reuse them.
- **Prompts name each character's species**, so humans stay human. The `pets` cast style now says "chibi characters" instead of "chibi animals".
- **Permissions:** Codex runs with `--sandbox read-only`; the Antigravity runner passes its skip-permissions flag and works in a scratch folder. Codex and Antigravity draw all panels in one agent session (20-minute timeout). Auto-selection order is openai, gemini, codex, antigravity, among approved routes.
- **Consent and fallback:** consent is still asked once per provider, and the message now says where prompts go. If an AI provider fails, the built-in artist draws the panels not yet drawn and a warning says so; character sheets made before the failure stay on disk and are published (stale AI panel files are removed so they can't win over the fallback). An unknown `--provider` is rejected.
- **`doctor`** lists each route, whether it is available and whether it is approved.
- Docs (README, SKILL.md, comic guide) and version bump to 1.0.0-rc.9; `dist/tracetoon.mjs` is regenerated.

A second commit fixes Codex image matching: Codex sometimes redraws an image, so its session folder can hold more images than prompts, in any order. The final reply names the chosen file per prompt; Tracetoon uses that (only files from the session's own folder) and falls back to file times only when the counts match exactly. That was found in the live run for this PR's comic (commit explanation).

## Where to start

`src/comic/providers.ts` (provider availability, the API and CLI runners, Codex output matching), then `comicArtCmd` in `src/commands/comic.ts`.

## Testing

Tests were added in `tests/comic.test.ts` and `tests/units.test.ts`, with a fake Codex in `tests/fake-codex.ts`. title: Retry timed-out judges and accept saved isolation proofs for effort arms
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

**Judge retries.** A timed-out or transient judge call used to invalidate the run. It is now retried, up to 3 attempts with backoff, including on resume after a persisted timeout. Codex judges now report timeouts as timeouts. Retries stop once the run is cancelled. On resume, a persisted failure of kind `format` no longer aborts by kind alone, only through the repair-used check. Failed judge attempts record which judge failed. The score report gains a judge-reliability table (`collectJudgeFailures`) next to the writer-reliability table.

**Isolation proofs.** Probes saved the bare model (`claude-sonnet-5-5`), but resume compared it with the arm spec (`claude-sonnet-5-5@medium`). Every resume of an arm with an effort was therefore refused with "Saved isolation proof does not match this experiment." Probes now record the arm. Proofs saved earlier match on the bare model, and the experiment id still binds the exact arms.

**Score and usage (earlier commit, 18d2df1).**
- Codex writer tokens and estimated cost now sum every thread a run spawned (main rollout plus forked subagent rollouts, each response counted once by response id) when the rollout total is at least the main-thread usage. Otherwise, and for older artifacts with no saved traces, usage stays main-thread and is labeled that way. Artifacts and score drafts record `usageScope` and `subagentThreads`, and the score table says what each cost covers.
- `score` recomputes all-thread usage for older runs from saved traces.
- The judgment walk skips `*.attempts` folders.
- Paired composite deltas gain a leave-one-case-out range and a per-case delta table.
- The writer environment hash ignores shell, terminal and session variables (`PWD`, `SHLVL`, `_`, `TERM_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_*`). Experiments frozen with the legacy hash keep it while it still matches.

## Testing

Tests were added or extended for judge retries, isolation resume, Codex usage, the environment hash and score tables. They were not re-run while preparing this description.

---
The description was drafted inline by the coordinating agent, with no separate drafter or independent reviewer. Comics are off for this repo.

title: Retry timed-out judges and count Codex subagent usage in comparison runs
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR retries timed-out judges, counts Codex subagent usage, accepts saved isolation proofs for effort arms, and adds reliability tables to the score report.

**Judge retries.** Judge calls that time out or fail transiently get up to 3 attempts with backoff. Codex judges now report timeouts as such. Failed judge attempts record their judge, and the score report gains a judge-reliability table beside writer reliability.

**Isolation proofs.** Probes saved the bare model while resume compared against the arm spec with its effort suffix, so resuming an arm with an effort was refused. Probes now record the arm, and proofs saved before that match on the bare model.

**Codex usage.** Codex writer tokens and estimated cost now sum the main rollout plus forked subagent rollouts, counting each model response once by response id. When rollouts are missing or total less than stdout, live runs keep the stdout counts with usageScope main-thread; otherwise they read the new rollouts from the sandbox CODEX_HOME and record meta.usageScope and meta.subagentThreads. Score recomputes usage across threads for older runs from the accepted attempt's saved traces, and the table says what each cost covers. The judgment walk skips `<order>.json.attempts` folders. Paired composite deltas gain a leave-one-case-out range, plus a per-case composite delta table. `checkArtifact` now rejects a meta.usageScope other than "main-thread" or "all-threads" and requires meta.subagentThreads to be a non-negative number.

**Environment hash.** Writer environment identity (Codex and Claude) ignores shell, terminal and session bookkeeping (PWD, SHLVL, TERM_SESSION_ID, CLAUDECODE, ...). Experiments frozen with the legacy hash keep it while it still matches.

Tests: a saved isolation proof for effort arms is accepted on resume (claude-comparison), Codex usage counts replayed history once (codex-usage), plus comparison, environment-hash, recovery and score suites. The comparison tests use a fake comparison setup, so they check the code around it, not the real setup.

title: Run compare in parallel, end to end on Codex or Claude
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

`prbench compare` could only run on Codex, one job at a time. This adds `--provider codex|claude|both` and `--parallel <n>`, so a comparison can run end to end on either provider, or on both.

- **Provider choice.** `codex` keeps Sol and Terra as writers and judges, and its frozen identity is unchanged. `claude` runs Claude Code on Opus and Sonnet at medium effort, with the same models judging. `both` runs two independent comparisons in `<out>/codex` and `<out>/claude`. Providers are never mixed, and a frozen experiment refuses to resume under another provider.
- **Parallel scheduling.** `--parallel <n>` (default 4) schedules writers and judges as one job graph; isolation probes run first under the same limit. A judge starts as soon as the two drafts it compares exist. Results are persisted in a fixed order, so they don't depend on timing, and `--parallel 1` keeps the serial order. After a failure nothing new starts, and running jobs finish and are saved.
- **Shared Codex login.** Concurrent Codex runs share the dedicated login through a symlink instead of queuing on exclusive copies.
- **Claude isolation and login.** Claude writers, probes and judges run isolated: the sandbox drops `ANTHROPIC_*`, `CLAUDE_CODE_*` and `CLAUDECODE`. A new `prbench auth claude` command handles login, and `prbench auth codex` is refused while a shared-login lease is held.
- **`--models <ids>`.** Replaces the provider's writer models while keeping its judges, so cheaper writers (Haiku, Luna) are scored by the same judges as stronger ones. Ids must be distinct, and `--provider both` refuses the option.

## Fixes made along the way

- **Judge references.** Claude judges invented fact IDs and cited the other draft's evidence. Each judge call now gets a schema whose reference fields are enums of exactly the IDs that side may cite. `checkJudgment` still validates what a schema can't express.
- **Claude environment identity.** The profile no longer hashes `PWD`, `OLDPWD`, `INIT_CWD` or `npm_*`, so launching from another directory doesn't block `--reuse-from`. The Codex hash is unchanged.
- **Scope audit.** An escaped leading dot, as in `rg -g '!\.agents/**'`, was turned into `/.agents/**` and flagged as host agent state. Such a backslash is now dropped. Windows paths such as `\.agents\skills\...` are still flagged.
- **Fake `gh`.** `gh --help`, `-h` and `gh help` print help and are never counted as a PR. Previously `gh pr create --help` was taken as a second, empty PR.
- **Windows-recorded cases on POSIX.** The sandbox names the checkout by the recorded path's last segment in either syntax, and Windows paths under a mapped prefix get POSIX separators. Per the commit message, on pr8 the candidate now links 92 replayed edits (13 of 24 hunks), and on pr5 it links 45 edits and all 30 hunks; before, 0.

## Testing

During development these passed, before the final edits: `bun test` (0 failures), `bun run test` (37 test files passed), and the focused suites `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts` and `tests/parallel-compare.test.ts -t "models replaces"`. I did not re-run them on the final commit for this description, and hosted CI status is unknown. New and updated tests are in `tests/parallel-compare.test.ts`, `tests/pool.test.ts`, `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts`, `tests/agentScope.test.ts`, `tests/sandbox.test.ts`, `tests/judge.test.ts` and `tests/codex.test.ts`.

The description was drafted and self-reviewed inline by the coordinating agent, not by separate agents. No comic was made, because comics are turned off in the Tracetoon settings here.

title: Run prbench comparisons in parallel, on Codex or Claude
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
`compare --provider codex|claude|both` picks who writes and who judges; `both` runs two independent comparisons in `<out>/codex` and `<out>/claude`.

**Providers.** `<agent>` accepts `codex or claude`, and the native arm comes from `provider.native` rather than a fixed `codex-native`. Codex keeps Sol and Terra (its frozen identity is unchanged); claude runs Claude Code on Opus and Sonnet at medium effort with the same models judging. Providers are never mixed, and a frozen experiment refuses to resume under another provider. Claude writers get the frozen skill and runtime, stripped Anthropic and Claude Code environment, an empty MCP config and user-only settings, stage timings and an early stop on the result event. A Claude isolation probe reads the startup catalogue; Claude judges run with a temporary home, no tools and no hooks. `prbench auth claude` stores a setup token (mode 0600).

**Parallelism.** `--parallel <n>` (default 4) schedules writers, judges and isolation probes as one job graph: a judge runs as soon as the two drafts it compares exist, results are persisted in a fixed order so they do not depend on timing, and `--parallel 1` keeps the serial order. After a failure nothing new starts and running jobs finish and are saved. Concurrent Codex runs share the dedicated login through a symlink instead of queuing on exclusive copies; Windows keeps the copy mode.

**Writer models.** To test whether a cheaper writer (Haiku, Luna) can match a stronger one, `compare --models <ids>` replaces the provider's writer models. The provider's judges stay the same, so cheap and strong writers are scored by the same judges; models must be distinct ids, and `--provider both` refuses the option since the two providers name different models.

**Judge schema.** Claude judges invented fact IDs and cited the other draft's evidence. Each judge call now gets a schema whose reference fields are enums of the IDs that side may cite (a side with no IDs for a prefix stays unconstrained).

**Smaller fixes.**
- The Claude profile hashed PWD, OLDPWD, INIT_CWD and npm_* variables, so launching from another directory blocked `--reuse-from`. Writers run in their own sandbox cwd; these never reach them. The Codex hash is unchanged for compatibility with frozen runs.
- Windows-recorded cases: the checkout is now named by the recorded path's last segment in either syntax, and a Windows path under a mapped prefix gets POSIX separators when the sandbox is POSIX. Unrelated host paths keep their spelling.
- A Codex writer ran `gh pr create --help`; the fake gh took it as a second PR creation. Help invocations (--help, -h, gh help) now print help, record a help call and never count as a PR.
- The scope audit turned a glob escape into `/.agents/**` and rejected the draft. A backslash that escapes a leading dot is now dropped when the token continues without backslashes.
- `prbench auth codex` now also refuses to sign in while a live run holds a shared-login lease. New tests (including `tests/pool.test.ts`, `tests/parallel-compare.test.ts`, `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts`) and fixtures cover the pool, parallel runs and Claude.

title: Performance gate: pass on paired priced cost per draft
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

The performance gate used to pass or fail on writer wall time and input-token medians. It now passes on priced cost per draft, using the cost `prbench score` reports.

- **Rule:** the gate passes when the candidate/baseline geometric mean of paired per-draft priced cost is at most 1.000. Pairs are same model, case and replicate. Log ratios are averaged within each case, then across cases. The case-clustered 95% interval is reported but no longer decides the result.
- **Cost source:** a new shared `draftCost` in `src/report/score.ts` is used by both `score` and the comparison, so both use the same per-model, cached-input-rate pricing. Codex usage counts across all threads when the artifact or saved traces show it.
- **Unpriced drafts:** any paired draft without a usable priced cost (unknown model price, missing tokens, Codex main-thread-only usage, nonpositive cost) makes the gate inconclusive. These are listed in `unpricedDrafts` and `summary.md`.
- **Behaviour change:** a candidate that is slower or uses more input tokens can now pass if it is cheaper. The old per-model time and token failure rules are removed. Writer wall time and token counts stay in the report as information.
- **Pairing:** pairs are no longer dropped for missing writer time. They count in `pairs`, and a new `timedPairs` counts the timed ones. Pairs with no baseline draft are skipped. Reports gain per-model median priced cost.
- **Validation:** comparability rules are unchanged; the `validationUnavailable` limitation text now says "cost, timing and token results".
- The report schema is now `prbench.performance/v3`. `CHANGELOG.md` and `README.md` are updated, and `CHANGELOG.md` notes that changing `src/performance.ts` changes the gate policy hash.

## Testing

`tests/performance.test.ts` and `tests/comparison.test.ts` were updated. I did not rerun the suite while preparing this description.

## Notes

title: Score drafts on an absolute scale and make low-effort writers retryable
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What changed

- **Absolute scoring.** `prbench score <roots…>` and a new Scores section in compare summaries report per-draft coverage, rubric, factual errors, unsupported claims and traps, with a 0-100 composite, case-clustered bootstrap intervals and paired candidate deltas. It can read older runs whose judgments use the current rubric version.
- **Accuracy-first view.** Summaries add an Accuracy section: error rate per arm, error classes, and each candidate against each baseline with a 0.05 claim-coverage guard and the cost ratio.
- **Cost estimates.** `src/report/prices.json` estimates USD from token counts when a run reports none (Codex).
- **Effort as part of the arm.** `compare --models model@effort`; writers get the bare model and that effort (default medium). Saved artifacts for an `@effort` arm must match both; bare model specs accept any saved effort. Efforts the provider doesn't accept are rejected up front. Isolation probes run at the configured effort, not the arm's (per the commit message, Haiku@low misreported the skill path and stopped whole runs).
- **Writer retries and reliability.** Writers that leave no draft (`no-draft`), whose draft the scope audit rejects, or that time out are retried (up to 3 attempts). A writer reliability table counts each kind per arm. Scope-rejected samples are no longer cached, so a retry doesn't hit the immutable cache entry.
- **Bookkeeping.** `failure.json` now records replicate, model, case and system; `summary.json` gains a `scores` field. The composite weights and error-class regexes are heuristic choices.
- **Fake gh** supports `--fill`, `--fill-first` and `--fill-verbose`, taking title and body from the branch's commits; explicit `--title`/`--body` win.

## Why

Low-effort writers were invalidating whole comparison runs (Luna@low refusing to publish, Sonnet@low running `gh pr create --fill`, one mistyped path, timeouts), and, per the session, the composite score hid the graph brief's main benefit, which is lower factual-error rates. Motivation is from the session and commit messages.

## Testing

I did not run the test suite while preparing this description. AGENTS.md asks for `bun run test` and `bun run typecheck`; hosted CI status is unknown. New tests cover scoring (`tests/score.test.ts`), arm effort parsing, the fake-Codex scope-reject retry, and fake-gh `--fill` (in `tests/sandbox.test.ts`). The isolation-probe change has no dedicated test.

---

title: Score drafts on an absolute scale, support per-arm writer effort, and retry unreliable writers
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The request was to move toward a score-based evaluation and to test cheap writers at lower effort, since A/B alone makes it hard to tell how much better we are getting. This PR adds the scoring and the per-arm effort, plus the retry and reporting needed to run low-effort writers.

**Scoring.** `prbench score <roots…>` and a Scores section in compare summaries: per-draft coverage (claims, context, uncertainties), rubric, factual errors, unsupported claims and traps, averaged over all judgments of the draft, with a documented 0-100 composite, case-clustered bootstrap intervals and paired candidate deltas. The commit message says it works on old runs retroactively; the diff scores only rubric-v6 judgments, and failure records saved without an arm are skipped in the reliability table. Tests in `tests/score.test.ts` cover the components, cost estimate, interval and accuracy view. An Accuracy section adds error rate per arm, error classes, and each candidate against each baseline with a 0.05 claim coverage guard and the cost ratio. `src/report/prices.json` estimates USD from token counts when a run reports none (Codex); its prices are third-party list prices to verify.

**Effort as part of the arm.** `compare --models model@effort` makes effort part of the arm: writers get the bare model and that effort (default medium, as before), and saved artifacts must match the model and, when the spec names an effort, that effort. Arms are checked against the provider's efforts, and identical spec strings are rejected. Isolation probes run at the configured effort, because, per the commit message, Haiku@low misreported the skill path twice and stopped whole runs.

**Writer reliability.** A low-effort writer can finish without a PR: per the commit message, Luna@low refused to publish when it skipped the skill's role phases, and Sonnet@low ran `gh pr create --fill`, which the fake gh recorded without a title. Both invalidated whole runs. Now "produced no PR" is `no-draft`, retried like a transient failure (3 attempts); a writer that times out is retried the same way and counted in its own column; summaries add a writer reliability table. A scope-rejected sample is no longer cached, so its retry doesn't hit the immutable cache entry; a test has the fake Codex writer type one mangled out-of-sandbox path and the run completes with one scope failure recorded. A rejected draft stays rejected and is never scored; per the commit message a new sample runs in a fresh sandbox, so one mistyped absolute path (Luna@low dropping a TMPDIR segment) no longer invalidates a whole run; these count as scope-rejected attempts in the reliability table. The fake `gh` gained `--fill`, `--fill-first` and `--fill-verbose`, taking title and body from the branch's commits (with several commits, the branch name can be the title).

The new tests replace collaborators with fakes (`fake-gh.ts`), so they check the logic around those steps, not the real ones.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` (240 pass, 0 fail, Ran 241 tests across 34 files. [446.83s]).

Where to start: `rebuildComparison` in `src/comparison.ts` (writer reliability table), then `src/report/score.ts`.

Feedback wanted: is the documented 0-100 composite the right basis for comparing arms?

title: Keep shell bookkeeping out of writers and out of the environment identity
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Per the commit message, a Claude comparison could not resume from a new shell: the Claude environment hash included per-process variables such as `CLAUDE_PID` and `INVOCATION_ID`, so its identity differed between shells. The same variables also reached writers, and the host session's `CLAUDE_EFFORT` could change a writer's effort. This PR does not touch the resume logic itself.

## Changes

- `src/run/sandbox.ts`: adds exported `VOLATILE_ENV` (systemd, session, dbus, ssh-agent, `SHLVL`, `OLDPWD`, `_` and similar names) and `VOLATILE_PREFIXES` (`KONSOLE_`, `CLAUDE_`). Sandboxes now drop all of them, so every `CLAUDE_*` and `KONSOLE_*` variable is stripped from writer environments. The dropped prefix `CLAUDE_CODE_` is widened to `CLAUDE_`, which also covers `CLAUDE_PID` and `CLAUDE_EFFORT`.
- `src/run/provider.ts`: `claudeComparableEnv` skips exactly the same list, so the hash no longer changes with bookkeeping a writer never sees. Other variables not already excluded (for example `SOME_TOOL_SETTING`) still change it.
- `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts`: new test that setting `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, `INVOCATION_ID` and `SHLVL` leaves the environment hash unchanged and absent from `sandbox.env`, while an unrelated variable (`SOME_TOOL_SETTING`) still changes the hash.

## Testing

Earlier in development, `bun test tests/claude-comparison.test.ts tests/sandbox.test.ts` passed (31 pass, 0 fail) and `bun test` passed (230 pass, 0 fail). Those runs were logged during development; I did not rerun them or hosted CI for this description.

title: Drop shell bookkeeping from writer sandboxes and the Claude environment hash
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Resuming a Claude comparison from a new shell changed its environment identity: the environment hash covered the inherited variables, including per-process ones like `CLAUDE_PID` and `INVOCATION_ID`. The same variables also reached writers, so `CLAUDE_EFFORT` from the host session could change a writer's effort. The edits were made in a session whose recorded request was about how the graph is constructed and optimizing it, and an earlier request asked to cancel an early run, apply a more aggressive fix and restart.

title: feat: add `showtail upgrade` to update a standalone install in place
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Adds `showtail upgrade`, so users with a standalone install can update without re-running the installer (the request that started this branch).

## What it does
- Looks up the latest GitHub release (`Tingsters/Showtail`, overridable via `SHOWTAIL_REPO`) and compares it with the running version. If it is current or newer, nothing changes.
- Otherwise it downloads the platform binary and `showtail.vsix`, runs the new binary with `--version` and requires the expected version, then swaps both files in. If a swap step fails, the originals are restored from backups.
- On Linux/macOS it then runs `setup --first-run --json` on the new binary to refresh capture integrations; if that fails, the command prints a note that they refresh on next run (human-readable output only; `--json` reports `integrationsRefreshed: false`).
- On Windows the running `.exe` can't be replaced, so a detached PowerShell helper (waits up to 30s for the process to exit) does the swap with rollback and runs the setup refresh itself; `pending` means the swap is scheduled, not finished.
- Refuses to run unless the executable is named `showtail`/`showtail.exe`, so a Bun/source run never overwrites the Bun runtime.
- `--json` emits the result object. `upgrade` is added to the commands that skip first-run bootstrap.

- Aborts if the release lacks `showtail.vsix`. Sends `GITHUB_TOKEN` as a Bearer token on the release lookup when set.
- Integrity check is limited to running the downloaded binary with `--version`; there is no checksum or signature verification, and the `.vsix` is not verified.
- The classroom doc now points students to `showtail upgrade` instead of re-running the installer.

## Where to look
- `src/core/selfUpgrade.ts`: release lookup, download, verification, replacement and the Windows helper script.
- `src/commands/upgrade.ts` and `src/cli.ts`: command wiring under a new "Maintain Showtail" help group.
- Docs: README, `docs/getting-started/installation.md`, `docs/reference/cli.md`, classroom workflow, CHANGELOG.

## Testing
Tests were added in `tests/selfUpgrade.test.ts` (222 lines) and `tests/cli.test.ts`. I did not re-run them while preparing this PR, and no real release download or Windows replacement was exercised here. Hosted CI status is not known.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The goal is to let users who installed Showtail update it in place: "Make a showtail upgrade command to upgrade showtail from an install so users don't have to re-run the installer."

`showtail upgrade` checks the latest GitHub Release, downloads the asset matching the host platform and architecture, checks that it reports the expected version, and replaces the installed binary. It also replaces `showtail.vsix` next to the binary, and fails before downloading if the release lacks that asset. After the swap it attempts to refresh capture integrations; if that fails, the command says they will refresh on the next run.

- **Standalone installs.** `installedExecutablePath` throws when the running executable isn't named `showtail`/`showtail.exe` (for example a Bun/source run), so the runtime isn't replaced. A CLI test checks the refusal happens before any network request.
- **Version outcomes.** `runUpgrade` prints "already up to date" when the status is `current`. It prints "newer than the latest release" when the status is `newer`. It prints a "pending" message when the status is `pending`, the Windows case. `--json` emits the result object instead.
- **Verification.** The downloaded binary is run with `--version` and must report the expected version. A test checks installed files stay intact when verification fails, and another that nothing is downloaded when already current.
- **Windows.** A detached PowerShell helper waits for the parent process to exit, swaps the binary and extension, and restores the backups if a step fails; it gives up after 30 seconds if Showtail hasn't exited. On Linux/macOS a failed swap also restores both files. The helper is launched with its output ignored.
- `showtail upgrade` skips first-run setup, can read `GITHUB_TOKEN` for the release lookup and `SHOWTAIL_REPO` to override the repository; README, CLI reference, install and classroom docs and the changelog describe it.

title: Prepare Windows code signing with the SignPath Foundation
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Prepares Showtail for free Windows code signing through the SignPath Foundation, and tightens the release pipeline and open-source licensing posture the Foundation requires. The request was to make the project meet the Foundation's requirements so an application would be accepted. Tagged releases fail at the signing job until maintainers finish SignPath onboarding.

## What changed

- **Release workflow** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`): a `validate` job checks that the tag is `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, matches `package.json` and `src/core/version.ts`, and is an ancestor of `origin/main`. Actions are pinned by SHA and Bun is pinned to 1.4.0 (previously `latest`). The workflow default token permission drops to `contents: read`; only the new `publish` job has `contents: write`. The ubuntu test leg now also runs typecheck, format check and `license:check`. Builds are split into `build-non-windows` and a new `build-sign-windows` job.
- **Publish job**: a new `publish` job adds an SPDX SBOM, a `SHA256SUMS` file, the LICENSE and notices, and the release preamble to the release. `build-all.sh` no longer builds the Windows exe, and CI gains a Windows build-with-metadata step.
- **Signing job**: it fails unless the `SIGNPATH_ENABLED` variable is `true`, `SIGNPATH_ORGANIZATION_ID` is set and the `SIGNPATH_API_TOKEN` secret exists. It uploads the unsigned exe, submits it to SignPath with policy `release-signing`, and requires exactly one signed exe with a `Valid` Authenticode status, a signer subject containing "SignPath Foundation", matching version metadata and working `--version` output.
- **SignPath config** (`.signpath/`): the artifact configuration, plus a README recording the expected project, policy and approval setup.
- **Licensing and policy docs**: `docs/code-signing-policy.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `.github/SIGNPATH_APPLICATION_CHECKLIST.md`, and updates to the README and docs pages. `scripts/verify-licenses.ts` backs a `license:check` script.
- **Repo hygiene**: `CODEOWNERS`, Dependabot, CodeQL, and a dependency-review workflow. Dependency review only runs when the `DEPENDENCY_REVIEW_ENABLED` variable is `true`, because the action hard-fails when Dependency Graph is off.
- **Build and install scripts**: split build scripts (`build-non-windows.sh`, `build-windows.ps1`), `.bun-version`, and `install.sh`/`install.ps1` (disclosure output and a usage comment only). `package.json` now ships `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- **Tests**: `tests/signingReadiness.test.ts` is new.

## Before this takes effect

Maintainers must complete SignPath onboarding and set the repository variables and secret above. Until then a tagged release will fail at the signing job by design.

## Testing

The development session logged `bun test` passing (688 pass, 0 fail) and `bun test tests/signingReadiness.test.ts` passing (4 pass), both before later edits. I did not re-run any checks while preparing this PR, and hosted CI status is unknown.

## Summary

Adds `showtail migrate`, which enriches existing (older) trails with detail Showtail now captures but earlier versions did not, by reading the transcripts the AI tools retain locally (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI/IDE, Copilot CLI, Copilot Chat). It recovers missing replies, edits, plans, decisions, models, tool calls/results and recap statistics.

## Behavior

- **Append-only.** Recovery never rewrites existing journal lines; only `migrate undo` rewrites the journal, re-chaining it without the batch under a declared marker. Recovered events keep the provider's timestamps and ordering; a separate enrichment record states when recovery happened and identifies the source by provider session id and transcript digest, not by committed absolute path. Current capture/redaction settings still apply.
- **`showtail migrate [tool]`** with `-s/--session`, `--file` (requires a tool), `--dry-run`, `-y/--yes`, `--json`, `--resume <run-id>`. With no tool it checks every supported provider. `showtail migrate undo [batch-id]` removes a batch and records the declared rewrite so `verify` accepts it.
- **One-time upgrade offer.** On the first interactive run after a history-generation upgrade, Showtail offers to scan for project trails (home directory, known projects, and cwds recorded in provider transcripts), shows one bulk preview, and migrates conclusive matches after one confirmation; ambiguous matches are asked about separately. Fresh installs are intended not to be prompted (but see the possible issue below), non-interactive upgrades defer the offer, and declining dismisses it permanently. Bulk progress stays in `~/.showtail-cli/migrations/`.
- Each provider plugin gains transcript-discovery support (`src/plugins/*`, `src/plugins/types.ts`), with the core logic in `src/core/migration.ts`, `src/commands/migrate.ts`, `src/commands/migrateAll.ts`, `src/core/projectDiscovery.ts` and `src/core/globalConfig.ts`.

Docs (`docs/reference/cli.md`, `docs/concepts/data-layout.md`, `docs/getting-started/installation.md`) and the CHANGELOG are updated.
- **Side effects to review:** `install.sh`/`install.ps1` pass a hidden `--offer-migration` flag; the `preAction` hook is now async and may show the offer on interactive commands except `migrate`, `--json`, `hook`, `setup`, `connect`, `disconnect` and `capabilities`; init/hook/report/status record projects in a global known-projects list; `verify` now validates conversation/enrichment entries and accepts undo markers; `import undo` no longer selects migration batches; the Antigravity IDE importer's `file://` regex changed so Unix edit paths keep their leading slash (sourceIds change shape, so re-importing may duplicate edits; no test covers it). Cancelling the bulk confirmation marks the offer declined; an error mid-run leaves it "running" (use `--resume` or per-project `migrate`).

Start review at `src/core/migration.ts`, then `src/commands/upgrade.ts` and `migrateAll.ts`.

New tests: `tests/migrate.test.ts`, `tests/migrateAll.test.ts`, `tests/projectDiscovery.test.ts`, `tests/globalConfig.test.ts`, plus additions to the plugin, Antigravity CLI and first-run setup tests.

title: fix: launch extension CLIs through cmd on Windows
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR changes how the VS Code and Antigravity extension installers launch `code`-style CLIs on Windows.

On Windows these CLIs are `.cmd` files, including a bare `code` that PATHEXT resolves to `code.cmd`, and a direct `spawnSync` cannot execute batch files.

A new `src/core/extensionCli.ts` adds `extensionCliInvocation`: when the target platform is `win32` it returns the command processor (`ComSpec`, then `COMSPEC`, then `cmd.exe`) with args `/d /c <cli> …args`; otherwise it returns the CLI and args unchanged. `runExtensionCli` builds that invocation, runs `spawnSync` with `encoding: 'utf8'` and returns the result; both installers now go through it. Each token is a separate spawn argument, so Node/Bun handles Windows quoting for paths with spaces.

`tests/vscodeExtension.test.ts` checks that a bare `code` and a `Program Files` `code.cmd` route through cmd.exe on win32, and that a POSIX launcher runs directly.

body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What changed

The graph evidence brief now tells a reader which function owns each behavior, and its code cells say which way a change went.

**Owners rows.** Sentences from the commit message are mapped to the one or two changed functions whose changed lines say them. Hunks now record per-function changed-line words (`fnWords`), so a hunk that defines several functions can tell them apart; a changed doc comment goes to the definition below it. Words shared by several functions count for less, linked hunks get a bonus, and a clear lead is required. Rows appear only for change units where two or more functions own different sentences, with at most 5 per unit and 6 in all, and never describe call relations. They show up in the TOON brief, the neighborhood tail and the lean review packet (lens A).

**Code cells.** Bare `+`/`-` become `added:` / `removed:`, pairs read `was ... -> now ...`, and for a changed boolean condition (including multi-line chains) the cell lists the operands dropped, kept and added instead of bare removed fragments. Value fallbacks (`a || ref`) stay as value changes. Direction words are largely exempted from the code-cell length budget (approximately).

**Docs.** `drafting.md` now tells drafters to read direction from code cells and name where a behavior lives from the owners rows.

title: Record each check in a chained shell command; keep full merge base
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What changed

The digest now records each verification command inside a chained shell command (several test commands still collapse into one run), and keeps the full merge base hash.

**Chained checks.** Agents often run something like `bun run bundle; bun x tsc --noEmit && bun test > log; bun scripts/eval-summaries.ts` in one call. Previously `commandRun` recorded only one run for that call and attached every result line of the whole output to it, so the eval's "57/57 checks pass" was credited to the tests, and the bundle, typecheck and eval looked like they never ran. Per the commit message, this led agents writing PR descriptions to claim checks were not run when they were.

`commandRuns` (in `src/digest/build.ts`) now returns one run per check, in order, and `sessionDigest` records each. When several checks share output, each keeps only the result lines of its own kind (test, typecheck, lint, build, eval). When the only basis for a failure is the shared exit status of a chain, the outcome is recorded as unknown instead. Several test commands in one call still collapse into a single run with an unknown outcome, as before. `commandRun` remains and returns the first run.

**Merge base.** `digest.json` stored `mergeBase` cut to 12 characters, but `tracetoon source --revision base` requires a full hash and always failed with "Code evidence must use the prepared base or head revision". The full hash is now kept.

## Where to look

Start at `commandRuns` in `src/digest/build.ts`. Tests are in `tests/evidence.test.ts` (chained checks) and `tests/preparation.test.ts` (merge base).

## Evidence

Historical runs in the agent sessions (tested content unverified; the first two ran before later edits): `bun test tests/preparation.test.ts 2>&1` passed, `bun test tests/evidence.test.ts 2>&1` passed, and `bun run test 2>&1` passed (Prettier clean; 36 source test files, 0 failed). `bun run bundle 2>&1` had an unknown outcome. title: Stop CI test jobs hanging on a Bun that does not exit
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The commit messages on this branch describe CI runs that stalled on Windows or failed on macOS (no CI result was captured for this PR): CLI processes that had already printed their whole result never exited, and `bun test` sometimes did not exit after printing its summary. This PR makes the test runner and the CLI tolerate that, so a hang becomes a bounded wait instead of a multi-hour job or a flaky timeout. The hang was seen on Windows with Bun 1.3.14 (commit messages attribute it to Bun rather than to any one test; this was not reproduced locally).

Motivation: the session began with a request to look into CI failures (S1); the diagnosis of a Windows hang comes from the commit messages.

## What changed

- **CLI exit** (`src/cli.ts`): after flushing stdout/stderr, the CLI calls `process.exit` with its exit code rather than waiting for a natural exit. If `TRACETOON_EXIT_FILE` is set, the code is written there just before exit, and the variable is removed from the environment so child processes don't inherit it.
- **Test runner** (`scripts/test-files.ts`, `test-source.ts`, `test-packaged.ts`): `test-files.ts` runs each file with `--timeout 120000` (`test-source.ts` and `test-packaged.ts` only gain an explicit exit after flushing). Per the diff, once Bun prints its `Ran N tests across M files.` summary, the runner waits 20s (`TRACETOON_TEST_EXIT_GRACE_MS`), kills the process tree if Bun is still alive, and takes pass/fail from the summary. A 15-minute per-file watchdog (`TRACETOON_TEST_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS`) kills a file that never finishes and fails it with its output so far.
- **Spawn guard for tests** (`tests/spawn-guard.ts`, `tests/helpers.ts`): `helpers.ts`, preloaded by every test file, wraps `spawnSync` of the CLI so that if the exit file appears and the process is still alive 3s later, it is killed and the recorded code returned. Commands that exit on their own, or never finish, behave as before. The `review-run`/`review-lean` helpers also use file-redirected output and count a timed-out call with a complete JSON result as finished.
- Smaller changes: the test job in `ci.yml` gets `timeout-minutes: 45`; the `review-run`/`review-lean` helpers cap each CLI call at 90s (SIGKILL); a `review-run` test now compares merged pass names without regard to order, fixing a macOS flake (a pass-order flake, not a hang).
- New tests: `tests/spawn-guard.test.ts` and additions to `tests/test-files.test.ts`.

## Also on this branch

The branch contains work merged from upstream that is not part of the hang fix: publishing from forks (`--head owner:branch`), one resolved target repo passed as `--repo` to every `gh` call (`src/github/target.ts`), check receipts read without `task begin`, and the matching tests. The diff against `main` therefore includes those files and the rebuilt `plugin/skills/tracetoon/dist/tracetoon.mjs`.

## Evidence

Historical runs from the development session (tested content not verified against the final commit):
- `bun test tests/spawn-guard.test.ts --timeout 120000`: 3 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test tests/review-run.test.ts tests/review-lean.test.ts --timeout 120000`: 37 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test tests/test-files.test.ts --timeout 120000`: 7 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test tests/flow.test.ts --timeout 120000`: 15 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run bundle`: source test files 49 passed, 0 failed

No hosted CI result was captured, so CI status on Windows or macOS is unknown. The kill-after-summary and guard paths are timing-based and have only been exercised by the tests above.
