title: Resolve one PR target repo and guard tests against hung Bun processes
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This branch makes publishing resolve one target repo instead of trusting gh's default (the fix for issue 52, asked as "Is this issue fixed?"), lets publish work from a fork clone, and stops Windows CI from hanging when Bun does not exit after finishing.

**One target repo.** Context, doctor and publish now share one target: gh's default repo when it is a remote of this clone (fork to upstream), else origin; a default that matches no remote is ignored when origin is a GitHub remote. In offline mode gh is not asked and origin is the target. The gh calls that read or write PRs or repo metadata (pr view/list/create/edit, repo view, title-rule and recent-comic lookups) pass `--repo`. Context records the target in context.json, render stores it in the approval (and the approval code) and the preview prints "PR target: ...". Publish refuses if the target, resolved again at publish time, now differs from the approved one (that resolution itself asks gh for its default repo). Comic image hosting still pushes to origin; the private-repo check uses the target. Doctor reports the target and checks push access on origin. `prTruth` in `src/git/pr.ts` now calls `resolveTarget` first (unless gh is disabled) and passes the target repo and origin owner to `existingPr`, which it previously called with only the checkout and head.

**Publishing from a fork.** When origin is a fork of the repository gh targets, `gh pr create` gets `--head owner:branch`, and the existing-PR lookup keeps PRs whose head lives in that fork. Digest and the render approval read `tracetoon check` receipts whenever the run has any, including runs that skipped `task begin`. Receipt summaries match "N passed/failed" and read stderr before stdout, so a wrapper's total wins over the last child's per-file lines. The receipt environment identity ignores temp-directory, terminal and display variables.

**Hang protection.** Per the commit message, Windows runs hung three times, in a different test file each time. Previously the runner waited for each file's close event with no limit. Now it kills a file after 15 minutes and fails it with the output so far (`TRACETOON_TEST_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS`); on Windows it kills the process tree, elsewhere the process itself. Once a file's summary line appears, it waits 20s for bun to exit, then kills it (grace overridable via `TRACETOON_TEST_EXIT_GRACE_MS`) and takes the result from the summary. The CI test job has a 45 minute limit instead of 6 hours. Because bunfig's timeout was ignored, the runner passes `--timeout` to bun itself, later raised to 120s.

**CLI exit and test guards.** The earlier whole-file hangs (review-lean, review-run, brief-extras) look like the same cause. With piped output, spawnSync on Windows waits for all holders of the pipe, so a leftover descendant could stall it after the command exits; a later Windows failure showed `review run --all` printing its whole result without the call returning. Real hangs are bounded by the per-file watchdog and the spawn caps. A killed child's pipes are destroyed and unref'd, and test-source and test-packaged exit explicitly after flushing. In the review helpers, a call that timed out with its whole JSON result on stdout counts as finished. The suite's default 5s timeout was too short for process-spawning tests (3-6s on loaded runners). The flag is passed where the runner spawns bun test, and the bundle was rebuilt for the new build identity. This was found while publishing Tingsters/tracetoon#53 from a fork. CLI processes that printed their result and kept running after they finished and kept appearing in new test files. On Windows CI, `tracetoon review import` printed its complete JSON and the process stayed alive. The entry point relied on a natural exit, so a handle left alive kept it running. `src/cli.ts` now flushes stdout and stderr, then calls `process.exit` with the command's exit code. When `$TRACETOON_EXIT_FILE` is set it also writes the exit code there, clearing the variable from its own environment. Commands that exit by themselves, or that do not finish, behave as before. `tests/spawn-guard.ts` kills a process still alive 3s after the exit file appears; one that hangs without finishing is not hidden. `tests/helpers.ts` routes spawned CLI calls through it. The review-run and review-lean helpers redirect output to files and cap each CLI call. A watchdog run caught review-run stalled for 15 minutes on Windows; product timeouts for a real reviewer are 15 minutes and the tests' spawnSync had none. review-run sets a shorter reviewer timeout so a hung fake codex is killed after a minute instead of fifteen. The merged-list test hard-coded pass order, which follows import order and depends on which concurrent reviewer finished first (failed on macOS); it no longer does. Test-only edits cover the new target logic in comic, flow and target tests.

The bundled `dist/tracetoon.mjs` was rebuilt, with a new `buildId` in `build.json`.

Limits: one run of `review-run.test.ts` in the session has no visible exit status (hidden by a pipe). the changed tests replace gh and other collaborators with fakes or stubs, so they check the logic around those steps, not the real steps. The logs hold CI results only for an earlier commit, not the final head. The Windows reruns are described only in the messages of commits 9af69e8 and fd4c9f7.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- `bun run typecheck`: passed, run on the submitted content.
- `bun run test`: timed out (incomplete), 900 s; it gave no pass/fail result on the code.

Where to start: `publishImpl` in `src/commands/publish.ts` (target check and fork `--head`), then `resolveTarget` in `src/github/target.ts`.

Feedback wanted: is a fixed 20s grace after the summary the right trade-off before killing a Bun process that has not exited?

title: Add a queryable evidence graph of how each PR was made
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This adds an evidence graph of how a PR was made, queryable by drafting agents, as a core Tracetoon feature rather than a partial integration.

**What changed**

- When the engine starts, a digest also builds `evidence-graph.json`: prompts linked to the edits made in their turn, edits to the diff hunks their lines survive in, runs to PR files edited after them, commits to the sessions that made them. If building the graph fails, for example because the engine cannot start, the digest is written with a note.
- The engine is cypherlite v0.16.1 compiled to WebAssembly, run in-process, pinned by hash in `build-dependencies.json` and rebuilt with `scripts/cypherlite.ts`; `buildManifest` now calls `verifyCypherlite()`, so a hash mismatch fails the build, and no native modules are added. Vendored files are in `src/graph/vendor/` and excluded from prettier.
- `tracetoon query` answers these named questions (outline, why, unverified, unexplained, stale, dead-ends, turn, pushback, schema) plus read-only Cypher, printed as TOON. `why` lists the hunks of its target, marking those no captured edit explains, and the commit message bodies.

body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The full independent reviewer was costly: per the commit message it took about 38% of each draft, mostly from reading the workflow doc, the whole brief and the whole patch, and from hand-writing `review.json` (often with a placeholder agent id or invalid refs). This adds a lean path where the reviewer reads one packet and reports only findings, and Tracetoon writes the `review.json` contract.

## What changed

- `tracetoon review-packet --lean [--run <id>]` writes `review-packet.md`: a fingerprint header, the title, the line-numbered rendered body (generated Validation section elided), open limits, changes, commit messages, tests and requests from the stored brief, a hunk-to-owning-symbol map, and the diff. The whole reduced patch is included when it is at most 16000 characters; otherwise only cited hunks, branching hunks and test assertion lines (`leanPacket` in `src/commands/review.ts`; `--lean` is required).
- The reviewer writes `review-findings.json` (v1): a cold read plus claim/omission findings (the reviewer prompt caps them at 8; parsing only warns above that), each with a verdict and `diff:`/brief/`path:line` evidence. Claims need a quote copied from the body; omissions may omit it. Validation lists every fix needed (`src/contribution/leanReview.ts`).

Placeholder agent ids are refused; brief refs and `path:line` are resolved to diff refs, and unknown evidence refs become warnings rather than failures (a claim quote not found in the title or body still fails the import). With no claim findings it adds a synthetic supported claim, and the review is marked incomplete (publishing still allowed) when guidance, change-map behavior checks or the comic review are missing.
- `plugin/skills/tracetoon/references/reviewer-lean.md` is the reviewer's whole instruction.

title: Add neighborhood evidence brief layout; report brief-check findings once
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This adds a second layout for the evidence brief that the writer reads, and changes `render` so it reports each brief-check finding once. Both came out of a session testing whether a graph-shaped brief gives a better PR description than a relational/vector one. The session request was to prove or disprove that thesis (S1), and the user chose to build the new brief on the previously measured commit rather than the feature-branch tip (D2). [S1, D2]

**Neighborhood layout.** Before, the brief was always the TOON tables from the `brief` query, capped at 60 rows per table, with commit sentences linked to files only through `implementedBy`. Now `TRACETOON_BRIEF_LAYOUT=neighborhood` (the default; `toon` keeps the old layout) renders one block per change unit: its requests, its commit sentences with the hunks they point to (`→ H#`), and each changed file with its hunks and key changed lines (`- old ⇒ + new`). Hunks store up to 24 key lines each, are citable as `H#`, and the blocks are packed to a 2,112-token evidence budget (`TRACETOON_BRIEF_BUDGET` overrides it): headers, requests, commit sentences and one line per file are always included, and code lines are then added by value per character until the budget is spent. On a large PR the fixed part is first clipped (request and sentence text down to 120 characters, file lines compacted) and can still exceed the budget, in which case no code lines are added. Each hunk's up to 24 key lines are chosen in `keyCodeLines` (`src/graph/build.ts`): a removed line is paired with its most similar added line (`- old ⇒ + new`) only when they share at least half their tokens and are not identical; then lines that define a symbol or branch; then the rest. Blank, brace-only, import and comment lines are dropped whenever any other candidate exists, and kept only when a hunk has nothing else. Each line is clipped to 160 characters. Rules, limits, tests, housekeeping and validation stay TOON tables outside the budget. `tracetoon query brief` prints the same text as `prepare` does. The sentence-to-hunk links come from a new `linkedHunks`, within each commit's own hunks: a file the sentence names (up to two) links its best-fitting hunk; a sentence listing several behaviors is split and each part may link a hunk (up to three); a commit with a single code hunk links a sentence that shares its words; two close-scoring hunks in one file are both linked; and two files that fit about equally link nothing. `describedHunks` (behind `implementedBy`) keeps its earlier, stricter behavior. The rules shown to the writer are reworded to name hunks and `→ H#` instead of TOON columns. [CH1, commit:5539230d1cab]

**Render loops.** Per the commit message, Codex graph-arm drafts ran up to 44 renders because `render` kept repeating findings the writer could not clear: a sentence attributing a result to the commit message flagged as a run claim 18 times, and the goal request and change rows reported uncovered dozens of times. The run-claim check now skips a sentence that names the commit message or carries a tag containing a 7 to 40 character hex sha (with or without `commit:` and `#n`), whether or not the sentence actually attributes the result. Separately, every kind of finding (untagged, run claim, unknown ref, uncovered, flag) that an earlier render of the run already reported is listed under "repeated" and no longer counted as open; this is a general demotion recorded in `brief-findings-seen.json`, not limited to false positives. The user chose to fix the loops in both arms before running the next experiment (D4). [CH2, commit:48a90d77c9cc, D4]

**Consequences.** The default brief text changes for everyone on this branch; existing tests pin `toon` through `tests/helpers.ts`. A finding blocks only on the first render that reports it, so a real finding the writer ignores once will not block the next render. A sentence containing the words "commit message", or tagged with a sha, is never treated as a run claim, even if it also states an unattributed result. The skill bundle and `build.json` build id were regenerated. The two reference docs were updated for `→ H#`, plus minor whitespace and reflow edits.

**Review path.** Start with `src/graph/neighborhood.ts` (rendering and packing), then `linkedHunks` in `src/graph/queries.ts`, then `demoteRepeats` and the `attributed` check in `src/graph/briefRender.ts`. The tests are `tests/neighborhood.test.ts` and `tests/render-loops.test.ts`. The rest is wiring, docs and the regenerated bundle.

**Validation.** During development `bun test tests/render-loops.test.ts` passed (2 pass, 0 fail); the tested content was not verified against the final revision. No captured result is available for the full test suite or `tsc` on this revision. `test:compiled` appears in two historical session commands (combined with `bun test`) whose outcomes were not captured, and `test:bundled` has no captured result; hosted CI status is not established here.

**Feedback wanted.** Whether `neighborhood` should be the default or opt-in, and whether demoting a finding after one report is acceptable or should require the writer to acknowledge it.

body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The graph arm of the shape test gave the writer too little evidence and flattened the graph into tables that cite each other by id; the plan was to give it a fixed budget and deliver it as a graph. This PR lays the evidence out as per-change neighborhoods; `toon` stays selectable and, per the commit message, reproduces the previous TOON tables byte for byte.

**Neighborhood layout.** When `TRACETOON_BRIEF_LAYOUT` is not `toon`, `graphBrief` renders one block per change: its requests (clipped to 320, 200 or 120 characters when the fixed lines do not fit), its commits with each sentence's hunks (`→ H#`), and each changed file with its hunks and key changed lines, shown as `- old ⇒ + new` when a removed line shares at least half its tokens with an added one, otherwise as `+ new` or `- old`. Hunks keep up to 24 key changed lines (long ones clipped) and are citable as `H#` through a hunks section in the changed `briefParts`. The commit message says blocks are packed to 2,112 evidence tokens (`TRACETOON_BRIEF_BUDGET`), with code lines added greedily by value per character and big PRs clipped to fit; the diff has constants for 24 key lines and a 2112-token budget.

**Sentence-to-hunk links.** `describedHunks` now filters through `isVersionFile`, extracted from it (via `scoredHunks`). Links are at hunk level and conservative: a named file, each part of a list sentence, a single code hunk that shares words, or the `describedHunks` scoring with its tie margin; when the top two hunks are in different files and fit about equally, neither is linked. `queryCmd` prints this text for `tracetoon query brief` when it is available.

**Render loops.** The commit message says Codex graph-arm drafts ran many renders because render kept repeating findings the writer could not clear. Now a finding an earlier render already reported is listed under "repeated" without blocking, and a sentence tagged with or naming the commit message is not a run claim. Previously such a sentence was flagged as a validation claim.

The quick-path and contribution-workflow skill text now tells writers to name a file for a sentence from its `implementedBy` or its `→ H#` hunks; the bundled skill build was regenerated.

For users, the neighborhood layout is the default on this branch, so briefs carry code lines; the budget caps the optional code lines, while headers, requests, sentences and file lines are kept; set the layout to `toon` for the old shape. **Receipt commands keep their shell quoting and repo paths.** Per the commit message, four of six accuracy flags in a Terra confirmation run were Tracetoon's own Validation lines. The evidence `cmd` for a receipt was the argv joined with spaces, so `bash -c 'bun run typecheck && bun run test'` read as a different command. The three-role path and the quick path remain available when the user asks. Without a brief the three-role path is still the default. title: feat(review): add review run --all and review merge
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Running reviewer passes one at a time meant the drafter got several separate finding lists and had to edit the body repeatedly. This adds one command that runs every planned pass and returns a single merged list, so the drafter applies findings in one edit pass and reviewer rechecks become optional.

- `tracetoon review run --all`: runs one pass per lens, plus general passes beyond the lens count, concurrently. Each slot has its own packet, reply, findings and reviewed-body files, and is imported as a single run is. If some passes fail, the ones that succeeded are imported, the failed passes and the rerun command are named, and the exit code is non-zero. body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Tracetoon had no `update` command, so upgrading meant re-running `install.sh` or `install.ps1`; the request was a CLI upgrade without a reinstall, and the plan for it was approved. The follow-up request also asked for the Claude Code marketplace plugin route to be planned. This PR adds `tracetoon update`, which looks up releases, installs the newest one in the chosen channel, and restores the old files if an early step fails.

**How it works**
- `applyRelease` verifies SHA-256 checksums and that the skill and runtime are one build, then replaces the binary, comic assets, the installed skill copies and the hooks, restoring the old files if a step fails before the old copies are discarded.
- Releases come from GitHub's releases list, or a test server when `TRACETOON_UPDATE_URL` is set; drafts and tags that are not versions are skipped, and the newest release is picked by publish time, with a numeric semver comparison breaking ties (`rc.2` before `rc.10`).
- Flags: `--check` (reports whether a newer release exists without installing), `--exit-code` (with `--check`, exit 10 when a newer release exists), `--channel stable|latest` (default `latest`, which includes candidates; `stable` does not) and `--to <version>`, which also serves as the rollback path.
- `update`, including `--check`, fails with an error when its disable-updates environment variable is set to `1`, and refuses to replace a plugin/bundle copy, a binary named by `TRACETOON_BIN`, or a binary the installer did not place; it says how to update instead.
- Both installers now write an `install.json` recording the install method, version, tag and path; the PowerShell installer ignores a failure to write it. The README documents the command, and the bundled build and its `build.json` build id are regenerated.

`tests/update.test.ts` covers version ordering, release selection, channel behaviour and what `update` may replace.

**Consequences:** installer-placed binaries can be upgraded or rolled back with `--to` from the CLI, while other install types are refused with instructions. Since `stable` means non-prerelease, it has nothing to install until a non-prerelease ships.

title: Recognise the VEX AIM's user serial port
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Makes the AIM's user serial port (interface 4) get found, so `user_port()` is no longer `None` for it and `read_user()`/`write_user()` can use it instead of the system-port fallback.

## Problem

`types_by_location()` only knew the V5 Brain layout (interface 0 = system, 2 = user). The AIM enumerates as a composite device with a UVC camera on interfaces 2 and 3, so its serial ports are interfaces 0 and 4. Interface 4 hit the "Unknown location" branch and was dropped, so `find_devices()` returned the AIM with `user_port() == None`. (Account from the commit message; the task was to submit a fix for the AIM serial port bug.)

## Changes

- An AIM (PID `0x0700`) port on interface 4 is now classified as the user port. The Brain mapping is unchanged.
- `types_by_location()` now returns `None` instead of `Some(empty)` when it recognised nothing, so the name-based fallbacks in `find_ports()` can run when no port at all was recognised (this applies to every device, not only the AIM).
- `write_user()` on a user port used a single `write()`, which may accept only part of the buffer, yet returned that count and never flushed. It now uses `write_all()` + `flush()` and returns the full length, as the system-port `send()` path does. It applies to any user port, including the V5 Brain, and is a separate small fix found while in the area.

## Testing

Three unit tests were added in `serial.rs`: AIM interfaces 0/4 map to system/user, Brain interfaces 0/2 still work, and an unrecognised AIM interface yields `None`. They feed interface numbers the way each OS reports them (macOS reports the data interface, +1). I did not run the test suite or test against AIM hardware for this description, and I know of no hosted CI result.

The VEX AIM's user serial port wasn't being detected, which is the serial-port bug on AIM devices this PR addresses.

Previously `types_by_location()` knew the V5 Brain layout (interface 0 = system, 2 = user) and no AIM-specific case. Interface 4 fell into the 'Unknown location' branch and was dropped, so `find_devices()` returned the AIM with `user_port() == None`, and `read_user()`/`write_user()` silently used the system-port fallback.

title: Find AIM REPL on USB interface 4 and add experimental upload tools
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Per the commit message, the AIM's MicroPython REPL is reachable on USB interface 4 (the committed results only show a serial port, not the interface number). This adds small scripts to talk to it, and adds experimental upload/load tools to the `vexaim-probe` crate.

## What changed

- **REPL helpers (`tests/`)**: `repl.py` sends lines to a serial port and prints the replies. `capture.py` is a raw capture helper. `pingpong.py` runs N `print("AIM_AGENT_V1 "+"PONG")` round trips and reports JSON with latency. The string is concatenated so the echoed input can't be mistaken for the output.
- **Recorded results (`build/`)**: `pingpong-run1.json` and the run logs. `pingpong-run1.json` shows 10/10 round trips at about 50 ms each, and the commit message reports the same. `build/main.mpy` (218 bytes) is a committed compiled MicroPython file. The first run's log shows `PING`/`CAPS`/`BOGUS` sent with no clear reply. The second shows `PING` raising `NameError` in the REPL, which shows the REPL is answering.
- **Experimental tools (`crates/vexaim-probe/src/bin/`)**: `aimupload` writes `slot_N.ini` and `slot_N.bin` to the vendor User area without running the program. `aimload run|stop [file]` issues a file load action. `dirlist` is read-only and queries several vendors. `aimload stop` sends the name `null`, and `run` defaults to `slot_1.bin`. `aimupload` defaults to the `vm` extension type. The upload file format is a hypothesis, built from cargo-v5 PR #22 and VAIMRC-Console. It is marked experimental in the source.
- **`Cargo.toml`**: enables the `file-commands` feature on `vex-v5-serial` and adds an empty `default` feature set. `Cargo.lock` gains `flate2` and its dependencies.

## What this does

Records the hardware replug and kicker tests for the VEX AIM skill and fixes what they exposed.

- With no robot plugged in, the serial library reports "could not infer serial port types". `devices()` now maps that to an empty device list, so the user sees the normal "no VEX device found" message.
- A new `is_disconnect` check recognises `broken pipe`, `no such device` and `input/output error`. Any `Fail::Io` whose text matches now says the robot disconnected mid-command (USB unplugged or robot off) and that a movement may or may not have run, so check the robot before re-running. `Fail::Io` is also used for enumeration, camera and file errors, so a matching error from those paths gets the same wording. Other I/O errors keep the old message. The new unit test covers only the `is_disconnect` matcher (broken pipe, no such device, and a timeout as a negative), not the message text, the `input/output error` case or the `devices()` mapping.
- The rebuilt Linux binary and its `SHA256SUMS` are updated.

**Tests and logs**
- `tests/replug.py` is a harness that waits for a human unplug and replug and times the recovery to the first successful `exec`. It then runs 5 follow-up round trips and beeps when it is safe to unplug. `tests/stress.py` runs N consecutive `exec` round trips.
- Raw logs are in `docs/replug-run1.jsonl` and `docs/replug-run{2,3,4}-udev.jsonl`.

- `docs/hardware-test-report.md`, `SKILL.md` and `references/api.md` now state the results. `SKILL.md` also says the camera orientation follows how the robot sits, because `snap` never flips the image.

## Results reported (from hardware sessions, not re-run for this PR)
- Run 1, without the udev rule: 5/5 recoveries but only 3/5 cycles fully clean. The journal shows ModemManager probing the ports for ~6-9 s after each enumeration.

title: Add fast contact play and reliable stationary tag search
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What changed

**Tag search.** Cargo search is unchanged, but searching for an AprilTag now goes through a new `find_tag` in `behaviors.py`. It takes up to three short stationary native-camera readings at each of eight viewpoints (45° apart, with a soft 20 s limit checked between views) instead of a continuous sweep. A hardware test found the purple tag only from stationary views after a continuous sweep missed it. `find`, `approach` and `deliver` pick this up. `reacquire` also waits 300 ms before reading a tag.

**Fast contact mode.** `behaviors.configure(verification="contact", tag_turn_dps=...)` is a new opt-in. The default stays `verification="vision"` and keeps the existing checks. In contact mode:
- a bounded contact move that hits its time limit (for example against a pen wall) is accepted instead of raising "Motion stalled";
- the retention reverse and the repeated possession gates are skipped, and the cargo-loss watchdog during approach is off;
- `deliver` trusts cargo remembered from an earlier `collect` in the same activity instead of requiring native possession, then continues to the marker and operates the kicker. This is the riskiest semantic change.

`configure` also validates `verification` and accepts `tag_turn_dps` (max 150, defaults to `turn_dps`). New report events are `tag_search_view` and `pickup_complete`.

When native possession or release can't be confirmed, results say so: `collected` / `delivered` is `None` and `evidence` is `contact_assumed` / `place_assumed`. `deliver` and `collect` results now carry `completed: True`. Missing targets and the activity deadline still stop the sequence.

**Motion limit.** Every finite motion now gets at least 1500 ms of margin for acceleration and delayed stopped reports. It still returns as soon as the robot reports it has stopped.

**Housekeeping.** Version is 0.5.1 (`VERSION`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`). README, device-commands, hardware-notes, release-notes and the vex-aim skill docs are updated. The release notes say the workshop installer requires 0.5.1, and the skill docs say the helpers need vexaim 0.5.1.

## Testing

I did not re-run tests for this description. The session logs show earlier unit-test runs (`dev/test_behaviors.py` among them) passing, but before later edits, so they don't establish that the final content passes. `dev/test_behaviors.py` gains coverage for stationary-only tag decoding, missing targets, false-negative possession, assumed placement, and deadlines. Hosted CI status is unknown.

Hardware: the earlier test (blue barrel to purple Tag 0) worked. A follow-up on the final 0.5.1 source could not reacquire blue in the current layout and stopped after a bounded search. Full hardware acceptance of the new mode is still pending (see `docs/hardware-notes.md`). This does not claim to fix all Bluetooth or lighting failures.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

On Wayland sessions, full Windows desktop mode (`winapps windows`) now prefers an SDL FreeRDP client over `xfreerdp`.

## Changes

- `waGetFreeRDPCommand` takes the launch mode as `$1`; the caller passes `"$1"`.
- When `FREERDP_COMMAND` is unset, the mode is `windows` and `XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`, it looks for `sdl-freerdp3`, `sdl3-freerdp`, then `sdl-freerdp`, then the `com.freerdp.FreeRDP` Flatpak run with `--command=sdl-freerdp` (setting `RDP_FLATPAK=1`).
- If none is found, the existing `xfreerdp` detection runs as before. RemoteApp/app launches and non-Wayland sessions are unchanged.
- The final availability check also accepts the new Flatpak command string.

## Limitations

- The SDL candidates skip the FreeRDP major-version check that the `xfreerdp` paths apply, and the Flatpak branch only checks that the app is installed, not that it ships `sdl-freerdp`.
- The existing windows-mode flags were written for `xfreerdp`; they were not verified against the SDL client.

## Testing

Not run: no Wayland session or FreeRDP install was exercised for this PR.

title: Prefer SDL FreeRDP for full-desktop mode on Wayland
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
On Wayland sessions, the full Windows desktop view now prefers the SDL FreeRDP client. Per the request, RemoteApp/RAIL support in SDL FreeRDP is not fully implemented, so this is scoped to full-desktop mode, as a minimal diff for upstream.

`waGetFreeRDPCommand` now receives the launch mode (`waGetFreeRDPCommand "$1"`). When the mode is `windows`, `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` is `wayland` and `FREERDP_COMMAND` is unset, it tries `sdl-freerdp3`, then `sdl3-freerdp`, then `sdl-freerdp`, then, if `flatpak` is installed and `com.freerdp.FreeRDP` is listed, the Flatpak (run with `--command=sdl-freerdp`, setting `RDP_FLATPAK=1`). The unversioned names are covered because on some systems `sdl-freerdp` is itself v3. If no SDL client was selected, the existing `xfreerdp` detection runs as before; other modes continue on the xfreerdp path. The final availability check also accepts the SDL Flatpak command string.

Previously, when `FREERDP_COMMAND` was unset, detection began with the `xfreerdp` check regardless of mode or session type.

Per the request, the shfmt reformatting and docs changes were dropped to keep the change minimal; `bin/winapps` is the only file in the diff.

title: Walk every book step in CI; fix stale checkpoint files
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What

Adds a harness that walks every authored step of the book through the compiled CLI, runs it in CI and as a release gate, and fixes the product bugs that surfaced while building it. The starting point was a failed step 6-05 (`java-6-05`) reported by the user.

## Changes

- **Harness**: `scripts/walk-books.ts` (`bun run test:books`) drives the built binary through persistent book workspaces and writes `test-results/book-walk/report.json`. Flags include `--book`, `--from`, `--skip-smoke` and `--keep-workspace`, and it smoke-launches two graphical steps (`py-9-01`, `java-11-01`). It fails on a CLI version mismatch or any step not run, and a full unfiltered walk also checks that all 154 steps are recorded as done.
- **CI**: a reusable `.github/workflows/book-walk.yml` (Java 21, Python, xvfb, JUnit console jar) is called from `ci.yml` and `release.yml`. The release job now `needs` it. `Dockerfile` test image gets the GTK/xvfb/xdotool packages.
- **Stale project files**: `prepareExerciseFiles` now removes files from an earlier checkpoint of the same project that the new checkpoint no longer wants, if they are still byte-identical to what AI First wrote. Ownership records for files that no longer exist, and for `clean` targets it deletes, are forgotten. Modified ones raise `checkpoint_conflict` and are left alone. `GeneratedFileStore` gains `recordsUnder` and `forget`. The book entry for 6-05 also lists `ThermostatApp.java` in `clean`.
- **Replay**: `replay execute` accepts `--relax-output`, which skips expected stdout/stderr comparison. It is rejected unless `AIFIRST_BOOK_WALK=1`. In `replay execute`'s JSON output, a command whose result does not match now also reports its command, timeout flag, stdout and stderr. `simpleRemoveArgument` now matches only a single `rm` path (quoted or unquoted); multi-argument `rm a b` falls through to the general shell path.
- **Learn UI**: failed tool results and failed program runs show their output via a shared `renderExecutionFailure`.
- **Version/deps**: CLI bumped to 0.13.2; `@aifirst/content` pinned to a commit hash; embedded content pack moves from 2.0.0 to 2.0.1.

## Tests

Added or extended tests (including Chapter 6 forward/reverse launcher reconciliation and refusal to remove a modified file; several run tests now stub a `java` binary): `book-walk-workflow`, `generated-files`, `native-learn`, `replay-flow`, `run`, `e2e`. I did not rerun the full suite or the book walk while preparing this description, so no results are claimed here; hosted CI on this PR will run the new `book-walk` job.

## Notes

The description was drafted inline by the coordinating agent and was not independently reviewed.

title: fix: use Homebrew for Maven on immutable Linux
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Starting `java-11-01` on Bazzite failed at "Installing Maven": the learner reported that dependency installation failed there, and the old Linux plan tried the system package manager (`dnf`), which doesn't work on an rpm-ostree image.

The installer now detects immutable Linux (`/run/ostree-booted` exists, or `rpm-ostree` is on PATH) and plans `brew install maven` ahead of the `apt-get`/`dnf` branches. If Homebrew isn't available it returns no plan rather than falling through to `dnf`, and the failure message tells the learner to install Homebrew, put `brew` on PATH and retry. Other platforms are unchanged, except that any Linux host with `rpm-ostree` on PATH is now treated as immutable and skips the `apt-get`/`dnf`/`apk` branches.

## Changes

- `src/dependencies.ts`: new exported `isImmutableLinux`; `systemDependencyInstallPlan` takes an injectable `exists` argument and uses it for the check; the no-plan message is specific to Maven on immutable Linux.
- `test/dependencies.test.ts`: covers detection (marker file, command, neither, non-Linux), the Homebrew plan, and no `dnf` fallback without Homebrew.
- `docs/learn-verification.md`: step 18 now asks to confirm Homebrew is chosen over `dnf` on rpm-ostree, and that `dnf` isn't run if Homebrew is missing.
- `package.json`: 0.10.2 → 0.10.3.

## Testing

No test-suite or real-Bazzite result was captured for this PR. The new unit tests use injected platform/PATH/file checks. The manual step in the verification doc is the check for a real immutable system.

title: fix: make Claude hooks independent of PATH
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Why

The Claude Code integration invoked a bare `aifirst` command, both in the replay `UserPromptSubmit` hook and in the commands the skill tells Claude to run. When Claude Code inherits a PATH without `aifirst` (likely, for example, an already-running terminal on Windows that predates the installer), the hook fails with `aifirst: command not found` and exit code 127. That is the failure reported in the session that led to this branch.

## What changed

- **Launcher.** `aifirst skill install --claude` now writes `~/.claude/skills/aifirst/aifirst-cli.sh`, which `exec`s the current executable (plus the Bun entrypoint when running from source). Windows paths are converted to the Git Bash form. Helpers: `bashPath`, `shellQuote`, `currentCliArgv`, `claudeCliCommand`, `launcherScript` in `src/agents/claude.ts`.
- **Hook.** The replay hook command becomes `bash '<launcher>' replay hook # aifirst-managed-replay-hook-v1`. `isReplayHook` recognises both the legacy `aifirst replay hook` and the marked form, so reinstalling replaces the old hook rather than adding a second one.
- **Skill and command text.** `skillMarkdown` and `commandFiles` take the CLI command and render it everywhere the text used `aifirst`; the default stays `aifirst`, so other targets are unchanged.
- **Permissions.** `claudeEntries(command = "aifirst")` builds the `Bash(...)` allowlist entries for the launcher command. When permissions are installed, legacy `Bash(aifirst …)` entries are dropped and the launcher entries added. Status checks (including `bookmode`'s `preApproved`) look for the launcher entries. `revokePermissions` removes both legacy and launcher entries.
- **Docs.** `docs/integrations/replay.md` describes the launcher, the migration command, a direct-path fallback for PowerShell, and the Windows vs. shell installer split.

## Tests

Updated `test/agents.test.ts`, `test/permissions.test.ts` and `test/upgrade.test.ts` to cover launcher generation, hook migration and the allowlist replacement. I did not run them as part of preparing this PR, so there is no result to report here.

## Notes for review

Start with `claudeAgent.install` and `allowPermissions` in `src/agents/claude.ts`. Existing installs only migrate once the skill is refreshed with `aifirst skill install --claude`.

This description was drafted and self-reviewed inline by the same agent (no separate drafter or reviewer was available), and no comic was generated.

title: fix: make Claude hooks independent of PATH
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The Claude hook depended on `aifirst` being on the parent process's `PATH`. This PR routes the Claude hook, generated instructions and permission rules through a stable launcher rather than relying on `PATH`, not just the `UserPromptSubmit` hook.

**Design.** The hook, the generated skill and command instructions, and the permission rules all use a command derived from a Claude-owned launcher for the current `aifirst` executable. Previously, permission entries were hardcoded as `Bash(aifirst <cmd>:*)`; they are now `Bash(<launcher command> <cmd>:*)`, and the hook carries a managed marker so the legacy `aifirst replay hook` entry is recognised and replaced. The launcher records the executable that ran `skill install`, and the emitted `replay execute` step text in `src/commands/replay.ts` still says bare `aifirst`.

- Launcher paths have backslashes replaced with slashes, and drive-letter paths (`C:/…`) become `/c/…` for Git Bash only when `platform === "win32"`.
- When run from source under Bun (`src/index.ts`), the launcher preserves the entrypoint; a compiled binary needs only the executable.
- Arguments are quoted so spaces and apostrophes don't allow shell expansion.
- Existing installs migrate through `skill install`: legacy bare-command permissions are migrated or revoked without disturbing unrelated entries. The allowlist check now compares against launcher-based entries.
- `docs/integrations/replay.md` gives platform-specific install instructions instead of sending Windows to `install.sh`.

title: Improve the learner replay experience: collapsible code, Enter-gated prompts, portable Windows replay
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Replays in the learner needed a smoother terminal experience and an executor that can run captured Save the Duckling commands on Windows without external bash; this PR reworks how replays are shown and run.

**Display.** Code blocks longer than 40 lines are collapsed and `e` expands them (in the TUI, the latest collapsed block); the TUI document view also handles up/down (`k`/`j`) and page-up/page-down scrolling. On an interactive terminal the read-only exercise prompt waits for Enter after it finishes typing; `pauseForEnter` ignores an `AbortError` and returns early when not interactive. Typing animation runs at 40 characters per second unless `noAnimation` is set. Status and text events that trail a replay operation are carried as native blocks, and tool calls and results render as cards in the TUI. `tui-learn.test.ts` covers the Home screens for progress and the command reference, which dismiss on a key.

**Execution.** Previously a command without an exit status reported 127. On the async path, a spawned command that times out gets exit code 124, and an operation marked `expectedTimeout` is judged failed if the command did not hit the timeout; `<shell>` scripts get no timeout there. Portable commands carry `<python>` and `<shell>` forms: `<python>` is materialized with the selected launcher (the Windows one on Windows), and `<shell>` scripts run as compound scripts on the async path with `<workspace>` replaced by `.`. `materializeReplayCommand` was extracted from `executor.ts` and is called by `runCommand`. The `replay` command now calls `executeReplayAsync`. `graphical-run.test.ts` covers replacing captured pygame window launches with a portable compile check; `windows-duckling-replay.test.ts` covers executing the full captured timeline without external bash. Updated test fixtures and drivers support these tests. A new CI job, `windows-duckling-replay` on `windows-latest`, executes the portable replay. The package version is 0.10.5.

For users, replays pause for Enter and fold long code; replay tool display now carries a `toolName`.

title: Defer guided setup to a new terminal when installing on macOS
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

A macOS user reported that after the piped installer reached "Set up 2 tools? [Y/n]" they couldn't type anything. The same user had hit a similar problem with the Bun installer, where exiting and running the installed command worked fine.

On macOS, `install/install.sh` now skips the `aifirst init </dev/tty` step. It prints `aifirst init` as the next step to run in a new terminal. The cause is believed to be Bun failing to poll stdin reopened through macOS's `/dev/tty` alias (oven-sh/bun#41495). This comes from a code comment in `install.sh`, and I haven't independently confirmed it. The same comment says a direct invocation inherits the real tty device and stays interactive. Linux and Windows are unchanged: setup still starts immediately where `/dev/tty` is readable. The README describes the temporary extra step.

This is a workaround. The plan is to remove it once a durable fix lands in a release.

## What to look at

- `install/install.sh`: the new `darwin` branch ahead of the existing `/dev/tty` check. `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP=1` still skips setup entirely.
- `install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh` and `install/fixtures/macos_installer_tty_driver.py`: a macOS-only smoke test. It runs the real installer piped, with a fake `curl` serving the just-built binary, then drives `aifirst init` through a pty. It takes the binary path as its argument.
- CI: `ci.yml` runs the test on Darwin and shellchecks the new script. `release.yml` runs it against the built darwin binary.

## Testing

I did not run the macOS smoke test here. The environment is Linux and the script exits with an error off Darwin. It is wired into the CI and release macOS jobs, where it will first run. The `release.yml` step runs it after the darwin binary smoke checks. The test answers "n" at the init prompt, so it checks that input is accepted, not that tools get installed.

title: Defer guided setup on macOS until after the piped installer exits
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
A macOS user reported that the installer reaches "Set up 2 tools? [Y/n]" and then accepts no input; the same user had seen Bun's installer fail to take input the same way, while running the installed command afterwards worked. This PR is the requested workaround plus smoke test: "do the safe workaround and wait for the durable fix to land in a release. Also, do the recommended smoke test."

Previously, `install.sh` ran `aifirst init </dev/tty` when `/dev/tty` was openable. Now, when `$OS` is `darwin`, it skips that and prints "On macOS, finish setup in a new terminal: aifirst init"; other platforms keep the `/dev/tty` branch. The in-code comment attributes the cause to Bun being unable to poll stdin reopened through macOS's `/dev/tty` alias (oven-sh/bun#41495), and says a direct invocation inherits the real `/dev/ttysNNN` device and stays interactive, so setup is deferred until the pipe exits. The README now describes the extra macOS step as temporary.

The regression test, `install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh`, exits 2 off macOS or with a bad binary argument. It serves the just-built binary through a fake `curl`, so the installer's download and checksum flow still runs without depending on a published tag. It pipes `install.sh` into `sh` inside a PTY, then runs `aifirst init` directly and fails if the prompt shows up before the installer's finish marker. A Python PTY driver (`install/fixtures/macos_installer_tty_driver.py`) answers `n` to the one-tool prompt (`Set up 1 tool? [Y/n]`, matching the test's fixture setup rather than the reported two-tool prompt) and the test then expects `Nothing installed.`; the driver and fails on a 45s timeout, a missing prompt, or a non-zero exit. CI runs the test on Darwin runners after the existing smoke checks, the release workflow runs it against the built darwin binary just before the artifact upload step (so a failure there stops the upload), and shellcheck now covers the new script.

The recorded runs were on linux/x64, so none shows the macOS path running. No CI run of the workflow edits is in the session logs, and the recorded checks ran without a terminal, so none shows the PTY path with a user at the keyboard.

Where to start: the `darwin` branch in `install/install.sh` (first-setup block), then `install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh`.

Feedback wanted: is deferring setup on macOS acceptable until the Bun fix ships, or should we try `/dev/tty` first and fall back?

title: build: prepare releases for SignPath signing
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Why

A Windows user reported `aifirst` not being recognized in PowerShell after installing ; follow-up in the session showed the released v0.7.0 Windows exe segfaulting on `--version` while a newer Bun ran fine, so the compiled build was suspected (this PR does not show which change fixes it). Windows binaries were being cross-compiled from Linux with no version metadata and no code signature. This prepares the project for SignPath Foundation code signing and standardizes on Apache-2.0 (replacing MIT, per the maintainer's decision).

## What changed

- **Windows builds are native.** A new `build-windows` job in `release.yml` runs on `windows-latest`, because Bun only writes PE version resources on a Windows host. `scripts/build-config.ts` (new) selects targets per host OS and passes `--windows-title/publisher/version/description/copyright`. Windows targets are rejected on non-Windows hosts, and `--all` is removed. The job checks the resulting metadata, smoke-tests the x64 and baseline `.exe` files, and uploads them as `binaries-windows-unsigned`.
- **Release workflow.** Linux and darwin build only their own targets. Bun is pinned via the new `.bun-version` (also used by `ci.yml` and the drift, content-sync and learn-compatibility workflows), replacing `latest`. The `release` job runs only for `v*` tag pushes, so manual dispatch is a build-only dry run (the `tag` input is removed). The tag/`package.json` version check applies only to pushes.
- **`--bytecode` is no longer passed** to `bun build` (the `buildArgs` helper doesn't include it); `src/index.ts` only rewrites the related comment. The old comment credited bytecode with faster startup, so startup time may change.
- **SignPath prep.** Adds `.signpath/artifact-configuration.xml` and `.signpath/README.md`, `CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md`, and `.github/CODEOWNERS`. Signing isn't connected yet; the signed artifact will later replace the unsigned input before checksums.
- **Licensing and docs.** Adds the Apache-2.0 `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`, `TRADEMARKS.md`, and README updates. `package.json` is updated accordingly. `CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md` and `TRADEMARKS.md` contain public policy statements worth a maintainer's read.
- **Claude Code pin** is bumped to 2.1.252 in `.github/claude-code-version`.
- **Tests:** new `test/build-config.test.ts` and `test/signpath.test.ts`, plus an addition to `test/platform.test.ts`.

`release` now also depends on `build-windows`, so that job gates publishing; it skips `tsc` and `bun test` (the Linux job runs them).

## Verification

- An earlier `npm run test:unit` run passed during development; it was not re-run for this PR text.
- The Claude Code pin commit's message reports a passing compatibility suite run in CI; no CI result was captured here.
- No captured evidence that the new Windows job has run; a manual `Release` dispatch would confirm. Only x64 and baseline are smoke-tested.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Windows users reported that the released `aifirst.exe` crashed on launch with a Bun segmentation fault, while a stock Bun runtime worked; the request was to fix it and publish replacement Windows executables for the latest release. This PR changes how releases are built and prepares the repository for a SignPath Foundation application.

**Build changes.** Previously the build chose a target from the host platform and threw "No build target" when none matched. Now `scripts/build-config.ts` adds `selectBuildTargets` and `buildArgs`: by default it builds the host OS family, an explicit `--target` is accepted unless it names a Windows target on a non-Windows host, and the obsolete all-platform and cross-host Windows builds are rejected. Windows metadata arguments are added when the target is a native Windows build. `build.ts` throws `Unsupported build host` on platforms other than linux, darwin and win32. The commit message describes this as building Windows artifacts natively with enforced PE metadata.

**Release workflow.** In `release.yml` the `build-linux-windows` job is replaced by a `build-linux` job and a `build-windows` job on `windows-latest`; The workflow comment says Bun writes Windows version resources on a Windows host, and that job builds with release metadata, fails unless every Windows exe carries the expected product, company, version, description and copyright, smoke-tests the x64 and x64-baseline exes, and uploads unsigned artifacts. The `release` job now needs `learn-compatibility`, `build-linux`, `build-windows` and `build-darwin`, and runs when the event is a push of a `v*` tag. Bun is pinned to 1.4.0 in `.bun-version`, which the other workflows now read instead of an unpinned `latest`.

**SignPath and licensing.** Adds a SignPath artifact configuration, a code-signing policy, a README note that the application is pending, CODEOWNERS entries and trademark terms. Licensing moves to Apache-2.0 (LICENSE, NOTICE, `package.json`), as requested in the session. A comment in `src/index.ts` is reworded. Tests: `test/build-config.test.ts` covers target selection and Windows metadata; `test/platform.test.ts` covers bytecode not being embedded in cross-compiled executables; `test/signpath.test.ts` covers the SignPath prerequisites and licensing files. ## Summary

Quality-of-life changes to the learner TUI. Long prompts and plans stream in slowly, and an exercise that read an image showed up as stray terminal characters.

The abort signal reaches only the non-shell command path; `<shell>` commands are not cancelled.
- **Menus.** Selections follow the latest output, and the picker detail is a scrollable compact pane.
- Version bump to 0.13.4.

`aifirst run` was restructured around `executePreparedExercise`. Its output path changed slightly, and a program with no output now prints "Program completed with no console output."

New and updated tests cover streaming and skip, scroll-follow, interactive programs, plan streaming, the renderer, run and replay flow (`test/tui-streaming.test.ts`, `test/terminal-renderer.test.ts`, `test/run.test.ts`, `test/replay-flow.test.ts`, others). body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Relicenses the repository's committed content from MIT to Apache License 2.0. The request in the session was to standardize AI First on Apache-2.0, citing its explicit contributor patent grant and patent-retaliation protection among other reasons.

## Changes

- Adds the standard Apache 2.0 `LICENSE` text and a `NOTICE` naming the copyright holders.
- Changes `license` in `package.json` from `MIT` to `Apache-2.0`.
- Adds a `License` section to `README.md` stating the license covers the committed source, schemas, examples, explanations and replay data, but not the private source manuscripts or the separately published Apress books.
- Adds `TRADEMARKS.md`, naming Stephen Chin, Cassandra Chin and Jennifer Reif as owners of the "AI First" names and logos. The Apache license does not grant rights to them; accurate reference is allowed, implying endorsement is not.

title: ci: verify every book step in isolation and in sequence
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What changed

CI used to run each exercise once, alone, in a throwaway temp directory. That could not catch a step that only breaks because of what earlier steps left in a shared project (for example, the Chapter 6 Maven workspace). This PR adds a second pass that walks each book in order in one persistent workspace, and makes that walk a gate on PRs, main and releases.

- **`scripts/run-exercises.ts`** is rewritten. It has two passes: `--isolated` (the old per-step behaviour) and `--sequential` (one workspace per book, steps in book order). With neither flag, both run. It also accepts `--report <file>` for a JSON report, `--json` and `--keep-workspace`. Steps with an external launch are reported as `delegated` to the CLI book walk. A sequential book stops at its first failure, and the failed workspace path is printed.
- In the sequential pass, for project-style steps the files the previous step managed in that project are removed unless the new step also uses them, along with any `scaffold.clean` paths. This stops stale files from leaking forward.
- **`scripts/lib/verify.ts`**: `verify` takes an optional `directory` to reuse a caller-owned workspace and does not delete it afterwards. The default is unchanged (a temp directory that is removed).
- **Workflows**: the old `run-exercises` job in `ci.yml` moves into a reusable `exercise-walk.yml`. It runs both passes, installs Maven and the JUnit launcher, and uploads `report.json` as an artifact even on failure. `ci.yml` calls it, and `release.yml` calls it and makes `release` depend on it. `actions/setup-java` goes from v4 to v5.
- **Book data fixes the walk needed**:
  - Java Chapter 6 poms now set `maven.compiler.source` and `target` to 17.
  - The Thermostat step cleans `ThermostatApp.java`.
  - Python `py-2-12` gets a `py-2-12/` project root so its `math.py` can't shadow the standard library.
- `.gitignore` gains one entry, and the package version goes from 2.0.0 to 2.0.1.

## Tests

- New `test/exercise-walk-workflow.test.ts` checks the workflow wiring: both passes, Maven, `if: always()` on the upload, and that CI and release call the walk.
- `test/filenames.test.ts` checks `py-2-12` resolves to `py-2-12/math.py`.

title: Defer guided setup to a new terminal in the macOS installer
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
A Mac user reported that the installer reaches "Set up 2 tools? [Y/n]" and then accepts no keyboard input; running the installed command afterwards works fine. This PR applies the safe workaround while a durable fix lands in a release.

On macOS, Bun cannot poll stdin reopened through the `/dev/tty` alias (oven-sh/bun#41495, per the code comment), whereas a direct invocation inherits the real tty device and stays interactive, so setup is deferred until the installer's pipe has exited.

When `$OS` is `darwin` and setup isn't skipped via `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP=1`, `install.sh` now skips guided setup and prints a two-line hint to finish setup in a new terminal by running `aifirst init`. Other platforms keep the existing `/dev/tty` branch and its fallback.

The CLI docs page now says that on Linux and Windows the installer continues directly into guided setup, while on macOS users open a new terminal and run `aifirst init`, described as a temporary step.


Where to start: the new `darwin` branch in the first-setup block of `static/install.sh`.

title: Stop xdg-desktop-portal on Gamescope exit to avoid stale KDE portal
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

After leaving Gaming Mode, Flatpaks such as Deskflow could fail because `xdg-desktop-portal` stayed alive in the shared user systemd manager without its KDE backend interfaces (InputCapture, FileChooser, Settings). This adds a best-effort teardown hook to the Gamescope drop-in so the next Plasma session activates a fresh portal.

## Changes

- `scripts/gamescope-clear-autologin.conf`: adds `ExecStopPost=-/usr/bin/systemctl --user stop xdg-desktop-portal.service` ahead of the existing autologin-clearing `ExecStopPost`. The leading `-` keeps a failing stop (shutdown, closing user bus) from marking the Gamescope unit failed. Autologin clearing remains failure-reporting. Comment text updated to match.
- `tests/test-units.sh` (new): static checks of hook count, ordering and the `-` prefix, plus a `systemd-analyze --user verify` of the drop-in when the Gamescope base unit is present (otherwise skipped).
- `tests/test-ensure.sh`: mode set to executable and shellcheck annotation cleanups, plus an `export` on `WAYLAND_SESSION_DIR` in the subshell; no behavior change intended.
- `README.md`: documents the hook, a troubleshooting entry with a `gdbus introspect` check and manual recovery commands, a note to re-run the installer after updating, and the new test.

## Testing

- `./tests/test-ensure.sh`: all passed (run directly by the agent before opening this PR; no receipt captured).
- `./tests/test-units.sh`: all passed, including the `systemd-analyze` verification of the drop-in.

title: fix(digest): don't count commands quoted inside scripts or heredocs
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What

The digest split shell command lines on `;`, `|`, `&&`, `||` and newlines even inside quotes and heredoc bodies. A line of an inline script that merely mentioned `bun test` (`python -c "..."`, `cat <<'EOF' ... EOF`) therefore counted as a test run, and its grouping key came out as `bun test',`. This fixes a known gap noted in PR #8 (per the commit message).

## How

- New `splitCommands` in `src/util/shell.ts` splits a command line while leaving quoted strings (with escapes) and heredoc bodies alone; splitting resumes after the heredoc terminator.
- Test detection (`testSegment`), grouping (`commandKey`) and commit detection (`makesCommit` in `correlate.ts`) now use it.
- Commit detection (`makesCommit`) now ignores `git commit` text that only appears inside quotes or heredocs, so it also affects which commits are matched to a session, not just test counts.
- `commandKey` also drops flags, heredoc and redirection tokens, so `python - <<'PY'` groups as `python`.
- Version bumped to 1.0.0-rc.12 and the bundled `dist/tracetoon.mjs` rebuilt.

## Tests

`tests/shell.test.ts` covers chains and pipes, quoted scripts, heredoc bodies and what follows them, test detection, and grouping keys.

title: fix(digest): leave work already in the base branch out of PR summaries
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Digests could include work that belonged to other PRs and misread some test and feedback signals. In the session the author asked to check whether Tracetoon's summaries are being generated properly (while dogfooding it); the commit message describes the fixes as the result of an evaluation harness.

Per the commit message, that harness (six real stretches of work with known ground truth) went from 41/48 to 50/50 checks. That is the commit's account only; it was not rerun for this description.

**What changes**
- **Earlier work is left out.** Previously the match window ended 30 minutes after the last commit (or at the current time for a dirty checkout), and nothing excluded work already merged. For a branch with commits, the window now ends 5 minutes after the last commit, and uncommitted changes no longer stretch it; the zero-commit (working tree) path is unchanged. A cutoff is set from the session's last commit that the base branch already has. Only the 200 most recent base commits are considered. A turn that ended before the cutoff is dropped (a turn's end is its last edit time); a turn that crosses it keeps its prompts, plans, decisions, replies and usage, and loses its other records stamped at or before the cutoff (later records stay). Link and artifact records are never dropped. Commits are matched by SHA in command output or by subject (at least 12 characters) in any `git commit` command containing it; this also changes `commitsMadeBy` and so the "commits made in sessions" count. Files under `.git` no longer count as repo edits.
- **Test results.** Failures are read from test output as well as exit status, so piped runs (`bun test | tail`) count and "tests went from failing to passing" can appear. A chained command is labeled by its test segment.
- **Rejection feedback.** Text typed while rejecting a tool call is kept as a prompt that continues the turn.
- **Diffs.** Binary file changes count as changed files. `prTruth` takes an optional `head`, used by the harness to describe past PRs.
- **Sagas.** Sharing an agent session no longer relates two PRs; only stacked branches or PRs linked in the logs do. The saga test in `tests/comic.test.ts` is rewritten to match: a shared session alone gives no saga, and a linked PR passes its saga id on.
- **Preview.** "Sessions used" is replaced by an Evidence section (facts, per-session prompts, plans, decisions, tests, milestones, suggested disclosure trailers). The writing guide gains a "Check every claim" section.
- **New local script.** `scripts/eval-summaries.ts` (258 lines) runs the harness. It has hardcoded SHAs, branches and `~/Development` paths, writes its report under `.git`, and is not wired into tests or CI.
- Version moves to 1.0.0-rc.6 and the bundle is rebuilt.

There is no recorded decision on the cutoff and window approach, so those choices are open to pushback.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Tracetoon is meant to be dogfooded on its own development, and the open question was whether its summaries are generated properly. This PR makes the digest more faithful to the work behind a PR and shows the digest's facts beside the description so each claim can be checked.

Previously the correlation window ended at `truth.dirty ? nowMs : last + 30 * 60_000`; it is now `last + 5 * 60_000`. Per the commit message, work already in the base branch is left out and work after the last commit belongs to the next PR. Turns that finished before the cutoff are dropped (a turn's end is its last edit), while a turn that crosses it keeps its conversation. Files under `.git` (Tracetoon's own run files) are not repo edits, and binary files count as changed.

Other digest fixes:
- Failure detection for test commands also reads the output, so piped runs such as `bun test | tail` are counted. Test commands are labeled by their test runner, not the first command.
- Quiet commits (`git commit -q`) are recognized by their subject; `prTruth` can describe a given head instead of the checkout.
- Feedback typed while rejecting a tool call is kept as a prompt and continues the turn.
- Sharing a session no longer makes two PRs a saga; stacked branches and linked PRs still relate.

The preview gains an Evidence section with the digest's facts, and the writing guide asks for a claim-by-claim check before rendering. `scripts/eval-summaries.ts` is an evaluation harness that rebuilds digests for six real stretches of work; its default output lists PASS/FAIL lines per check and `--json` prints a JSON object with `pass`, `total` and per-case results; the commit message calls it local. ## Summary

Three fixes found while dogfooding Tracetoon on its own PRs, plus a version bump to 1.0.0-rc.8.

- **Clickable preview links** (b95f159): `render` and `preview` printed a bare path, which agents relayed as a relative path the user couldn't open. They now print an absolute `file:///` URL (Ctrl+click in terminals), also returned as `previewUrl` in `--json`; `preview` prints the comic image path as a `file:///` URL too. The skill text tells agents to pass the link on as printed.
- **Earlier work and viewed commits no longer land in a PR's story** (f167fc6): a turn's end was judged by every edit, so an edit outside the repo (a report, notes) kept a whole earlier turn in the PR. Edits inside the repo now decide where a turn ends (a turn with no in-repo edits still falls back to all its records). Separately, a commit SHA in any command's output counted as the session having made the commit, so `git log` in another repo claimed authorship; now a SHA in output only counts when the command makes commits (commit, merge, cherry-pick, revert, am, rebase, pull), chained or not. - **`cd`-prefixed commands are judged by where they run** (c973ef3): agents log a command with the shell directory from before it ran, so `cd ../other-repo && bun test` was filed under this repo. - The eval harness pins two cases (PR #1 and a Codex case) to fixed commits, since their branches have since merged or been committed.

New tests cover `leadingCd`, commit-maker detection and the preview URL in `tests/units.test.ts`, `tests/flow.test.ts` and `tests/summary-fixes.test.ts`. The bundled `plugin/skills/tracetoon/dist/tracetoon.mjs` is rebuilt.

## What changed

`tracetoon comic art` now draws the comic with an AI image model once the user has approved a route, and falls back to the built-in artist if the provider fails (a warning says so).

title: Add crossjudge command to judge drafts across two compare runs
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What

`compare` only judges drafts within one run. This adds `prbench crossjudge --candidate <dir> --baseline <dir> --out <dir>` (entry point `crossJudge` in `src/crossjudge.ts`), which pairs the `tracetoon-candidate` drafts of one finished `compare` run with the `tracetoon-baseline` drafts of another (for example runs that used different writer models) and judges them from the artifacts those runs saved. No writer runs. Case definitions and fact sheets are loaded from the baseline run.

## Behavior

- Each run must be a `prbench.comparison/v2` experiment with exactly one writer model.
- The runs must agree on judge contract, judges, rubric version, replicates, split and cases, and the judge contract must match this harness. A mismatch fails; the run comparison lists every differing field. Effort, provider and systems are not compared.
- Each draft needs a saved receipt whose digest and experiment id match; a missing or mismatched draft aborts before any judge call.
- Each pair is judged in both orders by every configured judge. Results are summarised with the same consensus rule `compare` uses (a win only when every judge's two orders agree), plus per-draft composite scores and judge cost. Output goes to `--out` (`crossjudge.json`, `pairs.json`, `summary.json`, `summary.md`, per-replicate judgments).
- Options: `--cache <dir>` (default `<parent of --out>/.prbench-cache/v2`), `--plan` (verify inputs and print planned judge calls without calling models), `--parallel <n>` (default 4, must be a positive integer).
- Outside `--plan` it requires a Claude login and prints consensus W/T/L, judge cost and the `summary.md` path. Errors exit with code 2.
- `modelRoot` in `src/comparison.ts` is now exported so crossjudge can locate each run's drafts.

title: Retry timed-out judges and fix isolation-proof resume for effort arms
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Two judge/resume fixes plus score-report improvements, taken from the commit messages (attributed to the commits `08b8254` and `18d2df1`).

- **Judge retries.** Timed-out and transient judge calls are retried up to 3 attempts with backoff instead of invalidating the run, including on resume after a persisted timeout. Codex judges now report timeouts as such. Failed judge attempts record their judge, and the score report gains a judge-reliability table beside writer reliability.
- **Isolation proofs for effort arms.** Probes saved the bare model (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) while resume compared against the arm spec (`claude-sonnet-5-5@medium`), so every resume of an arm with an effort was refused with "Saved isolation proof does not match this experiment." Probes now record the arm; proofs saved earlier match on the bare model (the experiment id still binds the exact arms).
- **Codex usage.** Writer tokens and estimated cost sum every thread the run spawned (main plus forked subagent rollouts), counting each response id once. Older runs are recomputed from saved traces, and the score table states what each cost covers.
- **Score report.** The judgment walk skips `*.attempts` folders; paired composite deltas gain a leave-one-case-out range and a per-case delta table.
- **Writer environment hash** (Codex and Claude) ignores shell, terminal and session bookkeeping variables; experiments frozen with the legacy hash keep it while it still matches.

title: Run compare in parallel on Codex or Claude, end to end
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

`prbench compare` previously used only Codex (Sol and Terra wrote the PRs and judged them), and ran everything serially. This PR adds a provider choice and a parallel scheduler.

- `--provider codex|claude|both` selects who writes and who judges. Codex keeps Sol and Terra, with its frozen identity unchanged. Claude runs Claude Code on Opus and Sonnet at medium effort, with the same models judging. `both` runs two independent comparisons in `<out>/codex` and `<out>/claude`. Providers are never mixed, and a frozen experiment refuses to resume under another provider.
- `--parallel <n>` (default 4) schedules writers and judges as one job graph (isolation probes run through their own bounded pool). A judge starts once the two drafts it compares exist. Results are persisted in a fixed order so they do not depend on timing, and `--parallel 1` keeps the serial order. After a failure nothing new starts; running jobs finish and are saved.
- `--models <ids>` replaces the provider's writer models while keeping its judges, so a cheaper writer (for example Haiku) is scored by the same judges. Ids must be distinct, and `--provider both` refuses the option.

## Fixes made along the way

- Judge references are constrained by a per-prompt schema. In the author's runs, Claude judges invented fact IDs or cited the other draft's evidence; reference fields are now enums of the IDs each side may cite. `checkJudgment` still validates what a schema can't express.
- The Claude environment identity no longer hashes the launch directory (`PWD`, `OLDPWD`, `INIT_CWD`, `npm_*`), so the identity no longer depends on where the comparison is launched (previously this blocked `--reuse-from`). The Codex hash is unchanged.
- Windows-recorded cases replay correctly on POSIX hosts: the checkout is named by the last segment of the recorded path, and Windows paths under a mapped prefix get POSIX separators. (Author-reported: replayed edits now link to the checkout where before none did.)
- The sandbox's fake `gh` treats `--help`, `-h` and `gh help` as help, not as a second PR creation with no title.
- An escaped dot in a shell glob is no longer read as an absolute host path.

## Also in this PR

- Concurrent Codex runs share the login file through a symlink with a lease (a copy mode remains for Windows), which changes credential handling; review this closely.
- New Claude writer arm with `--effort` plumbing; `--development` and `--reuse-from` use per-provider subdirectories.
- The sandbox drops `CLAUDECODE`, `ANTHROPIC_` and `CLAUDE_CODE_` environment variables; README documents the providers.

## Testing

Earlier in development, targeted `bun test` runs of the claude-comparison, agents, codex and isolation test files passed, but those ran before later edits, so they don't establish the final state. I did not re-run the suite for this description. New tests: `tests/parallel-compare.test.ts`, `tests/pool.test.ts`. No hosted CI status was checked.

body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The request was to let `compare` run either a Claude end-to-end run (writers and judges), a Codex end-to-end run, or both, without mixing Claude and ChatGPT runs and judges, and to add the parallel pipeline so results come back quickly.

**Providers.** `compare --provider codex|claude|both` picks who writes and who judges. Codex keeps Sol and Terra with its frozen identity unchanged; Claude runs Claude Code on Opus and Sonnet at medium effort, with the same models judging; `both` runs two independent comparisons in `<out>/codex` and `<out>/claude`. Providers are not mixed, and a frozen experiment refuses to resume under another provider. Claude writers get the frozen skill and runtime with a stripped Anthropic/Claude Code environment and MCP servers turned off; the Claude comparison system is `claudeComparisonSystem`, with a native arm and a Tracetoon arm. A Claude isolation probe reads the startup catalogue, and Claude judges run with no tools and no hooks. `prbench auth claude` stores a setup token.

**Parallelism.** `--parallel <n>` (default 4) schedules writers, judges and isolation probes as one job graph: a judge runs as soon as the two drafts it compares exist, results are persisted in a fixed order, and `--parallel 1` keeps the serial order. After a failure nothing new starts and running jobs finish and are saved. Concurrent Codex runs share the dedicated login through a symlink instead of queuing on exclusive copies; Windows keeps the copy mode.

**Writer models.** To test whether a cheaper writer (Haiku, Luna) can match a stronger one, `compare --models <ids>` replaces the provider's writer models. The provider's judges stay the same, so cheap and strong writers are scored by the same judges. Models must be distinct ids, and `--provider both` refuses the option.

Fixes found along the way:
- Claude judges invented fact IDs and cited the other draft's evidence; judge calls given a reference set now get a schema whose reference fields are enums of the IDs that side may cite.
- The Claude profile hashed PWD, OLDPWD, INIT_CWD and npm_* variables, so launching from another directory blocked `--reuse-from`; writers run in their own sandbox cwd, and the Codex hash is unchanged for frozen runs.
- Replaying the public cases on Linux made Tracetoon's prepare fail on the checkout's name. Session paths were also rewritten just up to the mapped prefix, so both Tracetoon arms lost all edit attribution; the checkout is now named by the recorded path's last segment in either syntax, a Windows path under a mapped prefix gets POSIX separators, and unrelated host paths keep their spelling. The commit message reports 92 linked edits on pr8 and 45 on pr5, versus 0 before.
- A Codex writer listed files with `rg --files -g '!\.agents/**'`; the scope audit read the escape as host agent state and rejected the draft. A backslash escaping a leading dot is now dropped when the token continues without backslashes; Windows paths are still flagged.
- A Codex writer ran `gh pr create --help` after opening its PR, and the fake `gh` took it as a second, empty PR creation. Help invocations (--help, -h, gh help) now print help, record a help call and do not count as a PR.

title: Performance gate: pass on paired priced cost per draft, not time and tokens
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

The performance gate used to pass on writer wall time and input tokens. It now passes on the cost of each draft, priced the same way `prbench score` prices it.

Per the commit message, the gate passes when the candidate/baseline geometric mean of paired per-draft priced cost is at most 1.000. Pairs are matched on model, case and replicate. Log ratios are averaged within each case, then across cases, so repeats and models of one case don't count as independent cases.

## What changed

- **Shared cost function.** `draftCost` in `src/report/score.ts` now holds the per-draft pricing:
  - It uses the reported total where the agent gives one.
  - Otherwise it estimates from token counts through the existing `estimateCostByModel`, which this PR doesn't change.
  - For Codex, usage counts only when it covers all threads; main-thread-only usage is marked as such.
- **Gate rule.** `src/performance.ts` bumps the schema to `prbench.performance/v3`.
  - The case-clustered 95% interval is reported but not required.
  - With every paired draft priced and validation usable, a ratio above 1.000 fails the gate.
  - The rule text is stated once as `COST_RULE` and shown in the report and `summary.md`.
- **Inconclusive when unpriced.** Any paired draft without a usable priced cost makes the gate inconclusive and is listed in `unpricedDrafts`. That covers a missing model price, missing tokens, Codex usage limited to the main thread, or a nonpositive cost.
- **Time and tokens are information only.** The writer-time ratio and token medians are still reported, but they no longer decide the result. Pairs without timing no longer drop out of the cost ratio.
- **Unchanged.** The validation-comparability handling is as before. Changing `src/performance.ts` changes the gate policy hash, as noted in the CHANGELOG.
- `src/comparison.ts` attaches `pricedCost` to each writer row and prints the rule, the cost ratio and the unpriced drafts in the comparison summary. README and CHANGELOG describe the new rule.
- The report also gains per-model median costs, `pricedPairs` and `timedPairs`.

## Testing

I did not run the tests or typecheck while preparing this description. `tests/performance.test.ts` and `tests/comparison.test.ts` were updated for the new rule. Hosted CI status is not known.
