title: Add absolute draft scoring and retry flaky low-effort writers
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Adds absolute per-draft scoring and an accuracy-first view to `prbench`, lets `compare` run writers at a chosen effort, and stops flaky low-effort writers from invalidating whole runs.

**Why:** the comparison data showed the graph brief's most repeatable win is accuracy (fewer factual errors), which the composite score hides, and low-effort writers (Luna@low, Sonnet@low, Haiku@low) kept killing runs by publishing nothing, mistyping a sandbox path, or timing out.

## Changes

- **Scoring** (`src/report/score.ts`, `src/cli.ts`): new `prbench score <roots…>` and a Scores section in compare summaries — per-draft coverage, rubric, factual errors, unsupported claims and traps, with a documented 0–100 composite, case-clustered bootstrap intervals and paired candidate deltas. Works retroactively on old runs.
- **Accuracy view**: error rate per arm, error classes, and each candidate against each baseline with a 0.05 claim-coverage guard and the cost ratio.
- **Cost estimates** (`src/report/prices.json`): USD estimated from token counts when a run reports none (Codex).
- **Effort per arm** (`src/run/arm.ts`, `src/comparison.ts`): `compare --models model@effort`; the writer gets the bare model plus that effort (default medium), saved artifacts must match both. Isolation probes run at the configured effort rather than the arm's (`src/run/isolation.ts`), since Haiku@low misreported the skill path.
- **Writer retries** (`src/run/comparisonWriter.ts`, `src/run/ledger.ts`): "no PR produced" (`no-draft`), scope-audit rejections and timeouts are each retried (up to 3 attempts) and counted per arm in a writer reliability table. Rejected drafts are never scored, and writer output is cached only after the scope audit passes so a retry doesn't hit the immutable cache entry.
- **Fake gh** (`src/run/fake-gh.ts`): supports `--fill`, `--fill-first`, `--fill-verbose`, taking title/body from the branch commits; explicit `--title`/`--body` win.

## Testing

Earlier in development, `bun test` passed (240 pass, 0 fail) and targeted suites for score, comparison, arm and sandbox passed. These ran before some later edits; I did not re-run them for this PR, and hosted CI status is unknown.

A Claude comparison could not be resumed from a new shell. The environment hash still covered most inherited variables, including per-process ones such as `CLAUDE_PID` and `INVOCATION_ID`, so the identity changed between shells. Sandboxes now drop `CLAUDE_*` variables and per-login session bookkeeping, and the Claude environment hash skips that same list (`claudeComparableEnv` in `provider.ts`, `sandboxEnv` in `sandbox.ts`), so other variables a writer can see still change it. The hash already skipped `FAKE_` and `PRBENCH_CLAUDE_` names, which the sandbox does not drop. The list is `VOLATILE_ENV` (e.g. `INVOCATION_ID`, `SHLVL`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`) plus `VOLATILE_PREFIXES` (`KONSOLE_`, `CLAUDE_`), exported from `sandbox.ts` and imported by `provider.ts`. Previously the sandbox dropped the `CODEX_`, `ANTHROPIC_` and `CLAUDE_CODE_` prefixes; `KONSOLE_` and `CLAUDE_` are now dropped too, and `CLAUDE_` takes over the last. Per the code comment, `CLAUDE_` covers the host session's `CLAUDE_CODE_*`, `CLAUDE_PID` and `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, which would otherwise reach a writer's Claude Code. Writers also lose `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `GPG_TTY` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`.

The new test in `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts`, `shell bookkeeping neither reaches writers nor changes the environment identity` sets `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, `INVOCATION_ID` and `SHLVL`, checks the hash is unchanged and the sandbox env lacks them, then checks that an unrelated variable still changes the hash.

The recorded request for these turns asked about how the graph is constructed and optimizing it; this diff does not touch graph code, so that request is not this change's purpose.

title: Add showtail upgrade command for standalone installs
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Adds `showtail upgrade` so people with a standalone install can update in place instead of re-running the installer. The request that started this work was: "Make a showtail upgrade command to upgrade showtail from an install so users don't have to re-run the installer."

## What changed

- **New command** (`src/cli.ts`, `src/commands/upgrade.ts`): `showtail upgrade [--json]`, listed under a new "Maintain Showtail:" help group. It is added to `NO_BOOTSTRAP`, so first-run setup does not run before it.
- **Upgrade logic** (`src/core/selfUpgrade.ts`):
  - Queries the latest release of `Tingsters/Showtail` (overridable with `SHOWTAIL_REPO`) and picks the asset for the current OS and architecture. Supported: linux/darwin on x64/arm64, and Windows x64.
  - Compares plain `x.y.z` versions. If the install is current or newer than the latest release, it makes no changes.
  - Refuses to run unless the executable is named `showtail` or `showtail.exe`, which keeps a Bun or source run (where the executable is the Bun runtime) from being replaced. This is a name check only.
  - Downloads the binary next to the install and runs `--version` on it. The reported version must match the release before anything is replaced. It then downloads `showtail.vsix`, and a release without that asset is an error.
  - On Linux and macOS it swaps the binary and `showtail.vsix` with backups, restores both if either swap fails, and then runs `setup --first-run --json` to refresh capture integrations. If that refresh fails, the command prints a note that integrations will refresh on the next run.
  - On Windows the running executable is locked, so a detached PowerShell helper waits for the process to exit, swaps the files with rollback on failure, and refreshes integrations. The command reports `pending`.
- **Docs**: CHANGELOG, README, installation guide, CLI reference and the classroom workflow page, which now points students to `showtail upgrade`.

## Testing

I did not run the test suite while preparing this description. The branch adds `tests/selfUpgrade.test.ts` (222 lines) and a CLI test in `tests/cli.test.ts`. Their results are not recorded here, and I have not checked hosted CI.

## Notes

- Integrity of the download rests on running the new binary with `--version`; there is no checksum or signature check. `GITHUB_TOKEN`, if set, is sent as a Bearer token on the release lookup only. Release tags that are not plain `x.y.z` make the command fail. Requests time out after 30s (release lookup) and 120s (downloads), and empty downloads are rejected.
- On Windows the helper is detached and silent and waits up to 30s for the process to exit; the command reports `extensionUpdated` and `integrationsRefreshed` as false because those finish afterwards.
- Windows replacement goes through a generated PowerShell script. The upgrade logic is tested through the injectable `fetchFn`, `verifyDownloaded`, `replaceDownloaded` and `refreshInstalledIntegrations` options; I have not exercised a real Windows swap.
- The description was drafted and self-reviewed inline by the coordinating agent. No independent reviewer was used.

For users, `upgrade` refuses to run when the executable isn't named `showtail`/`showtail.exe` (a Bun or source invocation), so the Bun runtime or a source checkout isn't replaced, and does so before any network request. `upgrade` is also exempt from the first-run bootstrap in `src/cli.ts`.

Prepares the repository for Windows code signing through the SignPath Foundation. Session prompts S1/S3 asked for a plan to meet the SignPath Foundation's requirements (including open-source licensing) and then to implement it. This PR does not enable signing by itself.

Two deterministic improvements to the graph evidence brief, so a drafter can tell which changed function carries a behavior and which way a change goes.

title: Record every check in a chained command, and keep the full merge base
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What and why

The digest recorded at most one verification run per shell command, and with the chained commands agents commonly write (`bun run bundle; bun x tsc --noEmit && bun test > log; bun scripts/eval-summaries.ts`) it picked the test run and attached every result line of the whole output to it. Per the commit message, the eval's "57/57 checks pass" ended up attached to the tests, while the bundle, typecheck and eval looked like they had never run, and agents writing PR descriptions then said checks "were not run" when they had been. The commit message also reports this caused most of the factual errors Opus made in a prbench comparison (not re-verified here).

Separately, `digest.json` stored the merge base cut to 12 characters, while `tracetoon source --revision base` requires a full hash, so it always failed with "Code evidence must use the prepared base or head revision".

## Changes

- **One run per check** (`src/digest/build.ts`): new `commandRuns` returns a run for each verification segment in a command (several test-runner segments collapse into one run); `commandRun` now returns the first of them in command order (previously a test segment took precedence; only tests still call it), and the digest loop records all of them. When a command holds several checks, each run keeps only the output lines of its own kind (test, typecheck, lint, build, eval). A failure known only from the exit status of such a chain is recorded as `unknown` rather than pinned on one check; a failure visible in a check's own result lines (e.g. "1 fail") is still `failed`. Chains with several test runners still collapse into one `unknown` test run, as before.
- **Full merge base**: the digest's `mergeBase` is no longer sliced to 12 characters.
- **Tests**: `tests/evidence.test.ts` covers a bundle/test/eval chain (kinds `build`, `test`, `eval`, with the eval line not leaking into the test run), `&&` chains, and the failure case. `tests/preparation.test.ts` checks `source --revision base` returns a 40-hex revision.

## Verification

title: Stop Windows CI hanging on Bun that won't exit; share one gh target repo
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Why

The commit messages report Windows CI runs hanging or failing after the tests had finished their work (no hosted CI result was captured for this description). Windows runs hung several times in a different test file each time. Bun 1.3.14 on Windows sometimes printed its full result and then never exited, so `spawnSync` in the tests (and the test runner itself) waited until a timeout or until the job was cancelled. The request that started this work was to look into those CI failures (S1); the commit messages record the Windows observations.

## What changed

- **CLI exits explicitly.** After stdout and stderr are flushed, `src/cli.ts` calls `process.exit` with the command's exit code instead of relying on a natural exit. It also writes that code to `$TRACETOON_EXIT_FILE` (when set) just before exiting, and removes the variable from its own environment so child processes do not inherit it.
- **Spawn guard for tests.** `tests/spawn-guard.ts` runs a command with inherited stdio. If the exit file appears and the process is still alive 3s later, it kills it (`taskkill /T /F` on Windows, `SIGKILL` elsewhere) and returns the recorded code. Commands that exit on their own, or never finish, behave as before. `tests/helpers.ts`, which is preloaded for every test file, mocks `node:child_process` so `spawnSync(bun, [cli.ts|tracetoon.mjs, ...])` goes through the guard.
- **Test runner tolerates a stuck Bun.** In `scripts/test-files.ts`, once a file's summary line appears the runner waits 20s for Bun to exit, then kills it and takes the result from the summary's pass/fail counts. Killed children's pipes are destroyed and unref'd. `test-source` and `test-packaged` exit explicitly after flushing.
- **Review test helpers.** `review-run` and `review-lean` tests redirect CLI output to files rather than pipes, because on Windows a piped `spawnSync` waits for every holder of the pipe. A call that timed out with its full JSON result on stdout counts as finished. Each CLI call is capped (90s) and a timeout error names the command with its partial output. Per-test timeout is 120s.
- **Per-file watchdog.** The test runner kills a test file (and its process tree) after 15 minutes (`TRACETOON_TEST_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS`) and prints what it had so far; the CI test job has a 45 minute limit instead of GitHub's 6 hour default. The `review-run` test also sets a 60s review timeout, and a merged-list test no longer depends on reviewer completion order (it failed on macOS).
- **One gh target repo.** The branch also carries earlier commits: `context`, `doctor` and `publish` share a single target (gh's default repo when it is a remote of this clone, else origin) and pass `--repo` to every PR/repo gh call; `publish` refuses if the target changed since approval; forks publish with `--head owner:branch`; `doctor` checks push access on origin. Check receipts are read whenever a run has any, not only after `task begin`.
- The bundled `plugin/skills/tracetoon/dist/tracetoon.mjs` and `build.json` are rebuilt for the new build identity.

## Testing

Commands run during development, with the results observed at the time (not re-run for this description):

- `bun test tests/spawn-guard.test.ts --timeout 120000`: 3 pass
- `bun test tests/flow.test.ts --timeout 120000`: 15 pass
- `bun test tests/review-run.test.ts tests/review-lean.test.ts --timeout 120000`: 37 pass
- `bun test tests/test-files.test.ts --timeout 120000`: 7 pass
- `bun run bundle`: source test files 49 passed, 0 failed
- `bun run build:check`: passed

No hosted CI result was captured for this head. The Windows hang is intermittent, so a green run would be suggestive, not proof.

## Notes

This description was drafted inline by the same agent that made the change, and self-reviewed rather than independently reviewed.

`tracetoon query` (`--run`, `--cypher` with `--params`, `--all` to lift the 60-row cap per section) asks named questions (outline, why, unverified, unexplained, stale, dead-ends, turn, pushback, schema) or read-only Cypher, and prints TOON. The graph is now an index: `why` lists the target's hunks, marking those no captured edit explains, plus commit message bodies.

**Skill instructions.** Per commit db53f4f, Terra candidate drafts dropped a commit-body motivation in 12 of 12 judgments, and the graph step lived in the delegated drafter's instructions and `role-packets.json`, so Sonnet drafting inline skipped it. The instructions now apply to whoever drafts, say to read the behavior hunks and expand commits with message bodies, and tell reviewers to treat graph leads as places to look, not findings. The graph schema lives in `src/graph/model.ts` (`tracetoon query schema`).

The diff also contains a vendored wasm binary and generated files (the vendored engine glue, the rebuilt bundle), which have no reviewable hand-written lines.

Per the approved plan to "give the graph arm its budget, delivered as a graph", this PR changes how the evidence is laid out for the writer: round 1 of the shape test showed the graph arm giving too little evidence and flattening it into tables that cite each other by id. Receipts joined argv with spaces, so `bash -c 'bun run typecheck && ...'` read as a different command. title: feat(review): run all review passes and merge their findings
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Applying reviewer findings was run by the Tracetoon runner as one review pass per lens, with an edit and recheck after each. This PR adds one command that runs every planned pass and returns a single merged list, so the drafter edits once and rechecks become optional.

## What changed

- `tracetoon review run --all` runs one pass per lens, plus any general passes beyond the lens count, concurrently. Each pass has its own packet, reply, findings and reviewed-body files and is imported the way a single run is. If some passes fail, the ones that succeeded are imported, the failed passes and the rerun command are named, and the command exits non-zero. On rerun, passes Tracetoon already ran and imported for the same body on the same verified model are skipped (`--fresh` reruns them). `--all --recheck` resumes passes Tracetoon ran earlier (with `contested`, only those with rejected findings), and `--note` passes rejections along.
- `tracetoon review merge` builds the same merged list from already-imported passes, for the agent runner.
- The merged list is written to `review-findings-merged.md`. Findings are deduplicated by normalized and near-duplicate quote (omissions by evidence), the strongest verdict is kept, ordering is by verdict strength then number of passes that raised it, each line names its passes, and the list is capped at 12. Claims whose quote is no longer in the body are dropped (`src/contribution/mergeFindings.ts`).
- A new `Review recheck: once|contested|none` SKILL line, with `prepare --review-recheck`, is stored in `review-plan.json` when it isn't `once`. Prepare, render and the review next steps follow it. The publish gate never needs a recheck.
- A single `review run` without `--lens` now also works when the plan asks for general passes beyond the lenses.
- The SKILL's step 2b is rewritten around one review command (or merge), one edit pass, and a recheck only as the setting says, replacing the old per-reviewer recheck text.

## Tests

Added `tests/merge-findings.test.ts`, and extended `tests/review-run.test.ts`, `tests/skill-settings.test.ts` and the fake Codex reviewer. I did not run the test suite fresh while preparing this PR. The development session logs show `bun test` runs on the review-run, merge-findings and skill-settings tests passing, but they don't establish results for this exact commit. title: Add `tracetoon update` to upgrade an installed Tracetoon in place
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Until now the only way to update Tracetoon was to re-run the installer. This adds a `tracetoon update` command that upgrades an installed copy in place (motivated by the user noticing there was no update command in the CLI).

## What it does

- Looks up the published releases and picks a target. `--channel latest` (default) includes release candidates; `--channel stable` ignores them; `--to <version>` installs a specific release and is also the rollback path.
- `--check` only reports; with `--exit-code` it exits 10 when a newer release exists.
- Downloads the release's `checksums.txt`, the skill zip and this platform's binary, and verifies SHA-256 for each before anything is replaced. It also checks that the skill version matches the release and that the skill's `build.json` build ID equals the downloaded runtime's `build-info`, so a new install pairs a skill and runtime from the same build (checked at update time, before anything is replaced).
- Replaces the binary, comic assets and every installed skill copy, then re-registers hooks (reporting if that step could not be done). If a step fails before the old copies are discarded, the previous files are restored (best effort); a failed hook registration is reported rather than rolled back.
- Refuses to replace a plugin/bundle copy, a binary chosen through an environment override, or a non-installed binary (update the plugin route with `/plugin marketplace update`). Setting the disable-updates variable to 1 blocks the command (named in the README).
- "Latest" is chosen by publish time (version breaks ties); updating to the version already installed is a no-op, even with `--to`.
- A semver comparator orders `rc.2` before `rc.10`. A plain update never goes backwards; only an explicit `--to` can.
- `install.sh` and `install.ps1` now record an `install.json` receipt, and an update-URL environment variable points lookups and downloads at a test server.
- README documents the command; the bundled `dist/tracetoon.mjs` and `build.json` are regenerated.

Code is in `src/commands/update.ts` and `src/update/{apply,layout,release,version}.ts`, wired up in `src/cli.ts`.

## Testing

New `tests/update.test.ts`. In the development session, `bun test tests/update.test.ts` passed (12 pass, 0 fail) and `bun run test` passed (50 source test files), but both ran before later edits, so they do not establish results for the final commit. I did not re-run them for this description, and hosted CI status is unknown.

## Notes

After updating, reload your agent host; Codex may require trusting the new hook entries in `/hooks`.

title: Recognise the VEX AIM's user serial port
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Problem

`types_by_location()` only knew the V5 Brain layout (USB interface 0 = system, 2 = user). The AIM (PID `0x0700`) is a composite device with a UVC camera on interfaces 2 and 3, so its serial ports are interfaces 0 and 4. Interface 4 hit the "Unknown location" branch and was dropped, so `find_devices()` returned an AIM with `user_port() == None`, and `read_user()`/`write_user()` silently used the system-port fallback.

## Changes (`packages/vex-v5-serial/src/serial.rs`)

- Treat interface 4 on the AIM as the user port (`AIM_USER_INTERFACE`). The Brain interface mapping (0 = system, 2 = user) is unchanged.
- `types_by_location()` now returns `None` when it recognised no ports (it used to return `Some(vec![])`), so the name-based fallbacks in `find_ports()` can run. This applies to every device type: when no VEX ports are recognised by location (including none connected) and the fallback can't infer types, `find_ports()`/`find_devices()` now return `CouldntInferTypes` instead of an empty list.
- `write_user()` used a single `write()` on the user port, which may accept only part of the buffer, yet reported that count and never flushed. It now uses `write_all()` + `flush()` and returns the full length, as the system-port path already does.
- Added unit tests: AIM interfaces 0/4 map to system/user, Brain interfaces 0/2 still work, and unrecognised ports yield `None`. The tests account for macOS reporting the CDC data interface (communication + 1).

## Testing

Unit tests were added. Not tested against physical AIM hardware.

## Notes

The description was drafted inline by the coordinating agent without a separate drafter or reviewer, and no comic was included.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What

Adds `vexaim snap`, which saves one frame from the AIM robot's camera as a JPEG, and a hint when `exec` output looks truncated. Also adds a release binary, an API reference, a CI build workflow and an upstream setup script.

- **`vexaim snap [-o FILE]`** (`crates/vexaim-cli/src/snap.rs`, `main.rs`): finds cameras whose name contains "AIM" (the robot shows up as a USB webcam) and requests 640x480 MJPEG at 30 fps via `nokhwa`. It tries each matching video node, since the AIM exposes two and only one streams. It discards the first 7 of 8 frames so auto-exposure can settle, strips the driver's zero padding, and writes the JPEG. The default name is `vexaim-snap-<unix-time>.jpg`. `--json` prints path, width, height and bytes. The no-AIM-camera error lists the cameras found. If the camera delivers a non-MJPEG format, the command fails rather than converting.
- **Truncation hint** (`main.rs`): when `exec` times out with at least 1500 bytes of stdout, the output gets a hint that the robot's USB buffer overflows above ~2 KB per burst. The JSON output gains `possible_output_truncation`.
- **`scripts/setup-upstream.sh`**: clones `vexide/vex-v5-serial`, checks out the pinned commit and applies the AIM user-port patch from `patches/`.
- **`.github/workflows/build.yml`**: builds and tests the CLI on Linux, Windows and macOS (arm64 and x86_64), then uploads each binary with a `SHA256SUMS` file. The file is marked untested on CI.

  - Replug behaviour is documented: with the udev rule installed, the robot works again within ~2 s of a stable replug (20/20 recoveries on Linux).

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The user was at the robot running unplug/replug tests and asked to "Retry the kicker test"; the goal was that the kicker moved.

**Behavior.** `is_disconnect` in `repl.rs` matches IO errors containing "broken pipe", "no such device" or "input/output error"; when one matches, the failure message says the robot disconnected during the command (USB unplugged or robot powered off). The message also warns that a movement command may or may not have run, so the robot should be checked before re-running. `devices()` now maps the library's `CouldntInferTypes` error to an empty list, so an unplugged robot reports no device rather than a serial I/O error. title: Search for tags with stationary views; add opt-in contact verification
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Adds three behavior changes to the shared behavior controller (`behaviors.py`) and bumps the release to 0.5.1.

The author asked for the robot's working blue-barrel-to-purple-tag run to be wrapped for kids, with quick, assume-it-works behavior instead of the camera checks and stop-and-think steps used in testing. The commit message does not describe a separate bug report beyond that.

**Stationary tag search.** Before, `find` on a tag used the same continuous 360-degree sweep as cargo. The hardware notes in this PR record that this sweep missed Tag 0 after 360.3 degrees, while stationary views found it. Now a tag target runs `find_tag`: up to eight views 45 degrees apart. Each view stops, waits 300 ms and reads three times 100 ms apart, then turns 45 degrees at `tag_turn_dps` (new option, default `turn_dps`). The 20 s limit is checked only between views, so a search can slightly overrun it; after the eighth view a missing tag raises `not_found`. `reacquire` also waits 300 ms before reading a tag. Cargo search is unchanged. `approach` and `deliver` reach the new search through `find`, and the named macros set `tag_turn_dps` to their `turn_dps`.

**Opt-in `verification="contact"`.** `configure` now validates `verification` (`"vision"` or `"contact"`, else `ValueError`) and caps `tag_turn_dps` at 150, both covered by tests. The default stays `"vision"`, which keeps the existing possession, retention and release checks, with the side effects listed under the default-mode note below. With `"contact"`:
- `collect` finishes one bounded contact stroke and continues, with no retention reverse, repeat contact or repeated native possession-sensor votes (`confirm`). No host camera images are involved in either mode. The guard that rejects a different held cargo still uses `confirm`. A stroke that stops at its time limit against a wall counts as an attempt rather than raising.
- `deliver` accepts cargo from the preceding `collect` in the same activity, skips the possession-loss gate, and does not require release confirmation.
- In contact mode, results carry `completed: true`, and `collected` / `delivered` are `True` only with native evidence and `None` when assumed (`evidence: contact_assumed` / `place_assumed`). A standalone `deliver` with no preceding `collect` and no native possession still raises `cargo_required`. Missing targets and the shared deadline still fail.

Example, traced through `collect` then `deliver` with the detector reporting no possession: `collect` returns `collected: None, completed: True, evidence: contact_assumed`. `deliver` places and backs away, then returns `delivered: None, completed: True, evidence: place_assumed`.

**Motion floor.** Every `motion` call, in both modes, now waits at least 1.5 s before reporting a stall. It still returns as soon as the robot reports stopped.

**Default-mode side effects.** Vision mode is not byte-for-byte unchanged: `deliver` now always includes `completed: true` and the `delivered` event gains an `evidence` field. `collect` also returns `completed: true` when the requested cargo is already held; the vision capture path does not add it. The 1.5 s floor above applies too.

**Evidence.** The diff adds simulation tests in `dev/test_behaviors.py` for stationary tag search in both directions, a bounded search with no tag, held cargo missing from the detector, a contact-limit stroke, missing target or cargo, the shared deadline, and the short-move margin. No test result for this revision was captured, and none is claimed here. Earlier in the development session, `python -m unittest discover -s dev -p test_behaviors.py` passed before later edits; the tested content was not verified. `docs/hardware-notes.md` records the earlier hardware run and a later source check. That check did not reacquire the blue barrel and is not full 0.5.1 hardware acceptance. Per AGENTS.md, CI does not verify real hardware. No result is recorded here for hosted CI or the installer tests.

**Consequences.** `"contact"` mode can report completion when the barrel was never attached or released, so callers must read `collected` / `delivered` rather than assume them. `docs/release-notes.md` also says the workshop installer requires 0.5.1 and that workshop instructions warm helpers, but this diff changes no installer or workshop files, so those statements are not backed by this PR. The skill docs now show `verification="contact"` in the example.

**Review path.** Start with `behaviors.py` (`contact`, `finish_contact`, `collect`, `deliver`, then `find_tag`), then the new tests in `dev/test_behaviors.py`. The docs, skill and version files are the rest.

title: Use SDL FreeRDP client for full desktop mode on Wayland
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

When the session is Wayland (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`) and WinApps is launched in full desktop mode (`windows`), `waGetFreeRDPCommand` now looks for an SDL-based FreeRDP client before falling back to `xfreerdp`. It tries, in order: `sdl-freerdp3`, `sdl3-freerdp`, `sdl-freerdp`, then the `com.freerdp.FreeRDP` Flatpak (run as `sdl-freerdp`, setting `RDP_FLATPAK=1`).

RemoteApp/app launches, and any user-set `FREERDP_COMMAND`, are unchanged and keep the existing `xfreerdp` detection. If no SDL client is found, detection continues as before.

## Details

- `waGetFreeRDPCommand` takes the launch mode as `$1`; the call site passes `"$1"`.
- The final validity check also accepts the new `flatpak run --command=sdl-freerdp com.freerdp.FreeRDP` command.
- The `xfreerdp` branch is now guarded by `[ -z "$FREERDP_COMMAND" ]` so it doesn't override an SDL match.

## Testing

Not run: no Wayland session or FreeRDP install was available here, and I ran no automated checks. The change is a small shell edit to `bin/winapps`.

Claude Code's hook shell on Windows can't find a bare `aifirst`, so the integration needs to stop depending on the parent process's `PATH`.

- Existing installs migrate on the next `skill install`: the legacy hook and legacy bare-command permissions are recognised and replaced, and `revokePermissions` also clears both legacy and launcher-form allow entries; unrelated allow entries are kept.
- The launcher records the executable path at install time, so a moved binary needs `skill install` rerun; the command still starts with `bash` resolved from `PATH`.

title: macOS installer: defer setup to a direct 'aifirst init'
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Problem

A macOS user reported that after the piped installer (`curl … | bash`) they could not type at the "Set up 2 tools? [Y/n]" prompt. The installer ran `aifirst init </dev/tty`, and on macOS the Bun-compiled binary can't poll stdin reopened through the `/dev/tty` alias (oven-sh/bun#41495). The reporter said running the installed command directly worked; the likely reason is that it inherits the real tty device.

## Change

- `install/install.sh`: on macOS (`$OS = darwin`) the installer no longer launches setup. It prints "On macOS, finish setup in a new terminal:" followed by `aifirst init`. Linux keeps the `/dev/tty` path, and `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP=1` still skips setup.
- `README.md`: says macOS users run `aifirst init` after install, as a temporary step, and scopes the "opens guided setup immediately" wording to Linux and Windows.
- `install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh` and `install/fixtures/macos_installer_tty_driver.py`: a macOS regression test. It runs the real install flow against a fake `curl` that serves the built binary, then checks that a direct `aifirst init` in a pty accepts input.
- CI runs that test on macOS in `ci.yml`, and the release smoke job in `release.yml` runs it against the darwin binary. `shellcheck` now also covers the new script.

This is a workaround. It should be removed once a Bun release fixes the underlying bug.

## Testing

I did not run the macOS test in this Linux environment, so it is unverified here. It runs only in macOS CI and the release smoke job. The test script exits with an error on non-Darwin systems.

title: Let any key skip typed-out prompts and plans in the learner TUI
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The learner TUI was slow to read through long exercise prompts and plans, and one exercise printed an image as garbled terminal characters. This PR makes the typed-out text skippable and keeps the UI responsive while exercises run. It also bumps the package version to 0.13.4.

## Why

The request (S1) was to finish a long prompt instantly on a click or keypress, make plans skippable the same way, and fix the garbled image output. The same request also asked for program output to stay inside the TUI, for the transcript to return to the bottom after a menu click, and for a compact plan picker. The rest of the change follows from those.

## What changed

- **Skippable animation** (`src/learn/terminalRenderer.ts`, `src/tui/session.ts`): in `renderExercisePrompt`, any key other than Esc or Ctrl+C now stops the per-character delay and prints the rest at once. Esc still goes back and Ctrl+C still exits. For markdown containing a `## Proposed plan` heading, `renderTerminalMarkdown` uses one skip controller for the whole document, and any key skips it. Other blocks still skip only on Space or Enter. In the TUI session, a mouse click or a key reveals prompts and plans, and the footer hints say so.
- **Binary reads in replays** (`src/replay/executor.ts`): a replayed `read` of a PNG now shows a one-line summary with its dimensions and byte size. Other files that aren't valid UTF-8, or that contain a NUL byte, show a type and size line. Neither dumps raw bytes into the terminal.
- **Async child processes** (new `src/process.ts`, `src/commands/run.ts`, `src/replay/executor.ts`): `runAsyncProcess` streams stdout and stderr through callbacks. It supports a timeout, an abort signal, and an interactive stdin handle. When the child is spawned detached (POSIX, with a signal or timeout), it kills the whole process group, using SIGTERM and then SIGKILL after 1s. Otherwise it kills the single process, and on Windows it uses `taskkill`. The exercise logic in `run.ts` moved into `executePreparedExercise`, which takes an input mode (`authored-sample` or `reader`). The final interactive command of a reader-input run has no timeout; earlier compile commands keep theirs. Timeouts now report exit code 124, and a timed-out or aborted command stops the compile/run sequence. In the async replay path (`executeReplayOperationAsync`), commands that aren't shell scripts now run through the same helper, and graphical commands are skipped on Linux (reported as exit 0) when no `DISPLAY` or `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set.
- **`aifirst run`**: interactive TTY runs in text mode stream output live, and a run with no output prints "Program completed with no console output."
- **TUI session and learner** (`src/tui/session.ts`, `src/learn/native.ts`): the transcript follows the latest output. A program-output panel streams stdout and stderr and has an input field for interactive programs. Esc or Ctrl+C stops a running verification command. The choice and plan picker uses a compact layout (`tuiChoiceLayout`) and scrolls its details with PgUp/PgDn. Ctrl+D sends EOF to a running program, and input typed before the process is ready is queued. `native.ts` now runs exercises in-process through `prepareExerciseFiles` and `executePreparedExercise`. It no longer spawns a nested `aifirst run --format json` process or parses its failure output.
- **Tests**: new driver fixtures and tests for skipping, scroll-follow, interactive programs, plan streaming, replay flow, and graphical runs. Process-group kill, SIGKILL escalation, abort via signal, and Windows `taskkill` have no dedicated tests.

## Validation

I did not run `bun test` or `bun run typecheck` while preparing this PR, and I'm not claiming any check results here.

## Review notes

- `src/process.ts` kills detached process groups; worth a look at the `detached` default (set only when a signal or timeout is given on non-Windows).
- `src/tui/session.ts` is the largest source change.
- `src/learn/native.ts` is a behavior change (in-process execution), not just a cleanup.

title: Keep terminal programs and prompt reveal responsive in the learner TUI
body:

The goal is to keep terminal programs inside the TUI with live output and, when a step needs it, an embedded input field, to let an ordinary keypress reveal the rest of a prompt or plan, and to stop synchronous process execution from freezing rendering on long-running commands such as PocketCFO.

Previously the program output in `src/learn/native.ts` was read from `parsed?.ran?.stdout`; it now comes from the executed result (`executed.stdout`).

- **Prompt and plan pacing:** while an exercise prompt types out, a keypress sets `skipped` and reveals it fully; for a `## Proposed plan` document the controller's `anyKey` makes any ordinary key reveal it. In the TUI a mouse click on the prompt or plan panel also reveals it. A revealing key does not also run the prompt.
- **TUI session:** the session follows the latest output after a prompt returns `run` and after a picker selection with a value; PageUp/PageDown scroll the detail panel when `detailScroll` is set; Ctrl+D is handled in interactive mode; detailed pickers are laid out compactly with a scrollable detail panel.
- **Program execution:** `runAsyncProcess` in `src/process.ts` runs a child without blocking the renderer; when `stdin` is `interactive` it hands the caller an input writer through `onInputReady`, a string or bytes value is supplied as the program's input, and a `win32` branch is added. In `src/commands/run.ts`, `executePreparedExercise` runs the steps and breaks on a non-zero exit, timeout or abort; `executionTimeoutMs` is extracted and `runTimeoutMs` calls it.
- **Replay executor:** async replay handles `<python>` commands; on Linux without `DISPLAY` or `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` a graphical operation is not launched and returns exit code 0 with "Skipped graphical launch because no display is available."; `replayReadText` describes a binary file such as a PNG by type instead of its bytes.
- Esc or Ctrl+C while a verification command runs from the TUI aborts it.

title: fix: make Python replays portable across platforms
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Python chapter replays recorded shell commands as `bash -lc ...` with a literal `python3`, which assumes a POSIX shell. This adds a `portableCommand` form and sanitized `display` metadata to those commands, and teaches the validator to require `portableCommand` for Python steps.

## Changes

- **Schema and types** (`schema/content.schema.json`, `src/types.ts`): new optional `display` (`toolName`, `description`, `command`) on write, edit, read, command operations and status events. Command operations also gain `portableCommand`, `timeoutMs` and `expectedTimeout`.
- **Importer** (`scripts/lib/import-showtail.ts`): when a step's source paths include a `.py` file, command operations get `portableCommand` of `["<shell>", <command>]`, with `python3` before `--version`, `-c`, `-m` or a `*.py` script replaced by `<python>`. `display` (tool name, description, command) is filled from the tool event on those commands only; the schema allows `display` on other operations and status events but the importer does not write it there.
- **Validator** (`scripts/validate.ts`): for `python` steps, a `bash` command that mentions `python`/`python3`, `rm`, `timeout`, `ls` or a `VAR=` assignment must have `portableCommand[0] === "<shell>"`. The check also applies to pre-plan events, workflow interludes and variants. The importer gates on a `.py` source path while the validator gates on `step.language === "python"`. It also rejects an empty `portableCommand`, and `expectedTimeout` without `timeoutMs`.
- **Content**: `books/ai-first-python-programming.json` updated with `portableCommand` and `display` (no `timeoutMs`/`expectedTimeout` are written; those are schema and validator support only); four showtail fixtures updated to match.
- **Tests**: new Python chapters 9-10 audit check, a showtail import assertion, and a small update to the privacy-equivalence test.
- Bumps `@aifirst/content` to 1.7.2.

## Testing

I did not run any tests while preparing this PR, and no hosted CI status was checked. Earlier development-session runs of `bun test` on the graphical-run, tui-learn, planning and windows-duckling-replay tests are in the session logs, but they predate later edits, so they say nothing about this exact content.

## Notes

The consumers that interpret `<shell>` and `<python>` are outside this repo and are not covered here. The title and description were drafted and self-reviewed inline by the coordinating agent, without separate drafter and reviewer agents.

title: Fix stale desktop portal after exiting Gaming Mode
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Problem

After returning from Gaming Mode to Plasma, Flatpak apps such as Deskflow could fail because the portal appeared to lack its KDE backend (the session log showed `No such interface "org.freedesktop.portal.FileChooser"`). Gamescope and Plasma can share the same user systemd manager, so the portal broker started in the Gamescope session survives into the desktop session.

## Change

- `scripts/gamescope-clear-autologin.conf`: adds `ExecStopPost=-/usr/bin/systemctl --user stop xdg-desktop-portal.service` to the Gamescope session template drop-in. It runs before the final autologin clear, so Plasma activates a fresh portal with the KDE environment. The `-` prefix makes it best-effort, so a closing user bus doesn't mark the Gamescope unit failed; the autologin clear still reports failures.
- `tests/test-units.sh` (new): checks there are two teardown hooks, the portal stop comes first and is best-effort, the autologin clear is not, and `systemd-analyze` accepts the drop-in (skipped if the tool or the base unit is unavailable). `tests/test-ensure.sh` gets shellcheck annotation cleanups, an `export` on `WAYLAND_SESSION_DIR`, and the executable bit.
- `README.md`: documents the hook, says to re-run the installer on existing installs, and adds troubleshooting to detect a stale portal and recover with `systemctl --user restart plasma-xdg-desktop-portal-kde.service xdg-desktop-portal.service`.

## Testing

Before opening this PR I ran `./tests/test-ensure.sh` and `./tests/test-units.sh` in the checkout; no failures were reported (no receipts recorded). The author reported doing a full Gaming Mode cycle with the change in place and Deskflow came back up fine; they also had an unrelated-looking display glitch on one monitor that needed a replug. I did not independently exercise a Gaming Mode → Plasma switch.

Start review at the drop-in; it is a one-line behavioral change (the rest of that diff is comments).

title: Commands quoted in scripts and heredocs no longer count as test runs
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Command lines were split on `;`, `|`, `&&`, `||` and newlines even inside quotes and heredoc bodies. A line inside an inline script (`python -c "..."`, `cat <<'EOF' ... EOF`) that mentioned `bun test` therefore counted as a test run, and its grouping key came out as `bun test',` (per the commit message, which also says this is a known gap noted in PR #8).

## What changes

- New `splitCommands` in `src/util/shell.ts` splits a command line into the commands it runs, leaving quoted strings (`"`, `'`, backtick, with backslash escapes outside single quotes) alone and skipping heredoc bodies (`<<EOF`, `<<-EOF`, quoted or bare delimiters). Splitting resumes after the terminator, so `cat > a <<'EOF' ... EOF` followed by `bun test x` still finds the real test run. A heredoc with no terminator swallows the rest of the command. Limits: `<<<` here-strings are not handled specially (the splitter can mistake `<<<word` for a heredoc), and `<<-`, backticks and unterminated heredocs have no dedicated tests.
- `testSegment` and `commandKey` in `src/digest/build.ts`, and `makesCommit` in `src/correlate/correlate.ts`, now use it instead of their own regex splits.
- `commandKey` also drops redirection and heredoc tokens (`<`, `>`, `2>`) when picking the first two tokens, so ``cd repo && python - <<'PY'`` groups as `python`.
- Version bumped to 1.0.0-rc.12 (`package.json`, `plugin.json`, `VERSION`, `src/version.ts`), and the bundled `dist/tracetoon.mjs` is rebuilt.

Where to start: `splitCommands` in `src/util/shell.ts`.

## Tests

`tests/shell.test.ts` covers chains and pipes, quoted separators and escapes, heredoc bodies (and what follows them), `isTestCommand` on quoted/heredoc scripts, `testSegment` with a redirected `bun test`, and `commandKey` with a heredoc.

The user wanted to "see if summaries are being generated properly with tracetoon first" before improving the comic. This PR adds an evaluation harness for the summaries, fixes digest problems in how sessions are matched to a PR, and shows the digest's facts beside the description so claims can be checked.

**Digest fixes** (mostly `src/correlate/correlate.ts`):
- Previously the window ended `last + 30 * 60_000` (or now, when the tree was dirty); it now ends `last + 5 * 60_000`.
- Work already in the base branch is left out when a session command shows a base commit: the cutoff is the last time the session committed something the base already has (a base SHA appearing in command output also counts). Turns whose last edit is before the cutoff are dropped, and a turn that crosses it keeps its conversation; only the 200 newest base commits are searched.
- Files under .git (Tracetoon's own run files) are not repo edits; binary files count as changed; work after the last commit belongs to the next PR, with up to 5 minutes of slack for clock differences.
- In `src/digest/build.ts`, `sessionDigest` now calls the extracted `testOutputFailed`, so failures are read from output and piped runs (`bun test | tail`) count; labels come from the test runner, not the first command. `tests/summary-fixes.test.ts` covers piped results, chained-command labels, binary diffs, rejection feedback and earlier work.
- Quiet commits (`git commit -q`) are recognized by their subject, and `prTruth` can describe a given head instead of the checkout.

title: Fix digest attribution leaks and print clickable preview links
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Three fixes to Tracetoon's digest and preview output, found while dogfooding it on its own PRs.

- **`cd`-prefixed commands.** Agents log a command with the shell's directory from *before* it ran, so `cd ../other-repo && bun test` was filed under this repo and its test failures appeared in the PR story. A new `leadingCd` helper (`src/trace/pathMatch.ts`) resolves a leading `cd`/`pushd`/`Set-Location`, and `belongs()` in `src/correlate/correlate.ts` judges the command by that directory (or keeps it if the command mentions a repo root).
- **Earlier work and viewed commits.** Previously a turn's end was judged by every edit, so editing a file outside the repo (a report, notes) after the last base commit kept a whole earlier turn, and its prompts, in the PR. Now only edits in the repo set that end (a turn with no in-repo edit still falls back to all its records). Separately, a commit SHA in any command's output counted as the session having made it, so `git log` in another repo claimed authorship. Now a SHA in output counts only when the command (or one part of an `&&`/`||`/`;`/pipe/newline chain) is a commit-making git command: commit, merge, cherry-pick, revert, am, rebase or pull. The match on a commit's subject is unchanged.
- **Preview links.** `render` and `preview` printed a bare path that a user reported in Codex as not very helpful. They now print an absolute `file:///` URL (`Preview (Ctrl+click to open): ...`), `preview` shows the comic image the same way, and `--json` adds `previewUrl`.

Also bumps to 1.0.0-rc.8, rebuilds the bundled `dist/tracetoon.mjs`, and pins two eval-harness cases to fixed commits (PR #1's merge parents, and the commit that later captured the vexaim-cli work).

Motivation for each fix is taken from the commit messages (written by the agent session); the preview-link change followed a user report that the Codex preview link wasn't followable.

## Where to start

`belongs()` and `commitMoments()` in `src/correlate/correlate.ts`, then `leadingCd` in `src/trace/pathMatch.ts`. `plugin/skills/tracetoon/SKILL.md` now also tells agents to show the preview link verbatim on its own line. `leadingCd` also handles `sl`, `-Path`, `~` and Git Bash `/c/x` paths (the last tested on Windows only); `belongs()`'s cd branch has no direct test. Known limit: only a *leading* `cd` is recognised; a `cd` later in a chain is not.

## Testing

New tests: `tests/units.test.ts` (commit detection, `leadingCd`), `tests/summary-fixes.test.ts` (outside-repo edit doesn't extend an earlier turn), `tests/flow.test.ts` (`previewUrl` and the printed link).

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What

`tracetoon comic art` can now draw a comic with an AI image model once the user has approved a route, and otherwise uses the built-in artist. The task prompt was to implement AI-generated cartoons in Tracetoon.

## Changes

- **New routes.** The Codex CLI (its built-in image tool, via the user's Codex login) and the Antigravity CLI (experimental) need no API key. Prompts go on stdin or in a file, never on the command line. The OpenAI (`gpt-image-2.5-flare`) and Gemini (`gemini-nano-banana-2.1`, Interactions API) providers move to current models and request formats.
- **Consent and fallback.** Consent is still asked once per provider, now saying where prompts go. If a provider fails partway, the built-in artist draws the panels not yet drawn and a warning says so (an unknown or unavailable provider is an error). Antigravity runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and Codex in a read-only sandbox. Auto-selection order is now openai, gemini, codex, antigravity (was gemini, then openai). `doctor` lists the routes and which are approved; its JSON `imageProviders` changes from an object of booleans to an array of objects.
- **Character sheets.** Each cast member in the comic without an existing sheet gets a reference portrait, attached to panels (all sheets for Codex/Antigravity, the panel's own characters for the API routes), uploaded to the assets branch on publish and recorded in the series bible so later episodes reuse it. Prompts name each character's species so humans stay human.
- **Codex image matching** (second commit). Codex can redraw an image, so its session folder may hold more images than prompts, in any order. The final Codex reply names the chosen file per prompt and is now used (only files from the session's own folder); file times are a fallback only when the counts match exactly. The commit message says it was found in a live run.
- Smaller behavior changes: the built-in artist deletes an existing `panel-N` image when it draws that panel; `comic prompts` now also emits character-sheet prompts; the pets style text now says "characters" instead of "animals"; `TRACETOON_CODEX_BIN`/`TRACETOON_AGY_BIN` override the binaries. Known gap: the API routes no longer anchor later panels to an already-existing panel 1 (they still use the first panel drawn in the same run).
- Docs (README, SKILL.md, comic guide), version bump to 1.0.0-rc.9, and the rebuilt bundle.

Added tests in `tests/comic.test.ts` and `tests/units.test.ts`, plus a fake Codex (`tests/fake-codex.ts`). ## What changed

Three changes to the harness, one per commit:

1. **Lean reviewed path for the adoption gate and admission.** A candidate is now accepted either by the existing three-role rule or by a current v2 review whose recorded passes meet the run's review plan: pass count from distinct reviewer agent ids, the planned lenses, the planned reviewer model and effort, and tool-run verified passes when the plan asks for them. `meta.workflow` now records `reviewPlan` and `reviewPasses` (from Tracetoon's `review-plan.json` and `review.json`), and workflow gaps name each failed requirement.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What changed

`prbench compare` always ran all three writer systems (native, baseline, candidate) and judged the candidate against both baseline and native. This adds a way to run fewer, and adds a composite delta to the accuracy report.

- **`--systems <list>`** (comma-separated `native`, `baseline`, `candidate`; full Tracetoon names and the provider's native name also accepted). Default is all three. Baseline and candidate are required; omitting `native` is allowed and runs no native writers, so only candidate vs baseline is judged (both orders). An unknown name or a missing baseline/candidate throws. The selection logic is in `src/run/provider.ts` (`selectSystems`, `manifestSystems`, `judgedAgainst`).

- A subset is recorded in manifest settings (and so in the experiment identity). Runs with all three systems omit the field, so their identity is unchanged. Resuming without `--systems` keeps the frozen systems; resuming with a different `--systems` fails the inputs-changed check.
- **Accuracy view** (`src/report/score.ts`): the candidate-vs-baseline table gains a `Composite Δ [95% CI]` column, using the same case-clustered bootstrap over per-case means as the existing error-rate delta.

Added cases in `tests/comparison.test.ts` and `tests/score.test.ts`.

title: Add crossjudge: judge drafts from one compare run against another
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What

Adds `prbench crossjudge --candidate <dir> --baseline <dir> --out <dir>`. It judges the `tracetoon-candidate` drafts of one finished `compare` run against the `tracetoon-baseline` drafts of another, for example runs that used different writer models. No writer runs; the saved artifacts are reused.

## How it works

- Both runs must be `prbench.comparison/v2` experiments with exactly one writer model. The two runs must agree on judges, replicates, split and case hashes (differences are listed in the error). The rubric version and judge contract must also match this checkout. Saved drafts are checked against their receipts, and a missing or mismatched draft fails before any judge call.
- Each pair is judged in both orders by every configured judge. The summary uses the consensus rule `compare` uses for its quality gate: a win needs every judge's two orders to agree on the same draft. It also reports per-draft composite scores and judge cost.
- Output goes to `summary.json`, `summary.md`, `pairs.json` and `crossjudge.json`. An `--out` that already holds a different cross-judge is refused; rerunning the same one reuses saved judgments. Errors exit with code 2.
- `--plan` verifies the inputs and prints the planned judge calls without calling models, and without needing a Claude login.
- `--cache` is a content-addressed stage cache. It defaults to `<parent of --out>/.prbench-cache/v2`. `--parallel` sets how many judge pairs run at once (default 4).
- `src/comparison.ts` now exports `modelRoot` so the new module can locate each run's drafts. Nothing else changes there.

## Tests

`tests/crossjudge.test.ts` is new. I did not rerun `bun run test` or `bun run typecheck` while preparing this PR, so I have no fresh result to report.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

- **Judge retries:** a timed-out or transient judge call is now retried (up to 3 attempts, with backoff) instead of invalidating the run on the first failure (the run still stops after the third failed attempt), including on resume after a persisted timeout. Codex judges report timeouts as timeouts. Failed judge attempts record which judge failed, and `score` gains a judge-reliability table (`collectJudgeFailures`) next to writer reliability. Retries stop when cancellation is requested, and a persisted `failureKind` of `"format"` no longer triggers the recovery-limit throw on its own (`src/judge/pairwise.ts`).
- **Isolation proofs for effort arms:** probes saved the bare model (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) while resume compared against the arm spec (`claude-sonnet-5-5@medium`), so every resume of an arm with an effort failed with "Saved isolation proof does not match this experiment." - **Codex usage (earlier commit on this branch):** writer tokens and estimated cost sum every thread a run spawned (main rollout plus forked subagent rollouts), counting each model response once by response id. Runs record `meta.usageScope` and `meta.subagentThreads`; `score` recomputes all-thread usage for older runs from saved traces and says what each cost covers.

title: Run prbench compare in parallel on Codex or Claude, end to end
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What changed

`prbench compare` used to run only on Codex (Sol and Terra wrote the PRs and judged them), one job at a time. This branch makes the provider selectable and runs the work concurrently.

- **`--provider codex|claude|both`.** Codex keeps Sol and Terra, and its frozen identity is unchanged. `claude` runs Claude Code on Opus and Sonnet at medium effort, with the same models judging. `both` runs two independent comparisons in `<out>/codex` and `<out>/claude`. Providers are never mixed, and a frozen experiment refuses to resume under another provider.
- **`--parallel <n>` (default 4).** Writers, judges and isolation probes run as one job graph. A judge starts as soon as the two drafts it compares exist. Results are persisted in a fixed order, so they don't depend on timing, and `--parallel 1` keeps the serial order. After a failure nothing new starts, and running jobs finish and are saved.
- **Codex login sharing.** Concurrent Codex runs share the dedicated login through a symlink instead of queuing on exclusive copies. Windows keeps the copy mode.
- **Claude support.** Writers get the frozen skill and runtime, a stripped Anthropic/Claude Code environment, no MCP or plugins, stage timings and an early stop on the result event. The isolation probe reads the startup catalogue, and judges run with a temporary home, no tools and no hooks. `prbench auth claude` stores a setup token (mode 0600).
- **`--models <ids>`.** Replaces the provider's writer models and keeps its judges, so a cheaper writer (the motivating case was Haiku and Luna as cheaper writers) is scored by the same judges. Ids must be distinct, and `--provider both` refuses the option.
- **Also in `both`.** It returns the worst child exit code and prefixes each child's output with `[provider]`. Retry waits are now abortable, and the quality gate uses the provider's native system (`claude-native` or `codex-native`).

## Fixes found while running it

- **Judge references.** Per the commit message, Claude judges invented fact IDs and cited the other draft's evidence. Each judge call now gets a schema whose reference fields are enums of the IDs that side may cite. `checkJudgment` still validates what a schema can't express.
- **Claude environment identity.** It no longer hashes `PWD`, `OLDPWD`, `INIT_CWD` or `npm_*`, so launching from another directory no longer changes the identity (the commit message says this had blocked `--reuse-from`). The Codex hash is unchanged.
- **Scope audit.** `rg --files -g '!\.agents/**'` was read as an absolute host path and rejected the draft. A backslash escaping a leading dot is now dropped. Windows paths such as `\.agents\skills\...` are still flagged.
- **Fake `gh`.** `gh pr create --help` was counted as a second, empty PR creation ("produced no PR"). Help invocations (`--help`, `-h`, `gh help`) now print help and never count as a PR.
- **Windows-recorded cases on POSIX.** The checkout is named by the last segment of the recorded path in either syntax, and Windows paths under a mapped prefix get POSIX separators. Per the commit message, on pr8 the candidate now links 92 replayed edits (13 of 24 hunks), and on pr5 it links 45 edits and all 30 hunks. Before, both linked 0.

## Testing

Historical results from development, run before later edits to files in this PR:

- An earlier `bun test` run passed with 0 failures.
- An earlier `bun run test` run passed (37 source test files, 0 failed).
- An earlier `bun test --timeout 60000 tests/claude-comparison.test.ts` run passed (15 pass, 0 fail).
- New test files: `tests/parallel-compare.test.ts` and `tests/pool.test.ts`; `tests/agentScope.test.ts` gains a case.

I did not rerun the suite for this PR. Hosted CI status is unknown, and there was no live Claude or Codex comparison against the final commit.

title: Performance gate: pass on paired priced cost per draft
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

The performance gate used to pass on writer wall time and token counts. It now passes on paired per-draft priced cost, the same cost `prbench score` reports (`prbench.performance/v3`).

## What changed

- **Rule:** the gate passes when the candidate/baseline geometric mean of paired per-draft priced cost is at most 1.000. Pairs are same model, case and replicate. Log ratios are averaged within each case, then across cases. The case-clustered 95% interval is reported but not required, so the bar is now non-regression on the point estimate (equal cost passes) rather than a demonstrated gain. The old inconclusive conditions for unrecorded tokens and missing per-model timing are gone; the `summary.md` limitation about token counts not being USD cost is replaced by a list-price, not-an-invoice note.
- **Replaced criteria:** the per-model median-time and median-token failure checks are gone. A faster but pricier candidate now fails, and a slower or token-heavier but cheaper one passes. When validation was unavailable, cost now decides.
- **Shared cost (`draftCost` in `src/report/score.ts`):** extracted from `collectDraftScores`. Reported totals are used where available. Otherwise every model is priced at its own rate, cached input at its own rate, and Codex across all threads. The comparison attaches `pricedCost` to each writer row (`src/comparison.ts`).
- **Unpriced drafts:** any paired draft without a usable priced cost makes the gate inconclusive. That covers an unknown model price, missing tokens, Codex usage from the main thread only, and nonpositive cost. Each one is listed in `unpricedDrafts` and `summary.md`, which also states the rule.
- **Information only:** the writer-time ratio is still reported via the same clustered-ratio helper. Token counts remain as per-model medians. Per-model summaries gain median cost fields. Pairs with missing timing are now kept.
- **Unchanged:** the validation-comparability rules.
- **Docs:** CHANGELOG and README are updated. Changing `src/performance.ts` changes the gate policy hash.

## Testing

Tests were added or updated in `tests/performance.test.ts` and `tests/comparison.test.ts`. No check receipts were recorded for this run, so I make no claim here about test or typecheck results.

title: Score drafts on an absolute scale and retry failed comparison writers
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Comparison runs could be invalidated by a single flaky writer, and there was no absolute view of draft quality or cost. This adds `prbench score`, per-arm effort, and retries for writers that fail in recoverable ways. It follows a planning round where accuracy plus a claim-coverage guard was chosen as the headline metric, and where the user asked to try Haiku at low effort and approved a plan to test the cheap-writer case.

**Scoring**
- New `prbench score <roots…>` command, and a Scores section in every compare summary (`src/report/score.ts`). Each draft gets coverage (claims, context, uncertainties), rubric, factual errors, unsupported claims and traps, averaged over its judgments, with a documented 0–100 composite, case-clustered bootstrap intervals and paired candidate deltas. It can be run on earlier runs' saved judgments (rubric version 6 only).
- An Accuracy section reports the share of judgments with at least one factual error per arm, error classes, and each candidate arm against each baseline arm with a 0.05 claim-coverage guard and a cost ratio.
- `src/report/prices.json` estimates USD from token counts when a run reports no cost (Codex).

**Effort as part of the arm**
- `compare --models model@effort`: writers get the bare model and that effort (default medium); saved artifacts must match the effort when one is named; a bare model accepts any saved effort. Isolation probes run at the configured effort, not the arm's, because Haiku@low misreported the skill path and stopped whole runs (per commit 552c319).

**Writer retries and reliability**
- A writer that leaves no draft (`no-draft`, previously "produced no PR"), whose draft the scope audit rejects, or that times out is retried up to 3 attempts. Rejected drafts are never scored. Scope-rejected output is cached only after the audit passes, so a retry doesn't hit the immutable cache entry.
- A writer reliability table in score and compare summaries counts no-draft, scope-rejected and timed-out attempts per arm.
- Fake `gh` supports `--fill`, `--fill-first` and `--fill-verbose`, taking title and body from the branch's commits; explicit `--title`/`--body` win.

**Testing**
During development, `bun test` passed (240 pass, 0 fail) and targeted suites for score, comparison, arm, sandbox and graph passed. I did not re-run them while preparing this PR, and hosted CI status is unknown. New tests cover scoring (`tests/score.test.ts`), effort arms, and the scope-rejected retry end to end (the fake Codex writer types one mangled out-of-sandbox path). body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The commit message says a Claude comparison could not resume from a new shell: the environment hash covered inherited variables such as per-process ones like `CLAUDE_PID` and `INVOCATION_ID`.

The same variables also reached writers, and `CLAUDE_EFFORT` from the host session could change a writer's effort.

**What changed**

- `sandbox.ts` exports a `VOLATILE_ENV` list of 18 names (including `INVOCATION_ID`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `GPG_TTY`, `SHLVL`, `OLDPWD` and `_`) and `VOLATILE_PREFIXES` (`KONSOLE_`, `CLAUDE_`).

- `claudeComparableEnv` in `provider.ts` also skips those names and prefixes, in addition to its existing exclusions, so environments that set them hash differently than before. Its matching is case-sensitive, while the sandbox compares upper-cased names.

title: feat: add `showtail upgrade` to update standalone installs in place
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Adds a `showtail upgrade` command so people with a standalone install can update to the latest GitHub release without re-running the installer. This came from the request to make an upgrade command so users don't have to re-run the installer.

## What it does

- Looks up the latest release for `Tingsters/Showtail` (overridable via `SHOWTAIL_REPO`) and picks the asset for the current OS and architecture (linux/darwin x64/arm64, windows x64).
- Compares versions: if already current, or newer than the latest release, it makes no changes.
- Downloads the new binary and runs it with `--version`; the install is only touched if that reports the expected version.
- Also downloads `showtail.vsix` (the release must include it) and replaces it next to the binary.
- On Linux/macOS it swaps files with backups and restores them if a step fails, then runs `setup --first-run --json` on the new binary to refresh capture integrations. If that refresh fails, text output notes that integrations will refresh on the next run (`--json` reports `integrationsRefreshed: false`).
- On Windows the running executable is locked, so a detached PowerShell helper waits for the process to exit and does the swap (with rollback); the command reports `pending`.
- It refuses to run when not launched from a binary named `showtail`/`showtail.exe`, so a Bun/source runtime is not replaced (this is a basename check only).
- `--json` emits the result object; `upgrade` is added to the commands that skip first-run bootstrap.

## Limits

- Versions must be plain `x.y.z`; a prerelease tag or current version makes the command throw.
- The download is checked only by running it with `--version`; the code does not verify a checksum or signature.
- `GITHUB_TOKEN`, when set, is sent as a Bearer token on the release API call.
- On Windows the helper's outcome is not reported back; the command only says the upgrade is pending.

## Where to look

Start with `selfUpgrade()` in `src/core/selfUpgrade.ts`; `src/commands/upgrade.ts` is the thin CLI layer. Docs are updated in the README, installation guide, CLI reference, classroom workflow and CHANGELOG.

## Testing

I did not run the test suite while preparing this description, and no check receipts were recorded; the branch adds `tests/selfUpgrade.test.ts` and a case in `tests/cli.test.ts`. The Windows helper script has not been exercised on Windows in this environment.

Note: the repo's CLAUDE.md describes landing directly on `main` without PRs; this PR was opened anyway because a PR was requested for this branch.

body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Installed copies of Showtail needed the installer re-run to update, which the request set out to avoid: "Make a showtail upgrade command to upgrade showtail from an install so users don't have to re-run the installer."

`showtail upgrade` (with `--json`, which prints the full result including its status) fetches the latest GitHub Release, maps the current platform to its asset, compares versions numerically, then downloads and replaces the installed binary and bundled extension. The release repo can be overridden with `SHOWTAIL_REPO`.

The downloaded binary is checked only by running it with `--version` and comparing the printed version; there is no checksum or signature comparison. After the swap, refreshing capture integrations is best effort: if it fails the upgrade still succeeds and the command says integrations refresh the next time Showtail runs. If placing the new files fails, the old binary and extension are restored.

When the installed version is current, no assets are downloaded; when it is newer than the latest release, nothing changes. On Windows the running executable can't be swapped, so a helper finishes the swap after the process exits and the command reports "pending"; its test checks the generated script text, not a real Windows swap.

An executable not named `showtail`/`showtail.exe` (such as a Bun runtime) is refused before any network request. If verification fails, the installed files are kept intact.

The macOS and arm64 branches in `src/core/selfUpgrade.ts` were not confirmed on those platforms.

README, installation, classroom-workflow and CLI reference docs and the CHANGELOG now point to `showtail upgrade`.

title: Prepare Windows code signing through SignPath Foundation
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

Prepares Showtail for free Windows code signing through the SignPath Foundation, as asked in the planning session (make the project properly open-source licensed and meet the Foundation's requirements). The release workflow now builds the Windows exe on Windows, submits it to SignPath, verifies the signature, and only then publishes. The signing step stays blocked until onboarding is done.

## What changed

- **Release workflow** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`): split into `validate`, `test`, `build-non-windows`, `build-sign-windows` and `publish` jobs.
  - `validate` requires a `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` tag that matches `package.json` and `src/core/version.ts` and is an ancestor of `main`.
  - `test` adds typecheck, format check and a license check on Ubuntu.
  - `build-sign-windows` fails unless `SIGNPATH_ENABLED=true`, `SIGNPATH_ORGANIZATION_ID` and `SIGNPATH_API_TOKEN` are set. It uploads the unsigned exe, submits it to SignPath, then checks the Authenticode status, signer, version metadata and `--version` output.
  - `publish` adds an SPDX SBOM, licenses and `SHA256SUMS`, and is the only job with `contents: write`.
  - Actions are pinned to commit SHAs and Bun to 1.4.0 (`.bun-version`); it was `latest` before.
- **Build scripts**: `scripts/build-windows.ps1` builds the exe with version metadata. `scripts/build-non-windows.sh` builds the Linux and macOS binaries. `scripts/build-all.sh` now covers only what a Unix host can build.
- **SignPath config**: `.signpath/artifact-configuration.xml` and `.signpath/README.md`.
- **Licensing**: `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, shipped in the package. `scripts/verify-licenses.ts` is run via `bun run license:check`.
- **Repo hygiene**: CODEOWNERS, Dependabot, CodeQL, and a dependency-review workflow gated until enabled (`.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml`). CI and the other workflows are also pinned.
- **Docs**: code signing policy, privacy, security, uninstallation and install pages, a SignPath application checklist, and a release preamble. `install.sh` and `install.ps1` gain small additions.
- **Tests**: `tests/signingReadiness.test.ts`.

## Not done / needs a human

- SignPath onboarding itself: the project, signing policy, API token and repository variables must be created before a release can be signed.
- The signing and publish path of the release workflow has not run, because it needs a tag and SignPath.

body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What changed

Two deterministic improvements to the graph evidence brief.

**Owners rows.** The TOON brief, the neighborhood tail and the lean review packet (lens A) now get an owners section. It maps clauses of the commit sentence to the one or two changed functions whose changed lines say them, so a reader sees where each behavior lives.
- Hunks now record per-function changed-line words (`fnWords`). A changed doc comment is credited to the definition below it, so a hunk that defines several functions can still tell them apart.
- Words most functions share count for less, linked hunks get a bonus, and a clear lead is required before a row is emitted.
- Rows appear only for change units where two or more functions own different sentences. There are at most 5 per unit and 6 in all, and they never print call relations.

**Direction in code cells.** Cells say `added:` / `removed:` instead of bare `+` / `-`, and `was ... -> now ...` for pairs. For a changed boolean condition, including multi-line chains, they list the operands it dropped, kept and added in place of the bare removed fragments. Value fallbacks (`a || ref`) stay as value changes. Direction words don't cost extra code-cell budget.

`plugin/skills/tracetoon/references/drafting.md` now tells drafters to read direction from code cells and name where a behavior lives from the owners rows.

Most of the code is in `src/graph/briefExtras.ts` and `src/graph/codeEvidence.ts`. `build.ts` holds the `fnWords` extraction; `searchBrief.ts` changes the code-cell budget (owners rows are excluded from it, and operand lines get a ranking boost); `queries.ts` and `review.ts` carry smaller wiring. title: Record each check in a chained shell command as its own run
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
When an agent chains checks in one shell command, such as `bun run bundle; bun x tsc --noEmit && bun test > log; bun scripts/eval-summaries.ts`, the digest listed only the test run, and that run carried every result line of the shared output. In the base code, `commandRun` used `verificationSegment`, which returns the test segment first, so the bundle, typecheck and eval runs were dropped and the eval's "57/57 checks pass" was attached to the tests. Per the commit message, agents writing PR descriptions then said checks "were not run" when they had been, and this caused most of the factual errors Opus made in a prbench comparison.

Now `commandRuns` returns one run per check in the command, in order. When there are several, each run keeps only the output lines of its own kind (test counts, `Found N errors`, `Bundled`, `N/M checks`, and so on). A non-zero exit status shared by a chain is recorded as `unknown`, since it can't be pinned on one check; a result line in a check's own output still sets its outcome as before (`runOutcome` is unchanged). A command with one check behaves as before, and several test commands still collapse into one listed run with `unknown` outcome. `commandRun` stays as a wrapper that returns the first run (which may now be a build rather than a test) and has no callers outside tests, and `sessionDigest` now records every run.

Second fix, also from the commit message: `digest.json` stored `mergeBase` cut to 12 characters, but `tracetoon source --revision base` needs the full hash and always failed with "Code evidence must use the prepared base or head revision". The digest now stores the full hash.

Tests: `tests/evidence.test.ts` covers a bundle, test and eval chain, a bundle, typecheck and test chain, and a chain that exits non-zero. `tests/preparation.test.ts` resolves `--revision base` and expects a 40-character revision.
