title: CI: stop Bun exit hangs from stalling test runs (plus merged publish work)
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Why

CI runs of the test suite kept stalling on Windows (and timing out on slower runners). The commit messages record the pattern: a CLI process or a `bun test` run printed its complete result and then did not exit, in a different test file each time (review-lean, review-run, brief-extras, brief-owners-direction, graph). Hangs ran to the 6h job limit, or a single `spawnSync` waited out its cap. The commit messages attribute this to Bun 1.3.14 on Windows failing to exit; that is their diagnosis, not something I reproduced here.

## What changed

- **CLI exits explicitly** (`src/cli.ts`): after the command finishes it flushes stdout and stderr, then calls `process.exit(process.exitCode ?? 0)` instead of relying on the event loop draining.
- **Spawn guard for tests** (`tests/spawn-guard.ts`, `tests/helpers.ts`): the CLI writes its exit code to `$TRACETOON_EXIT_FILE` just before exiting (cleared from its own environment so children don't inherit it). The guard runs a command with inherited stdio; if the file appears and the process is still alive 3s later, it kills it (`taskkill /T` on Windows) and returns the recorded code. `helpers.ts`, preloaded for every test file, mocks `node:child_process` so `spawnSync(bun, [cli.ts|tracetoon.mjs, ...])` goes through the guard. Commands that exit on their own, or never finish, keep their exit code or hang as before, now under a small wrapper process.
- **Test runner watchdog** (`scripts/test-files.ts`, `test-source.ts`, `test-packaged.ts`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`): a file is killed with its process tree after 15 minutes (`TRACETOON_TEST_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS`) and its partial output printed; once a file's summary line appears, the runner waits 20s for bun to exit, then kills it and takes the result from the summary; killed children's pipes are destroyed and unref'd; the source and packaged runners exit explicitly. The CI test job gets a 45 minute limit.
- **Bounded CLI calls in tests** (`review-run`, `review-lean`): the CLI helpers redirect stdout/stderr to files (piped `spawnSync` on Windows waits for every holder of the pipe), cap each call and name the command and partial output on timeout, treat a timed-out call with a complete JSON result as finished, and the test runner passes `--timeout 120000` (120s per test). `review-run` shortens the reviewer timeout to 60s so a hung fake codex dies after a minute.

This diff against `main` also contains earlier work merged into the branch (about 600 added lines): fork publishing and a single `--repo` target for `gh` (`src/commands/publish.ts`, `src/git/pr.ts`, `src/github/*`, `src/workflow/checks.ts`, `doctor.ts`, `digest.ts`) with their tests, plus the rebuilt `dist/tracetoon.mjs` bundle. That work is not part of the hang fix. Reviewers may prefer to read the commits from `2fe71a3` on. The global `node:child_process` mock in `tests/helpers.ts` affects every test file. `review-run.test.ts` also relaxes a pass-order assertion.

## Testing

Results below are historical session runs, against intermediate states of the branch; I did not rerun them to write this description, and I have not seen hosted CI status for the final commit.

- `bun test tests/review-run.test.ts tests/review-lean.test.ts --timeout 120000`: 37 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test tests/test-files.test.ts --timeout 120000`: 7 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test tests/spawn-guard.test.ts --timeout 120000`: 3 pass, 0 fail
- `bun test tests/flow.test.ts --timeout 120000`: 15 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run bundle`: passed, with "Source test files: 49 passed, 0 failed"

The last Windows rerun described in the commit messages passed the source suite but failed the bundled stage on a stalled `graph.test.ts` CLI call. The spawn guard is the response to that failure, and nothing in this environment confirms it on Windows.

## Where to start

`tests/spawn-guard.ts` (the 3s kill-after-exit-file logic) and the end of `src/cli.ts`.

title: Make CLI tests survive a Bun that won't exit; share one PR target
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Windows CI hangs showed up in a different test file each time, with no output until the job was cancelled. Commit messages attribute them to CLI processes that printed their result and never exited. This PR makes the CLI exit explicitly, bounds the test calls and runner against a process that still does not, and separately gives every PR step one shared target repo.

**Exit handling**
- The CLI flushes stdout and stderr, then calls `process.exit` with the command's code, instead of relying on a natural exit.
- When `$TRACETOON_EXIT_FILE` is set it writes its exit code there just before exiting, having cleared the variable from its own environment.
- `tests/spawn-guard.ts` runs a command with inherited stdio; if the exit file appears and the process is still alive 3s later, it kills it and returns the recorded code. Commands that exit themselves, or never finish, behave as before.
- `tests/helpers.ts` routes the test files' CLI spawns through that guard.
- The runner waited for each file's close event with no limit. It now kills a file after 15 minutes (its whole process tree via `taskkill /T` on Windows), prints what it had and fails it, and the CI test job has a 45 minute limit.
- Once a file's summary line appears the runner waits 20s for bun to exit, then kills it and takes the result from the summary (fail/error counts). Killed children's pipes are destroyed so they cannot keep the runner alive.
- The review CLI helpers redirect output to files, since piped spawnSync on Windows waits for every pipe holder; the per-test timeout is 120s and real hangs stay bounded by the watchdog.
- review-run's tests cap each CLI call, each CLI call has a cap (180s per the commit message), and a hung fake codex is meant to be killed after a minute instead of fifteen (per that message).
- The merged-list test no longer hard-codes pass order, which depends on which concurrent reviewer finished first.

**Shared PR target**
PR truth previously started from an existing-PR lookup by head; it now starts from the resolved target. Context, doctor and publish now share one target: gh's default repo when it is a remote of this clone (fork to upstream), else origin; a stale default matching no remote is ignored in favour of origin when origin exists. The gh calls for PRs and repo metadata (pr view/list/create/edit, repo view, title-rule and recent-comic lookups) carry `--repo`. Context records it, render stores it in the approval, and the preview prints it. Publish refuses to post if the target, re-resolved at publish time, now differs from the approved one. Doctor reports the target and tests push access against origin. Comic image hosting still pushes to origin; the private-repo check uses the target.

When origin's owner differs from the target repo's owner (a fork), `gh pr create` gets `--head owner:branch`, and the existing-PR lookup keeps PRs whose head lives in that fork. Digest and render read check receipts whenever the run has any, including runs without `task begin`. Receipt summaries read stderr before stdout, and the environment identity ignores temp-directory, terminal and display variables.

New or changed tests: `tests/spawn-guard.test.ts`, `tests/test-files.test.ts`, `tests/target.test.ts`, `tests/receipts-and-fork.test.ts` and `tests/flow.test.ts`. The recorded tests fake collaborators. The Windows reruns are described only in commit messages 9af69e8f453c and fd4c9f7b30d5. Logged CI results are for an earlier commit, not the final head. `dist/tracetoon.mjs` is regenerated. The fork fix came from publishing a PR from a fork. The goal was to settle a reported issue ("Is this issue fixed?").


**Where to start:** the exit handling in `src/cli.ts` (explicit exit and exit file), then `tests/spawn-guard.ts`.

**Feedback wanted:** is a 3s grace after the exit file appears the right trade-off between killing a slow-exiting process and masking a real hang?

title: Add a queryable evidence graph of how each PR was made
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## What changed

`digest` now also builds `evidence-graph.json`, which links the session evidence to the diff: prompts to the edits made in their turn, edits to the diff hunks their lines survive in, check runs to the PR files edited after them, and commits to the sessions that made them. If the graph can't be built, `digest` warns and continues without it. The graph runs in-process on cypherlite v0.16.1 compiled to WebAssembly. The wasm is pinned by hash in `build-dependencies.json` and rebuilt with `scripts/cypherlite.ts`, so no native modules are added.

Agents read it with the new `tracetoon query`. It offers named questions (`outline`, `why`, `unverified`, `unexplained`, `stale`, `dead-ends`, `turn`, `pushback`, `schema`) and read-only Cypher, and prints TOON. Start in `src/graph/queries.ts` and `src/commands/query.ts`.

Other changes:
- **Digest:** it records per-file facts and the checks run after the last edit, plus per-run later edits. Its budgeting now favors evidence that explains the PR.
- **Checks:** a shell command that chains several checks (for example bundle, then `tsc && bun test`) used to record only the test run, with another check's result line attached to it. Chained checks are now split into separate runs that keep only result lines of their kind. Some runner segments can still merge into one run with an unknown outcome. A non-zero exit in a chain is no longer attributed to every check in it.
- **Merge base:** `digest.json` stored the merge base cut to 12 characters, which is too short to use as a revision for `tracetoon source --revision base`. It now keeps the full hash (per the commit message).
- **Also:** `doctor` gains a check, advisory graph leads (`unverified`, `unexplained`) reach the reviewer input, and small edits touch `src/comic/raster.ts` and `src/util/assets.ts`.
- **Getting drafters to use the graph:**
  - `prepare` output gains a `next` pointer and a `graphOutline`.
  - `evidence-notes.md` repeats the pointer and the outline.
  - `render` adds `graphHint` when the digest has a graph and no `query` ran.
  - SKILL.md and the drafter instructions apply the graph step to whoever drafts, including inline.

## Why

Per the commit messages (no session prompt asks for these specific fixes), a prbench comparison of the graph (Codex Sol/Terra, Claude Opus/Sonnet; 5 cases x 3 replicates) found no benefit. It traced this to three problems:
- `query why` returned only commit subjects and only the hunks linked to a captured edit. Terra drafts dropped a commit-body motivation in 12 of 12 judgments. `why` now lists every hunk and marks those no captured edit explains, and it includes commit message bodies. `outline` lists commits and which have a body.
- Chained checks were mis-attributed, as described above.
- Sonnet never queried the graph (0 of 15 drafts) because the instruction lived only in files it doesn't open. After the pointer was added, 2 of 5 drafts queried it, one query each. Embedding the outline in `prepare` and `evidence-notes.md` is the follow-up, and its effect has not been measured.

The session asked for a deeper integration of a graph database into tracetoon (S2) and, later, for fixing why Sonnet wasn't using the graph and testing cheaper drafters (S11). Those cheaper-drafter runs are not reported here.

## Validation

Historical results from earlier in the session. Files changed afterwards, and the tested content was not recorded:
- `bun run test`: 37 source test files passed, 0 failed.
- `bun test tests/graph.test.ts`: 10 pass. `bun test tests/evidence.test.ts`: 11 pass. `bun test tests/preparation.test.ts`: 3 pass.
- Prettier on `src` and `tests` passed. The last logged `bun run bundle` has no recorded result, so I treat it as unknown.

I did not re-run these for this description, and I have no hosted CI result. `scripts/eval-graph.ts` supports the comparison but was not run here.

## Review notes

The 6.5 MB `cypherlite.wasm` and the rebuilt `dist/tracetoon.mjs` are generated artifacts, so review the sources instead. `src/graph/vendor/` is vendored code. The riskiest logic is the check splitting in `src/digest/build.ts`.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The request was a proper, core integration of a lightweight graph database, not a partial one. This PR builds a per-run evidence graph of how the PR was made and steers drafters to it.

**The graph.** When the engine starts, each digest also writes `evidence-graph.json`: prompts linked to the edits of their turn, edits to the diff hunks their lines survive in, runs to PR files edited afterwards, commits to the sessions that made them. It runs in-process on cypherlite v0.16.1 compiled to WebAssembly, pinned by hash in `build-dependencies.json` and rebuilt with `scripts/cypherlite.ts`, so no native modules are added. If the engine cannot start, the digest is still written with a note. `tracetoon query` (60 rows per section unless `--all`) answers named questions (outline, why, unverified, unexplained, stale, dead-ends, turn, pushback, schema) and read-only Cypher, as TOON. `doctor`, packaged contracts, docs, an offline benchmark (`scripts/eval-graph.ts`) and `tests/graph.test.ts` come with it.

**Digest and review.** Budget trimming uses graph relevance when a graph exists, stale test claims name later-edited files, and the reviewer gets unverified files and unexplained hunks as leads.

**Getting drafters to look.** The commit messages report that Sonnet queried the graph in 0 of 15 drafts of a prbench comparison. Per the commit messages, Sonnet drafts inline and skipped the graph, which the skill had described only as the delegated drafter's step; it reads the `prepare` output and the top of `evidence-notes.md` and opens the drafter instructions when publish refuses. The graph step had lived only in those instructions and in `role-packets.json`, and now applies to whoever drafts. `prepare` prints a `next` step (`query outline`, then `query why` per behavior file), `evidence-notes.md` opens with the same pointer, and `render` adds `graphHint` when no query ran in the run. According to the follow-up commit, the pointer moved Sonnet from 0 of 15 to 2 of 5 candidate drafts with a query, so the outline now comes to the drafter: `prepare --json` carries `graphOutline`, and the notes include it at digest and render, capped at 40 rows per section and omitted if the graph can't be read.

**Fixes.** Previously the skill said to navigate by the graph "rather than reading every fact and the whole patch", while `query why` returned commit subjects and the hunks linked to a captured edit; `why` now lists the target's hunks (marking unexplained ones) with each commit's message body, and the instructions say to read the behavior hunks and expand those commits. The commit message states Terra drafts dropped a commit-body motivation in 12 of 12 judgments. Per the commit message, writers then claimed checks "were not run"; one shell command chaining several checks (bundle; tsc && bun test; eval) had recorded only the test run, and chained checks are now split into separate runs, and reviewers treat graph leads as places to look, not findings. `digest.json` now keeps the full merge-base hash instead of 12 characters. title: Add neighborhood brief layout; report each brief-check finding once
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This adds a neighborhood layout for the evidence brief and changes `render` so a brief-check finding that an earlier render of the run already listed stops blocking. Start with `src/graph/neighborhood.ts`, then `demoteRepeats` in `src/graph/briefRender.ts`.

## Why

The commit message for 48a90d7 says Codex graph-arm drafts ran up to 44 renders because `render` kept repeating findings the writer could not clear. The neighborhood layout comes from the session's work comparing a graph-shaped brief with a relational/vector one; this PR does not run that comparison.

## What changed

- **Neighborhood layout.** Each change gets a block with its requests, its commit sentences linked to hunks (`→ H#`), and its files with key changed lines. Blocks are packed toward 2,112 evidence tokens by default (`TRACETOON_BRIEF_BUDGET` overrides this); headers, requests, sentences and file lines are always kept, so the budget is not a hard cap (commit 5539230).
- **Layout switch.** `TRACETOON_BRIEF_LAYOUT=toon` keeps the old TOON tables. Any other value, or none, uses the neighborhood layout. Nothing else in the diff makes the neighborhood layout branch-specific. `tracetoon query brief` follows the same layout.
- **Hunk links.** Sentence-to-hunk links are conservative: a named file, each part of a list sentence, a single code hunk that shares words, or a scored match with a tie margin. Hunks are citable as `H#` and render checks them.
- **Findings reported once.** `render` records the brief-check findings it reports in `brief-findings-seen.json` in the run folder. A finding already recorded moves to a non-blocking "repeated" list. This applies to untagged sentences, run claims, unknown refs, uncovered rows and flags alike, so a real unfixed finding also stops blocking after one render.
- **Commit-message attribution.** A sentence that mentions "commit message", or is tagged with a commit, is no longer counted as a run claim.
- **Docs and bundle.** The writer instructions mention `→ H#` hunks (plus some incidental whitespace edits), and the plugin bundle is rebuilt.

## Validation

Per the session log, `bun test tests/render-loops.test.ts` passed (2 pass, 0 fail). Other logged test runs have unknown or mixed results; one combined invocation (R21) logged `1 fail` in one of its steps. Nothing was re-run for this description, and hosted CI status is unknown.

## Review notes

The riskiest parts are the hunk-linking heuristics in `src/graph/queries.ts`, which could link a sentence to the wrong hunk, and `demoteRepeats`, which lets a real finding stop blocking after one render. Feedback on the 2,112-token default is welcome.

If some passes fail, the ones that succeeded are imported, the failed passes and the rerun command are named, and the command exits non-zero. The rerun skips passes already imported for the same body on the same verified model, unless `--fresh` is given. `--all --recheck` resumes every slot that already has a run (with `contested`, only those with rejected findings); `--note` passes rejections along. `--all` rejects `--lens`, and `--note` and the contested list only take effect with `--recheck`.

- Single `review run` without `--lens` now also works when the plan asks for general passes beyond the lenses.
- SKILL.md step 2b: one review command (or merge), one edit pass, recheck only as the setting says.

`src/commands/reviewRun.ts` has most of the change; `src/contribution/mergeFindings.ts` is new. Tests live in `tests/review-run.test.ts`, `tests/merge-findings.test.ts` and `tests/skill-settings.test.ts`, with `tests/fake-codex-review.ts` updated for the concurrent passes.

title: Add `tracetoon update` to upgrade in place
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Why

There was no way to upgrade an installed Tracetoon from the CLI. In the session this came from, the question was "how do you update tracetoon, I see no update command in the CLI" (S1), and an approved plan followed for an update command (S4).

## What changes

`tracetoon update` looks up the published releases and installs a newer one in place. Before this change, the only route was reinstalling by hand.

- **Lookup:** `--channel stable|latest` selects the stream. The default is `latest`, which includes release candidates. `stable` errors if no stable release exists yet.
- **Check only:** `--check` reports the current and target versions without installing. Adding `--exit-code` makes it exit 10 when a newer release exists.
- **Pinning and rollback:** `--to <version>` installs that exact release. It is the only way to go backwards; a plain update never downgrades. The target is the newest release by publish time, and `--channel` is ignored when `--to` is given.
- **Version ordering:** a new semver comparator orders `rc.2` before `rc.10`.
- **Install:** the update checks SHA-256 checksums and that the skill and runtime come from one build. It then replaces the binary, comic assets and the skill copies in the known agent locations, and re-registers the hooks. If a step fails before the old copies are removed, it restores the old files; a failed hook registration is not fatal and prints a hint to run `tracetoon hook install`. A failure after the old copies are removed is not rolled back, and no test covers that case.
- **Refusals:** it won't replace a plugin/bundle copy, a `TRACETOON_BIN` binary, or a binary that isn't the installed one. An environment variable (named `…_DISABLE_UPDATES`, set to `1`) turns the command off.
- **Installers:** `install.sh` and `install.ps1` now record `install.json`; `update` also writes it after a successful install. Nothing reads it yet.
- **Testing hook:** `TRACETOON_UPDATE_URL` points the lookup and downloads at a test server.

The README documents the command. `plugin/skills/tracetoon/dist/tracetoon.mjs` and `build.json` are regenerated bundle output.

## Where to start

`src/commands/update.ts` has the flow. `src/update/apply.ts` has the replace-and-roll-back logic and carries the most risk.

## Testing

`tests/update.test.ts` is new. Logged runs from the session, before later edits: `bun test tests/update.test.ts` passed (12 pass, 0 fail), and `bun run test` passed (50 test files). These logged results are from before later edits. I did not re-run them for this PR.

title: Recognise the VEX AIM's user serial port and write whole buffers to it
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Problem

`types_by_location()` only knew the V5 Brain layout (interface 0 = system, 2 = user). The AIM enumerates as a composite device with a UVC camera on interfaces 2 and 3, so its serial ports are interfaces 0 and 4. Interface 4 hit the "unknown location" branch and was dropped, so `find_devices()` returned the AIM with `user_port() == None`, and `read_user()`/`write_user()` silently used the system-port fallback.

## Changes

- Treat interface 4 on the AIM (PID `0x0700`) as the user port.
- `types_by_location()` now returns `None` when it recognised nothing (it returned `Some(empty)` before), so the name-based fallbacks in `find_ports()` can run.
- `write_user()` used a single `write()` on the user port, which may accept only part of the buffer, and reported that count without flushing. It now uses `write_all()` + `flush()` and returns the full length, as the system-port `send()` path does.
- Add unit tests for AIM interfaces 0/4, Brain interfaces 0/2 (unchanged behaviour), and unrecognised ports returning `None`. Interface numbers are shifted by one on macOS to mirror how `serialport` reports them.

## Testing

Only the new unit tests in `serial.rs` cover this; they use synthetic port info. Not tested against real AIM hardware, and I did not run the test suite when preparing this description.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The user was at the robot for unplug/replug tests and asked for the kicker test to be retried. This PR records those hardware results, makes the CLI explain a mid-command disconnect, and updates the skill docs to match.

**CLI.** Previously `Fail::Io` errors printed as `serial I/O error`. Errors containing "broken pipe", "no such device" or "input/output error" now print a disconnect message: the robot may have been unplugged or powered off, output may be incomplete, and a movement command may or may not have run. `devices()` now returns an empty list instead of an error when the serial library cannot infer device types (nothing recognisable plugged in). A unit test asserts the matcher accepts "broken pipe" and "no such device" and rejects a timeout. The change also adds the `tests/replug.py` and `tests/stress.py` harnesses.

Runs 2-4 with the udev rule recovered 15/15; with run 1 that is 20/20 over 4 runs, which the report counts as meeting its replug criterion (>=5 recoveries without VEXcode). One slow cycle in run 4 was a bouncing cable, not a slow recovery. The kicker moved: `kicker.kick(SOFT)` ran and a human confirmed it.

**Skill docs.** `SKILL.md` gains a replug-behaviour paragraph and a note that camera orientation reflects how the robot is physically sitting (the test robot sat upside down); `api.md` marks `kick(SOFT)` as run and confirmed.

title: Add stationary AprilTag search and opt-in contact-based fast play (0.5.1)
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Two changes to the native vision behaviors, bumping the release to 0.5.1.

**Stationary tag search.** Before, `behaviors.find` looked for an AprilTag with the same continuous rotation sweep used for objects. Now a tag target goes to a new `find_tag`: it takes up to eight stationary views 45° apart (settle 300 ms, three detector reads 100 ms apart), stops at 20 s (checked between views), and raises `not_found` if none sees the tag. `reacquire` also pauses 300 ms before reading a tag. Cargo search is unchanged.

**Opt-in fast play.** `behaviors.configure(verification="contact", tag_turn_dps=...)` makes a bounded contact attempt count as pickup and lets `deliver` continue to the marker and fire `kicker.place` without the retention reverse, repeated possession gates or camera confirmations. Results report what was actually confirmed: `collect` returns `completed: True` with `evidence` of `native_possession` or `contact_assumed` (`collected` is `None` when assumed), and `deliver` returns `place_assumed` with `delivered: None` unless native release was seen. The default stays `verification="vision"` with the previous checks. A missing target, missing cargo or the whole-activity deadline still stops the sequence (covered by tests). `configure` now also validates `verification` and caps `tag_turn_dps` at 150, and the named-macro path sets `tag_turn_dps` from `turn_dps`. `deliver` results (and `collect` when cargo is already held) also gain `completed: True` in the default mode. Separately, every finite native motion now has a 1500 ms minimum limit for acceleration/status lag; it still returns as soon as the robot reports stopped.

**Why.** Per the author's request (S6), after a Windows test where the robot picked up the blue barrel and found the purple tag, the kid-facing path should be "more aggressive and just assume it works", quickly, without the diagnostic camera checks and stops used while testing. The stationary tag views come from that test: the continuous 0.5.0 Tag 0 sweep missed the marker, while stationary views found it at the third view (see `docs/hardware-notes.md`).

**Evidence and limits.**
- Historical session runs (before later edits, so not proof of the final content): `python -m unittest discover -s dev -p test_behaviors.py` passed (R5, R7). Several later combined runs have unknown outcome. I did not re-run tests while preparing this PR.
- New tests in `dev/test_behaviors.py` cover stationary-only tag decoding in both directions, bounded search with no marker, false-negative possession, contact limit without claiming attachment, shared deadline, assumed release and the frozen-clock watchdog. They use the simulator; CI does not verify real hardware.
- Hardware notes record the earlier camera-verified delivery. A final check of the 0.5.1 source on the robot did not reacquire blue and stopped after a bounded search, so full 0.5.1 hardware acceptance is still pending. Contact-based play is a completion policy, not a force sensor.

Release notes, README, device docs, the bundled skill and Cargo/VERSION move to 0.5.1 together. Note: the release notes also say the workshop installer and workshop instructions were updated; this diff contains no such change (workshop material lives in a separate repository), so that sentence needs author confirmation.

title: Use SDL FreeRDP client for full desktop mode on Wayland
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Summary

On Wayland, `winapps windows` (full desktop view) now prefers an SDL FreeRDP client over `xfreerdp`. RemoteApp/app launches and non-Wayland sessions keep using the existing `xfreerdp` path.

Per the commit message, this is meant for the full Windows desktop on Wayland sessions.

## What changes

In `waGetFreeRDPCommand` (`bin/winapps`), when `FREERDP_COMMAND` is not already set, the first argument is `windows` and `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` is `wayland`, it looks for, in order:

1. `sdl-freerdp3`
2. `sdl3-freerdp`
3. `sdl-freerdp`
4. the FreeRDP Flatpak (`com.freerdp.FreeRDP`) running `sdl-freerdp`, which also sets `RDP_FLATPAK=1`

Several names are probed because the SDL client may be unversioned (`sdl-freerdp`) on some systems, per the author's request while developing this. If none is found, the existing `xfreerdp` detection runs unchanged. The final validity check now also accepts the SDL Flatpak command. The main script passes `$1` to `waGetFreeRDPCommand` so the function can see the mode. A user-set `FREERDP_COMMAND` is still respected.

## Testing

Not run; no tests or manual runs were recorded for this change. Unverified: the SDL path reuses the existing `xfreerdp` Windows-mode flags (`/wm-class`, `+dynamic-resolution`), and the SDL Flatpak branch skips the FreeRDP 3+ version check applied to the `xfreerdp` Flatpak.
